ITID-91111.def: A planned, rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team crafts and sends department-targeted, context-tailored phishing emails to a specific business unit to measure click-through, credential submission, and reporting behavior, and to test whether email security and SOC detection controls identify the activity.
ITID-91111.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise simulating spear-phishing targeted at a specific department to test that group's susceptibility and detection response.
scopeIncludes: Tailored pretext and lure content researched for a single named department
Tracking of click-through, credential-entry, and user-reporting rates within that department
Testing of email gateway and SOC alerting on the targeted campaign
scopeExcludes: Organization-wide, non-targeted phishing sweeps (covered by the Unclassified/General leaf)
Executive-only targeting (covered by the Whaling Simulation leaf)
Multi-channel campaigns combining voice/SMS with email (covered by the Vishing/Smishing leaf)
ITID-91111.severity: A department click-through or credential-submission rate significantly above baseline, or a failure of the SOC to detect/alert on the campaign, is a Critical finding.
ITID-91111.priority: P1 remediation for missed SOC detection; P2 for elevated click-through with no credential loss; P3 for isolated low-rate clicks with prompt reporting.
ITID-91111.escalation: Escalate to the department manager and Security Awareness lead for elevated click rates; escalate to the CISO if the SOC fails to detect the campaign within the exercise window.
indicators: Elevated click-through rate versus organizational baseline
Credential submission on the simulated landing page
Low or delayed user reporting of the suspicious email to the SOC/helpdesk
vectors: Department-specific pretext emails referencing plausible internal projects, vendors, or processes
Simulated malicious link or attachment delivered to targeted mailboxes
Simulated credential-harvesting landing page linked from the lure
rootCauses: Insufficient department-specific security awareness training
Email gateway rules not tuned to catch tailored lures
Low user confidence in reporting suspicious email
controls: Email gateway phishing detection and sandboxing
ITID-91111.detection: Measures whether targeted, context-aware phishing bypasses email filtering and whether the SOC detects and triages user reports for a specific business unit.
ITID-91111.response: Deliver department-specific findings and remediation to the business unit and Security Awareness team; retarget training; retest after remediation window.
metrics: Department click-through rate
Credential submission rate
Time to user report
SOC time to detect/alert
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91111.notes: Requires signed authorization and pre-notification of department leadership per policy; simulated lures must avoid content that could cause reputational or emotional harm.

playbook.name: Spear-Phishing Simulation Targeting Specific Department
playbook.description: Authorized exercise sending a tailored spear-phishing lure to a targeted department to measure susceptibility and reporting behaviour.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and target department scope
steps.desc: Document the target department, the pretext theme, the click/credential-entry metrics to be measured, and success criteria (e.g. report rate vs click rate).
steps.guidance: Agree scope with the department head's chain of command via the sponsor only; do not tip off the target department directly.
steps.outcome: Written scope statement naming the department, pretext, and metrics.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and a 'get-out-of-jail-free' authorization letter from the CISO/sponsor covering the simulated phishing infrastructure and lure content.
steps.guidance: Ensure the letter names the sending domain/IP so mail and security teams can attribute the campaign if flagged.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before any email is sent.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide and document whether the SOC/blue team will be notified in advance of this campaign or kept unaware to test detection.
steps.guidance: At minimum the CISO/sponsor must be notified; SOC notification is a separate, explicit decision recorded in the RoE.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated to the relevant parties per the decision.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope boundaries
steps.desc: Explicitly state that no real credentials are to be stored beyond the test window, no lateral movement or data access follows a click, and no production mail flow disruption is permitted.
steps.guidance: Limit the landing page to capture only a 'clicked/entered-data' flag, not actual usable data.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and client contact channel
steps.desc: Set up a dedicated abort channel and contact with the client sponsor in case the campaign triggers an unintended incident response, media attention, or employee distress.
steps.guidance: Pre-arrange a stop-word or hotline the sponsor can use to halt sending mid-campaign.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable before launch.
steps.abort: If real panic, escalation to executives, or law-enforcement contact occurs, halt sending immediately via the abort channel.

steps.title: Deploy phishing infrastructure and send the lure
steps.desc: Stand up the simulated sending domain and landing page, then send the tailored spear-phishing email to the scoped department at the agreed time.
steps.guidance: Use a phishing-simulation platform to control volume and timing within the approved window.
steps.outcome: Campaign sent to 100% of the scoped recipient list with delivery confirmed.
steps.abort: If the sending domain is blocked or the campaign is mis-scoped, pause and correct before resuming.

steps.title: Monitor click, report, and credential-entry telemetry in real time
steps.desc: Track opens, clicks, credential submissions, and employee reports as they occur throughout the campaign window.
steps.guidance: Watch for signs the campaign is being escalated internally as a real incident.
steps.outcome: Real-time dashboard of engagement metrics maintained for the full campaign window.

steps.title: Tear down test infrastructure and purge captured data
steps.desc: Decommission the simulated domain/landing page and purge any captured test data beyond what is needed for reporting.
steps.guidance: Confirm no real credentials were persisted; if any were inadvertently captured, purge immediately.
steps.outcome: Test infrastructure removed; only aggregate metrics retained.

steps.title: Log susceptible individuals into targeted remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record which recipients clicked or entered data and route them to a tracked awareness-training remediation item with a due date.
steps.guidance: Treat this as coaching, not disciplinary, unless organizational policy states otherwise.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per susceptible recipient/group with severity/priority assigned.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report covering click/report rates, notable findings, and recommended awareness or control improvements, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.guidance: Compare results against prior campaigns if available to show trend.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91112.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team crafts highly personalized phishing lures targeting named executives (C-suite, board members) to test executive susceptibility, executive-tier email protections, and SOC/VIP-monitoring response.
ITID-91112.purpose: Authorized red-team exercise simulating whaling (executive-targeted) phishing to test the additional risk exposure and detection response for high-value executive accounts.
scopeIncludes: Personalized, high-effort pretexts targeting named executives
Testing of executive-tier email protection controls (e.g., impersonation protection, VIP monitoring)
Testing of assistant/delegate mailbox exposure where in scope
scopeExcludes: Department-wide, non-executive targeting (covered by the Spear-Phishing leaf)
Voice/SMS-combined campaigns (covered by the Vishing/Smishing leaf)
ITID-91112.severity: Any executive click-through, credential submission, or wire-transfer-style social-engineering compliance is a Critical finding given the elevated business-email-compromise risk.
ITID-91112.priority: P1 for any executive credential compromise or BEC-style compliance; P2 for click-through without further compromise.
ITID-91112.escalation: Escalate immediately to the CISO and executive's Chief of Staff/EA for any successful compromise; board-level notification for board-member targeting outcomes.
indicators: Executive click-through or credential submission
Failure of VIP/executive impersonation protections to flag the lure
Assistant/delegate account susceptibility
vectors: Highly researched, personalized pretexts referencing real executive context (travel, public statements, org events)
Simulated CEO-fraud/BEC-style urgency requests
Simulated credential-harvesting page targeting executive SSO
rootCauses: Executives exempted from standard awareness training cadence
Executive-tier email protections not enabled or mistuned
Public executive information (OSINT exposure) enabling highly convincing lures
controls: Out-of-band verification procedures for financial requests
ITID-91112.detection: Measures executive-tier susceptibility and whether VIP-specific email protections and out-of-band verification procedures function as intended.
ITID-91112.response: Provide confidential findings directly to affected executives and the CISO; mandate targeted executive briefing; retest.
metrics: Executive click-through/compromise rate
VIP protection alert rate
Out-of-band verification compliance rate
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91112.notes: Requires explicit sign-off from the CISO and, where board members are targeted, from the board risk committee; results handled under strict confidentiality given executive sensitivity.

playbook.name: Whaling Simulation Targeting Executive Team
playbook.description: Authorized exercise sending a tailored, high-value lure to executives to test susceptibility of the most sensitive targets.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and executive target list
steps.desc: Document the named executives in scope, the pretext theme (e.g. board matter, M&A, legal), and success criteria.
steps.guidance: Keep the exact target list restricted to the minimum sponsors necessary to preserve test validity.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming executives, pretext, and metrics.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and executive sponsor sign-off
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter from the CISO/board-level sponsor explicitly covering executive targeting.
steps.guidance: Given the sensitivity of targeting executives, obtain sign-off one level above the CISO where possible (e.g. audit committee or CEO).
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before any email is sent.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without explicit executive-level authorization.

steps.title: Decide SOC/executive-assistant advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether SOC and executive assistants are notified in advance or kept unaware to preserve test realism.
steps.guidance: Consider that executive assistants often triage mail; document if they are excluded from or included in the test population.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope boundaries
steps.desc: State that no real credentials, financial transactions, or confidential data are to be solicited or retained beyond a click/entry flag.
steps.guidance: Explicitly forbid any request for wire transfer or real financial action, even simulated, to avoid confusion with real fraud.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and executive-office contact channel
steps.desc: Set up a direct line to the executive sponsor's office to halt the campaign immediately if it causes disproportionate alarm or business disruption.
steps.guidance: Executives may escalate faster and higher than general staff; ensure the abort path can reach them within minutes.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable before launch.
steps.abort: If an executive contacts legal, law enforcement, or the board, halt immediately and disclose the test.

steps.title: Deploy phishing infrastructure and send the whaling lure
steps.desc: Stand up the simulated sending identity and landing page, then send the tailored lure to the scoped executives at the agreed time.
steps.guidance: Use a low-volume, high-customization approach consistent with real whaling attacks (e.g. spoofed board member).
steps.outcome: Campaign delivered to all scoped executives with delivery confirmed.
steps.abort: If delivery is blocked by executive-tier email protections, pause and coordinate with the mail team lead (who is aware of the test) rather than bypassing controls destructively.

steps.title: Monitor engagement and organizational response in real time
steps.desc: Track opens, clicks, entries, and any internal escalation (e.g. assistant forwarding to IT security) throughout the window.
steps.guidance: Be ready to identify the test the moment a real incident response process is triggered.
steps.outcome: Real-time engagement and escalation log maintained.

steps.title: Tear down test infrastructure and purge captured data
steps.desc: Decommission the simulated sending identity/landing page and purge captured test data beyond reporting needs.
steps.guidance: Confirm no real executive credentials were persisted.
steps.outcome: Test infrastructure removed; only aggregate metrics retained.

steps.title: Route findings into executive protection remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record susceptibility findings and route to a remediation backlog covering executive-tier controls (e.g. banner tuning, assistant training).
steps.guidance: Prioritize technical controls (DMARC, banner rules) alongside individual coaching.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created with severity assigned.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and confidential executive briefing
steps.desc: Publish a report and brief the executive sponsor privately, given the sensitivity of naming individual executives.
steps.guidance: Handle the report as confidential/restricted distribution.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and confidential briefing completed.

ITID-91113.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise combining simulated phone-based pretext calls and/or SMS lures with a coordinated email phishing component to measure susceptibility across channels and whether controls/staff correlate suspicious activity across channels.
ITID-91113.purpose: Authorized red-team exercise combining voice (vishing) and SMS (smishing) social engineering with email phishing to test multi-channel susceptibility and cross-channel detection.
scopeIncludes: Simulated pretext phone calls to target staff
Simulated SMS lures with malicious links or credential requests
Coordinated email component reinforcing the voice/SMS pretext
scopeExcludes: Single-channel email-only phishing (covered by Spear-Phishing/Whaling leaves)
Executive-exclusive targeting (covered by Whaling leaf)
ITID-91113.severity: Disclosure of credentials or sensitive information over phone/SMS, or successful multi-channel compliance, is a Critical finding.
ITID-91113.priority: P1 for any credential or sensitive-data disclosure via voice/SMS; P2 for partial compliance (e.g., confirming personal details) without credential loss.
ITID-91113.escalation: Escalate to the Security Awareness lead and helpdesk management for any successful vishing/smishing compliance; escalate to CISO if helpdesk fails to follow verification procedures.
indicators: Staff providing credentials or verification codes over the phone
Click-through on SMS-delivered links
Helpdesk bypassing identity-verification procedures under pretext pressure
vectors: Pretext phone calls impersonating IT support or executives
SMS messages with urgent, credential-harvesting links
Coordinated email follow-up to reinforce the voice/SMS pretext
rootCauses: Helpdesk verification procedures not consistently enforced
Lack of staff awareness of voice/SMS phishing tactics
No caller-ID/number verification for internal-sounding calls
controls: Security awareness training covering voice/SMS phishing
ITID-91113.detection: Measures cross-channel susceptibility and whether helpdesk and staff verification procedures hold up against coordinated multi-channel social engineering.
ITID-91113.response: Report findings to Security Awareness and Helpdesk management; reinforce verification procedures; retest helpdesk compliance specifically.
metrics: Vishing compliance rate
Smishing click-through rate
Helpdesk verification-procedure adherence rate
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91113.notes: Voice/SMS pretexts must avoid impersonating law enforcement, emergency services, or causing undue distress; requires coordination with telephony/SMS providers where applicable.

playbook.name: Vishing/Smishing Simulation Combined with Email Phishing
playbook.description: Authorized multi-channel exercise combining voice, SMS, and email phishing lures to test cross-channel susceptibility.

steps.title: Define multi-channel engagement objectives and scope
steps.desc: Document the target population, the combination of channels (voice call, SMS, email), pretext, and success criteria per channel.
steps.guidance: Consider sequencing: e.g. email first, then a follow-up vishing call referencing the email to increase realism.
steps.outcome: Written scope covering all channels, pretext, and metrics.

steps.title: Obtain signed RoE and authorization covering telephony/SMS providers
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter that explicitly covers the caller-ID spoofing/SMS sender ID to be used, given telecom and carrier compliance implications.
steps.guidance: Check with telephony provider/carrier compliance policies before spoofing caller ID, even for an authorized test.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter naming the phone numbers/SMS sender IDs used.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without confirming carrier-compliant use of spoofed numbers.

steps.title: Decide SOC and help-desk advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC and telephone help desk are notified in advance, since vishing calls to the help desk may trigger real support tickets.
steps.guidance: Unannounced tests risk consuming real help-desk resources; document the trade-off decision explicitly.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope boundaries across channels
steps.desc: State that no real password resets, account changes, or financial actions are to be requested or actioned on any channel.
steps.guidance: Vishing scripts must stop short of instructing any real system change.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list covering all three channels.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and client contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to the sponsor to halt the campaign if it causes real help-desk overload, law-enforcement contact, or employee distress.
steps.guidance: Pre-brief a single trusted help-desk lead who can quietly redirect confused real tickets without breaking the test.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable before launch.
steps.abort: If police or telecom fraud units are contacted, disclose the test immediately.

steps.title: Execute the email phishing lure
steps.desc: Send the initial email lure to the scoped population per the agreed pretext and timing.
steps.guidance: Track opens/clicks as the baseline channel.
steps.outcome: Email lure delivered to the full scoped population.

steps.title: Execute the SMS and voice follow-up
steps.desc: Send the SMS lure and place the vishing calls referencing the email, per the agreed script and timing.
steps.guidance: Record call outcomes (e.g. info disclosed, call refused, escalated) consistently for later analysis.
steps.outcome: SMS and voice contact attempts completed against the scoped population.
steps.abort: If a recipient threatens legal action or contacts authorities mid-call, terminate the call and disclose per the abort protocol.

steps.title: Tear down test infrastructure and purge captured data
steps.desc: Decommission spoofed numbers/sender IDs and purge any real personal data captured beyond the click/disclosure flag.
steps.guidance: Confirm no real credentials or personal data were persisted.
steps.outcome: Test infrastructure removed; only aggregate metrics retained.

steps.title: Route cross-channel findings into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record which individuals/departments were susceptible on which channel and route to a remediation backlog with severity.
steps.guidance: Highlight channel-specific gaps (e.g. help-desk verification procedure weakness) separately from individual coaching needs.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per finding.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a cross-channel after-action report and brief the CISO/sponsor, including help-desk process recommendations.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91114.def: A planned, rules-of-engagement-bound phishing simulation exercise, such as a broad organization-wide non-targeted campaign, that is not yet or does not need to be classified into a more specific Phishing Campaign Simulation category.
ITID-91114.purpose: Intake bucket for authorized phishing campaign simulations that do not fit a more specific department-targeted, executive-targeted, or multi-channel simulation leaf.
scopeIncludes: Organization-wide, non-targeted phishing simulations
Ad-hoc or newly designed phishing simulation formats pending permanent classification
scopeExcludes: Department-targeted campaigns (Spear-Phishing leaf)
Executive-targeted campaigns (Whaling leaf)
Multi-channel voice/SMS combined campaigns (Vishing/Smishing leaf)
ITID-91114.severity: Apply standard phishing-simulation severity criteria (elevated click-through or credential submission relative to baseline) pending reclassification.
ITID-91114.priority: P2 by default pending triage and possible reclassification to a more specific leaf.
ITID-91114.escalation: Escalate to the Security Awareness lead for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf where the pattern is identified.
indicators: Click-through or credential submission above baseline
Low reporting rate
vectors: Generic or broad-audience phishing lures not targeted to a specific department, executive, or channel combination
rootCauses: Simulation type not yet formally categorized
One-off or pilot phishing simulation formats
ITID-91114.detection: Provides general baseline visibility into organizational phishing susceptibility pending more specific classification.
ITID-91114.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Phishing Campaign Simulation leaf where the campaign pattern is clear; otherwise track as general awareness metric.
metrics: Overall organizational click-through rate
Overall reporting rate
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91114.notes: This is an intake/catch-all category; SOC analysts should reclassify to a specific leaf whenever the campaign pattern becomes clear.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Phishing Campaign Simulation
playbook.description: Baseline authorized phishing simulation exercise used when the specific phishing sub-type is not otherwise categorized.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and target population
steps.desc: Document the target population, general pretext, and success criteria for the campaign.
steps.guidance: Use this leaf only when the campaign does not fit spear-phishing, whaling, or vishing/smishing categories.
steps.outcome: Written scope statement covering population, pretext, and metrics.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter from the CISO/sponsor covering the simulated infrastructure and content.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before launch.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide and document whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance or kept unaware.
steps.guidance: At minimum the CISO/sponsor must be notified.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope boundaries
steps.desc: State that no real credentials or data are retained beyond a click/entry flag, and no production disruption is permitted.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and client contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel and sponsor contact to halt the campaign if it escalates unexpectedly.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: Halt sending immediately on sponsor request or genuine incident escalation.

steps.title: Deploy infrastructure and send the campaign
steps.desc: Stand up the simulated sending domain/landing page and send the campaign to the scoped population.
steps.outcome: Campaign sent and delivery confirmed.

steps.title: Monitor engagement telemetry in real time
steps.desc: Track opens, clicks, entries, and reports throughout the campaign window.
steps.outcome: Real-time engagement dashboard maintained.

steps.title: Tear down test infrastructure and purge captured data
steps.desc: Decommission the simulated infrastructure and purge captured test data beyond reporting needs.
steps.outcome: Test infrastructure removed; only aggregate metrics retained.

steps.title: Log susceptible individuals into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record susceptible recipients and route to a tracked awareness-training remediation item.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report covering results and recommendations, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91121.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team stands up a look-alike login page (e.g., for SSO, email, or a business application) and drives users to it to capture whether credentials are entered and whether the organization detects the fraudulent domain/page and any resulting anomalous authentication.
ITID-91121.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise simulating credential harvesting through a fake login page to test user susceptibility and web/identity-layer detection controls.
scopeIncludes: Deployment of a controlled, non-production look-alike login page
Measurement of credential submission rate
Testing of anomalous-login/impossible-travel detection using captured test credentials
scopeExcludes: Post-credential lateral movement techniques (Pass-the-Hash leaf)
Privilege escalation after initial access (Privilege Escalation Chain leaf)
ITID-91121.severity: Any credential submission that is not detected/alerted by identity or SOC monitoring is a Critical finding.
ITID-91121.priority: P1 for undetected credential submission followed by simulated login; P2 for credential submission that is detected/alerted.
ITID-91121.escalation: Escalate to the Identity/IAM team and CISO if simulated credential use is not flagged by conditional-access or anomalous-login detection.
indicators: Credentials entered on the fake login page
No alert generated on subsequent simulated login from an unexpected location/device
Domain/brand impersonation not flagged by web/email filtering
vectors: Look-alike domain hosting a cloned login page
Delivery of the login page link via email or other pretext
Simulated authentication using harvested test credentials from an atypical location
rootCauses: No conditional access or anomalous-login detection tuned for impossible travel/new device
Lack of MFA enforcement on the targeted application
Users unable to distinguish legitimate from spoofed login domains
ITID-91121.detection: Measures whether identity monitoring detects use of harvested credentials and whether MFA blocks simulated account takeover even when credentials are captured.
ITID-91121.response: Report findings to IAM/Identity team; enforce/verify MFA coverage; retest after remediation.
metrics: Credential submission rate
Time to detect anomalous login from harvested credential
MFA block rate on simulated takeover attempt
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91121.notes: Captured test credentials must be immediately invalidated/rotated post-exercise and never used beyond the defined authorization window.

playbook.name: Simulated Credential Harvesting via Fake Login Page
playbook.description: Authorized exercise deploying a fake login page to test whether users submit credentials to an unverified site.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and target application to spoof
steps.desc: Document which login page is being spoofed (e.g. SSO/webmail), the target population, and success criteria.
steps.guidance: Choose a look-alike that reflects a plausible real threat vector, not the actual production login page verbatim if that risks confusion.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming the spoofed application, population, and metrics.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the fake login domain and credential-capture mechanism.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before deployment.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance, since a fake login page may trigger phishing-detection or takedown workflows.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the mail/web filtering team to avoid the page being auto-blocked if the test needs to run unannounced.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope boundaries for captured credentials
steps.desc: State that captured credentials are never used to log into real systems, are stored encrypted, and are purged after reporting.
steps.guidance: Restrict access to captured credential data to the named test operators only.
steps.outcome: Written data-handling policy appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and client contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the campaign if the fake login page is publicly reported as a real phishing site or blocked by a third-party blocklist.
steps.guidance: Prepare a rapid takedown/disclosure statement in case a security vendor flags the page publicly.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If the page is publicly listed as malicious or reported to law enforcement, take it down and disclose the test immediately.

steps.title: Deploy the fake login page and delivery mechanism
steps.desc: Stand up the credential-harvesting page and deliver the lure (email/link) to the scoped population.
steps.outcome: Fake login page live and lure delivered to the scoped population.

steps.title: Capture and log submission attempts without storing usable credentials
steps.desc: Log which users submitted data to the fake page, capturing only a flag/timestamp rather than persisting the actual password value where feasible.
steps.guidance: If the platform captures the actual submitted password, ensure it is immediately hashed or discarded per the data-handling policy.
steps.outcome: Submission log maintained for the full campaign window.

steps.title: Tear down the fake login page and purge captured data
steps.desc: Decommission the fake page and securely purge all captured credential data.
steps.guidance: Confirm deletion is verified, not just scheduled.
steps.outcome: Fake login page removed; captured data purged.

steps.title: Route susceptible users into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record which users submitted credentials and route to an awareness-training or MFA-enforcement remediation item.
steps.guidance: Recommend MFA enforcement as a compensating control regardless of individual outcomes.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created with severity assigned.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report on submission rates and recommended controls, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91122.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team, using a legitimately obtained test credential/hash within a designated test scope, performs simulated pass-the-hash authentication to move between systems, testing EDR and identity-monitoring detection of NTLM-relay/hash-reuse behavior.
ITID-91122.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise simulating pass-the-hash lateral movement to test whether internal detection controls identify credential-relay-based movement between systems.
scopeIncludes: Simulated NTLM hash capture/reuse within an authorized, scoped set of test systems
Testing of EDR and SIEM detection for pass-the-hash indicators
Movement between a defined chain of test hosts
scopeExcludes: Initial credential harvesting via phishing (covered by Credential Harvesting leaf)
Post-movement privilege escalation chains (covered by Privilege Escalation Chain leaf)
ITID-91122.severity: Undetected lateral movement across more than one host tier (e.g., workstation to server) is a Critical finding.
ITID-91122.priority: P1 for undetected multi-hop lateral movement; P2 for detected but delayed containment.
ITID-91122.escalation: Escalate to the Identity/Infrastructure Security team and CISO for any undetected lateral movement reaching a server or domain-tier asset.
indicators: No EDR alert on NTLM-relay or hash-reuse behavior
No SIEM correlation of anomalous authentication patterns across hosts
Successful simulated authentication to a downstream host using a relayed hash
vectors: Simulated capture of an NTLM hash from a compromised test host
Simulated reuse of the captured hash to authenticate to additional in-scope hosts without cracking the password
rootCauses: NTLM not restricted/disabled where Kerberos is feasible
Lack of EDR behavioral detection for hash-reuse patterns
Flat internal network segmentation allowing broad lateral reach

playbook.name: Simulated Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement Exercise
playbook.description: Authorized red team exercise using a captured/synthetic hash to move laterally between test-scoped hosts and validate detection.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and lateral-movement scope
steps.desc: Document the starting foothold, the set of scoped hosts/segments for lateral movement, and success criteria (e.g. reach a defined target host).
steps.guidance: Scope should reflect a realistic post-compromise position, e.g. a single already-compromised workstation.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming hosts/segments in play and objectives.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter explicitly covering the credential/hash material to be used and the systems it may touch.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC is notified in advance or kept unaware to test detection of pass-the-hash activity.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and techniques
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude production systems outside the test segment, domain controllers unless specifically authorized, and any action causing account lockout of real users.
steps.guidance: Use a dedicated test account/hash where possible rather than a real employee's live credential.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and client contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to the sponsor/blue-team lead in case the movement triggers a real incident response or affects production availability.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If a real SOC incident ticket is opened that is not being tracked as part of the test, disclose immediately.

steps.title: Extract or stage the test credential hash
steps.desc: From the authorized foothold, extract or stage the hash material to be reused for the pass-the-hash technique.
steps.guidance: Use a dedicated test account's hash wherever the scope allows rather than a real production account.
steps.outcome: Hash material staged and validated for reuse.

steps.title: Execute pass-the-hash authentication to move laterally
steps.desc: Use the staged hash to authenticate to the next scoped host(s), documenting each hop and access gained.
steps.guidance: Log each lateral hop with timestamp for later correlation with SOC detection telemetry.
steps.outcome: Successful authentication to at least one additional scoped host recorded.
steps.abort: If movement reaches a host outside the agreed scope, stop and back out immediately.

steps.title: Remove test artifacts and revert session state
steps.desc: Clear any cached sessions, scheduled tasks, or files created during the exercise on each touched host.
steps.guidance: Verify via host logs that no persistence mechanism remains.
steps.outcome: All touched hosts confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route detection gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record which hops were detected/undetected by the SOC and route undetected paths to a remediation backlog (e.g. credential guard, tiering) with severity.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per detection gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report detailing the movement path, detection outcomes, and recommended hardening, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91123.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise starting from a pre-authorized low-privilege foothold and chaining a sequence of privilege escalation techniques (local and/or domain) to reach a defined elevated-access target, testing detection at each stage of the chain.
ITID-91123.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise chaining multiple privilege escalation techniques from an initial foothold to elevated access, to test whether the organization detects and contains an escalating compromise.
scopeIncludes: Chained escalation from a defined low-privilege starting point to a defined target privilege level
Testing of detection at each stage of the escalation chain
Documentation of the full attack path for remediation
scopeExcludes: Single-step hash-reuse lateral movement without escalation chaining (Pass-the-Hash leaf)
Initial credential harvesting (Credential Harvesting leaf)
ITID-91123.severity: Reaching the defined elevated-access target without detection at any stage is a Critical finding.
ITID-91123.priority: P1 for undetected full-chain escalation; P2 for partial detection with delayed containment.
ITID-91123.escalation: Escalate immediately to the CISO and Infrastructure Security team when the exercise reaches domain-admin-equivalent or crown-jewel access undetected.
indicators: No alerting at intermediate escalation steps
Successful reach of the defined elevated-access target
Absence of EDR/SIEM correlation across the escalation chain
vectors: Exploitation of misconfigured local privileges or service accounts
Abuse of overly permissive group memberships
Chaining of multiple lower-severity misconfigurations into a full privilege escalation path
rootCauses: Excessive standing privileges/local admin rights
Lack of privilege-escalation-specific EDR behavioral rules
Insufficient least-privilege enforcement and periodic access review
ITID-91123.detection: Measures end-to-end detection of a realistic multi-stage privilege escalation chain, not just isolated techniques.
ITID-91123.response: Deliver a full attack-path report with prioritized remediation of the weakest link; retest the chain after remediation.
metrics: Number of undetected escalation stages
Time to detect any stage of the chain
Time to full containment
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
Privilege Escalation Chain Simulation Safety SOP
ITID-91123.notes: Starting foothold and target elevated-access level must be explicitly pre-authorized in writing before execution; chain must stay within the defined blast radius.

playbook.name: Simulated Privilege Escalation Chain Exercise
playbook.description: Authorized red team exercise chaining misconfigurations/vulnerabilities to escalate from a low-privilege foothold to elevated access.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and escalation-path scope
steps.desc: Document the starting low-privilege foothold, the target privilege level to reach, and the systems in scope for the escalation chain.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming starting point, target, and in-scope systems.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the escalation techniques to be attempted.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC is notified in advance or kept unaware to test detection of privilege escalation activity.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and techniques
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude techniques that could crash a production system (e.g. unstable kernel exploits) and any target outside the agreed system list.
steps.guidance: Prefer proof-of-concept validation over destructive exploitation where a vulnerability is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and client contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the chain if an attempted technique risks system instability or unintended access to sensitive data.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If a step risks crashing a production service, halt and switch to proof-of-concept-only validation.

steps.title: Enumerate escalation opportunities from the foothold
steps.desc: From the authorized low-privilege foothold, enumerate misconfigurations, vulnerable services, or weak permissions that could enable escalation.
steps.outcome: Candidate escalation vectors identified and documented.

steps.title: Execute the escalation chain to reach the target privilege level
steps.desc: Chain the identified vectors step by step, documenting each stage and the resulting privilege gained.
steps.guidance: Stop as soon as the agreed target privilege level is proven, do not go further than necessary.
steps.outcome: Target privilege level reached and evidenced (e.g. screenshot, command output).
steps.abort: If an unexpected side effect occurs (e.g. service outage), halt immediately and notify the sponsor.

steps.title: Revert configuration changes and remove test artifacts
steps.desc: Undo any configuration changes made to achieve escalation and remove any tools/files planted during the chain.
steps.guidance: Verify each touched host is restored to its pre-test configuration.
steps.outcome: All touched hosts confirmed reverted and clean.

steps.title: Route escalation vectors into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record each exploited misconfiguration/vulnerability and route to a remediation backlog with severity ratings.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per escalation vector.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report detailing the escalation chain, root causes, and recommended hardening, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

playbook.name: Simulated SQL Injection Attack Against Test Environment
playbook.description: Authorized exercise probing a test/staging web application for SQL injection vulnerabilities and validating exploitability.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and target application scope
steps.desc: Document the target application/environment (test/staging, not production), the injection points to be assessed, and success criteria.
steps.guidance: Confirm the environment is genuinely a test/staging instance and not shared with production data.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming the application, environment, and objectives.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the specific application and environment.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/application-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/application owner is notified in advance or kept unaware to test detection (e.g. WAF alerting).
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and data-handling limits
steps.desc: Explicitly forbid any destructive query (DROP/DELETE/UPDATE) beyond proof-of-concept, and forbid extraction of real production data even if reachable.
steps.guidance: Prefer read-only proof-of-concept extraction (e.g. version() call) over bulk data dumps.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and application-owner contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt testing if the injection risks corrupting the test database or if it unexpectedly reaches production data.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If a query appears to touch production data or the database becomes unstable, halt immediately.

steps.title: Enumerate and confirm injectable parameters
steps.desc: Test identified input parameters for SQL injection using both automated and manual techniques.
steps.guidance: Use both boolean-based and time-based blind techniques where error-based injection is not evident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of injectable parameters with technique used.

steps.title: Exploit confirmed injection to demonstrate impact
steps.desc: Demonstrate impact via a controlled proof-of-concept (e.g. extracting a database version or a single non-sensitive test row).
steps.guidance: Do not extract more data than needed to prove the vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Proof-of-concept impact demonstrated and evidenced.

steps.title: Verify test environment integrity and remove test artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm the test database was not corrupted and remove any test rows/records created during exploitation.
steps.outcome: Test environment confirmed intact and clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route vulnerabilities into remediation backlog with severity ratings
steps.desc: Record each confirmed injection point with a CVSS-style severity rating and route to the vulnerability-management backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per vulnerability with severity.

steps.title: Produce technical findings report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report detailing injectable parameters, proof-of-concept impact, and remediation guidance, and brief the application owner/CISO.
steps.outcome: Findings report delivered and briefing completed.

scopeIncludes: Reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS payload testing

Testing of WAF/behavioral detection for script-injection patterns
scopeExcludes: SQL/database injection (SQL Injection leaf)
API/business-logic abuse (API Abuse leaf)
ITID-91132.severity: Any successful stored XSS capable of session hijacking or admin-context execution is a Critical finding; reflected XSS requiring user interaction is High.
ITID-91132.priority: P1 for exploitable stored XSS in an authenticated/admin context; P2 for reflected/DOM-based XSS requiring victim interaction.

No WAF alert on script-injection payloads
vectors: Crafted `<script>`/event-handler payloads submitted via form fields, URL parameters, or file uploads
Stored payloads placed in persisted fields (comments, profile data) to trigger on subsequent views

Inconsistent output encoding across the application
User-generated content rendered without sanitization
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript

CSP coverage rate
Time to remediation

steps.title: Decide SOC/application-team advance notification

ITID-91134.response: Triage and reclassify where a clear technique pattern emerges; otherwise track under general metrics.
metrics: Number of findings pending reclassification
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
Web Application Testing Scope and Safety SOP
ITID-91134.notes: Intake/catch-all category; reclassify as soon as the technique pattern is clear.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Web Application Attack Simulation
playbook.description: Baseline authorized web application attack simulation used when the specific attack class is not otherwise categorized.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and target application scope
steps.desc: Document the target application/environment, the general attack surface to be assessed, and success criteria.
steps.guidance: Use this leaf only when the exercise does not fit SQL injection, XSS, or API abuse categories specifically.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming the application, environment, and objectives.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the application and testing techniques.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/application-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/application owner is notified in advance or kept unaware.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and data-handling limits
steps.desc: Explicitly forbid destructive actions and extraction/alteration of real production data.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and application-owner contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt testing if an attempted attack risks affecting real production data or availability.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: Halt immediately if production impact is observed.

steps.title: Enumerate the application attack surface
steps.desc: Map the application's attack surface (inputs, authentication, session handling, third-party components).
steps.outcome: Attack surface map documented.

steps.title: Attempt identified attack vectors and confirm exploitability
steps.desc: Test the enumerated attack surface for exploitable weaknesses using controlled, non-destructive techniques.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of exploitable vulnerabilities with evidence.

steps.title: Verify application integrity and remove test artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm the application was not left in a degraded or altered state and remove any test data/artifacts.
steps.outcome: Application confirmed intact and clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route vulnerabilities into remediation backlog with severity ratings
steps.desc: Record each vulnerability with a CVSS-style severity rating and route to the vulnerability-management backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per vulnerability with severity.

steps.title: Produce technical findings report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report detailing findings and remediation guidance, and brief the application owner/CISO.
steps.outcome: Findings report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91141.def: A planned, rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team simulates ransomware-style file encryption using reversible or benign encryption in an isolated environment, to test whether detection and response controls identify and contain the activity before real damage would occur.
ITID-91141.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise that simulates a ransomware encryption event in a controlled, non-destructive manner to test detection and response.
scopeIncludes: Simulated mass file-encryption behavior using a controlled, reversible tool
Testing EDR/backup-integrity alerting in response to the simulated behavior
scopeExcludes: Simulated deployment via a phishing vector (a sibling ITID covers the delivery mechanism specifically)
Any use of genuinely destructive or irreversible encryption — strictly out of scope for this test type
ITID-91141.severity: A failure to detect and contain the simulated encryption activity before it reaches a defined blast-radius threshold is a Critical finding.
ITID-91141.priority: P1 remediation for any missed detection; P2 for detection with delayed containment.
ITID-91141.escalation: Escalate immediately to the CISO if the simulation reveals the organization would not have detected a real ransomware event before significant encryption occurred.
indicators: No EDR alert on the simulated mass-file-modification behavior
Backup integrity monitoring fails to flag the simulated activity
vectors: Controlled execution of a reversible file-encryption tool against a designated test-data set in an isolated environment
rootCauses: EDR behavioral rules not tuned for mass file-modification patterns
Lack of backup-integrity monitoring
controls: EDR behavioral detection for mass file modification
ITID-91141.detection: Directly measures detection and containment speed for ransomware-style behavior, independent of the delivery mechanism.
ITID-91141.response: File findings for any detection/containment gap; retest after remediation; never execute against production data.
metrics: Time to detect simulated encryption activity
Time to automated/manual containment
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91141.notes: Must use only reversible/benign encryption tooling in an isolated, non-production environment with a signed authorization letter and defined blast-radius boundary.

playbook.name: Simulated Ransomware Encryption Exercise (Non-Destructive/Controlled)
playbook.description: Authorized, tightly controlled exercise simulating ransomware-style encryption behaviour against a designated safe target with a pre-arranged kill-switch.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and designate a safe, isolated target
steps.desc: Document the objectives, and designate a specific, isolated, non-production target system/dataset with dummy data that will receive the simulated encryption.
steps.guidance: The target must be fully isolated from production and contain only disposable dummy data; never use a live production system.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming the isolated target system and dummy dataset.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and executive authorization
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter explicitly approving controlled, non-destructive ransomware-style encryption, including executive sign-off given the risk profile.
steps.guidance: Given the potential for catastrophic misuse, require sign-off above the standard CISO level (e.g. CIO/CEO) in addition to the RoE.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and executive authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without explicit executive authorization naming the exact target and non-destructive constraint.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test detection and response to ransomware behaviour.
steps.guidance: Given the severity of the simulated activity, strongly consider at least a restricted advance-notification group even in an 'unannounced' variant.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Verify target isolation and confirm dummy-data-only scope
steps.desc: Independently verify the designated target is network-isolated from production and contains only dummy/disposable data before any encryption routine runs.
steps.guidance: Perform a network-path check and data inventory check as a hard gate before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Isolation and dummy-data-only status independently confirmed and signed off.
steps.abort: If isolation cannot be verified, do not proceed under any circumstances.

steps.title: Establish pre-arranged kill-switch and emergency stop channel
steps.desc: Configure and test a kill-switch mechanism that immediately halts and reverses the simulated encryption routine, plus a direct emergency channel to the client contact.
steps.guidance: The kill-switch must be tested successfully before the live exercise begins, not assumed to work.
steps.outcome: Kill-switch tested successfully and emergency channel confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If the kill-switch cannot be demonstrated to work reliably, do not proceed with the exercise.

steps.title: Execute the controlled, non-destructive encryption simulation
steps.desc: Run the simulated ransomware encryption routine against the designated isolated target only, using a reversible/controlled encryption technique.
steps.guidance: Use a purpose-built ransomware-simulation tool (not live ransomware code) that guarantees reversibility.
steps.outcome: Simulated encryption executed against the isolated target with all activity logged.
steps.abort: If encryption activity is detected outside the designated target, trigger the kill-switch immediately.
steps.tool: Ransomware simulation tool (e.g. controlled encryptor with reversible key escrow)

steps.title: Monitor detection and response telemetry in real time
steps.desc: Track SOC/EDR alerting and response actions triggered by the simulated encryption behaviour throughout the exercise.
steps.outcome: Real-time detection/response telemetry log maintained for the full exercise window.

steps.title: Trigger kill-switch, decrypt/restore target, and verify full reversal
steps.desc: Trigger the kill-switch to halt the simulation, decrypt or restore the target from the pre-encryption snapshot, and independently verify full data integrity.
steps.guidance: Verify file-by-file or via checksum comparison against the pre-exercise state; do not rely solely on the tool's self-reported success.
steps.outcome: Target fully restored and independently verified identical to its pre-exercise state.
steps.abort: If restoration cannot be independently verified as complete, escalate immediately to the incident response team.

steps.title: Route detection/response gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record detection and response gaps observed (e.g. delayed EDR alert, missing isolation automation) and route to a remediation backlog with severity.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per detection/response gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report covering detection timing, response effectiveness, and recommended improvements, and brief the CISO/executive sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91142.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which a simulated phishing email delivers a benign dropper that, once executed in an isolated test environment, triggers reversible file-encryption behavior, testing whether email, endpoint, and behavioral detection controls catch the activity at any stage of the chain.
ITID-91142.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise simulating the full chain from a phishing-delivered dropper to controlled, non-destructive ransomware-style encryption, to test the detection chain from initial access through impact.
scopeIncludes: Simulated phishing delivery of a benign dropper
Execution of controlled, reversible encryption behavior following the simulated delivery
Testing of detection at the delivery, execution, and encryption stages
scopeExcludes: Standalone encryption-only simulation with no delivery vector (Ransomware Encryption Exercise leaf)
Tabletop-only response exercises with no technical execution (Tabletop Ransomware Response leaf)
ITID-91142.severity: Undetected progression from phishing delivery through to simulated encryption onset is a Critical finding.
ITID-91142.priority: P1 for any undetected full-chain progression; P2 for detection only at the encryption stage (missed earlier stages).
ITID-91142.escalation: Escalate immediately to the CISO if the simulated chain reaches the encryption stage without any prior detection.
indicators: No email/endpoint alert on the simulated dropper delivery or execution
No EDR alert on the simulated mass file-modification behavior
Detection only occurring after simulated encryption has begun
vectors: Phishing email delivering a benign, controlled dropper payload
Dropper execution triggering a reversible file-encryption routine against designated test data in an isolated environment
rootCauses: Email/endpoint controls not layered to catch multiple stages independently
EDR behavioral rules not tuned for mass file-modification patterns following execution
Lack of macro/script execution restrictions
controls: EDR behavioral detection for mass file modification
ITID-91142.detection: Measures the full detection chain from delivery through impact, revealing whether a gap at one stage compounds into a missed detection overall.
ITID-91142.response: File findings for each stage where detection failed; prioritize the earliest missed stage for remediation; retest full chain after fixes.
metrics: Stage at which detection first occurred (delivery/execution/encryption/none)
Time to detect
Time to containment
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91142.notes: Must use only reversible/benign dropper and encryption tooling in an isolated, non-production environment with signed authorization and a defined blast-radius boundary.

playbook.name: Simulated Ransomware Deployment via Phishing Vector Exercise
playbook.description: Authorized, controlled exercise chaining a phishing delivery vector to a non-destructive ransomware-style payload against a designated safe target.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives, phishing pretext, and designate a safe target
steps.desc: Document the objectives, phishing delivery pretext, and the specific isolated, non-production target that will ultimately receive the simulated payload.
steps.guidance: The final payload target must be isolated from production with dummy data only, even though the initial delivery vector is a real phishing email to real users.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming the pretext, delivery population, and isolated payload target.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and executive authorization
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and executive authorization letter covering both the phishing delivery and the non-destructive ransomware-style payload behaviour.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and executive authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without explicit executive authorization covering both stages.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test the full detection chain from phishing click to payload execution.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Verify payload target isolation and confirm dummy-data-only scope
steps.desc: Independently verify the designated payload landing target is network-isolated from production and contains only dummy data before the phishing lure is sent.
steps.guidance: The payload must be engineered so it can only execute against the pre-designated isolated target, not any host the phishing click happens to originate from.
steps.outcome: Isolation and dummy-data-only status independently confirmed and signed off.
steps.abort: If isolation cannot be verified, do not proceed under any circumstances.

steps.title: Establish pre-arranged kill-switch and emergency stop channel
steps.desc: Configure and test a kill-switch that halts and reverses the simulated payload, plus a direct emergency channel to the client contact.
steps.guidance: Test the kill-switch end-to-end before sending the phishing lure.
steps.outcome: Kill-switch tested successfully and emergency channel confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If the kill-switch cannot be demonstrated to work reliably, do not proceed with the exercise.

steps.title: Deliver the phishing lure and trigger the payload chain
steps.desc: Send the phishing lure to the scoped population and, upon a successful click/execution, chain to the non-destructive ransomware-style payload against the designated isolated target only.
steps.outcome: Phishing lure delivered and payload chain executed against the isolated target with all activity logged.
steps.abort: If the payload path deviates from the pre-designated isolated target, trigger the kill-switch immediately.
steps.tool: Phishing simulation platform + ransomware simulation tool

steps.title: Monitor detection and response telemetry across the full chain
steps.desc: Track email security, EDR, and SOC response actions across the phishing click, payload delivery, and simulated encryption stages.
steps.outcome: Real-time telemetry log maintained across the full attack chain.

steps.title: Trigger kill-switch, restore target, and verify full reversal
steps.desc: Trigger the kill-switch, restore the target from its pre-exercise snapshot, and independently verify complete data integrity.
steps.outcome: Target fully restored and independently verified identical to its pre-exercise state.
steps.abort: If restoration cannot be independently verified as complete, escalate immediately to the incident response team.

steps.title: Route chain-wide detection/response gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record gaps observed at each chain stage (delivery, execution, encryption detection) and route to a remediation backlog with severity.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per detection/response gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report covering the full attack-chain timeline, detection effectiveness, and recommended improvements, and brief the CISO/executive sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91143.def: A planned, facilitator-led tabletop exercise in which stakeholders (SOC, IT, Legal, Communications, Executive leadership) walk through a simulated ransomware incident scenario to validate the incident response plan, decision authority, and communication procedures.
ITID-91143.purpose: Captures an authorized, discussion-based exercise simulating a ransomware incident scenario to test the organization's response plan, decision-making, and cross-team coordination without technical execution.
scopeIncludes: Facilitated discussion-based walkthrough of a ransomware scenario
Validation of the incident response plan and decision-tree for ransomware events
Testing of cross-team communication and escalation procedures
scopeExcludes: Technical execution of simulated encryption (Ransomware Encryption Exercise / Deployment via Phishing leaves)
ITID-91143.severity: A failure to identify a clear decision-maker, communication breakdown, or a plan gap that would materially delay response is a Critical finding.
ITID-91143.priority: P1 for critical plan gaps affecting containment/decision speed; P2 for communication or documentation gaps.
ITID-91143.escalation: Escalate identified plan gaps to the CISO and Incident Response plan owner for immediate remediation before the next real incident.
indicators: Participants unable to identify the correct escalation path or decision-maker
Confusion over backup restoration authority or ransom-payment decision process
Communication plan gaps for regulatory/customer notification timelines
vectors: Facilitated scenario injects simulating ransom notes, encrypted-file discovery, and escalating business impact
rootCauses: Incident response plan not recently rehearsed or updated
Unclear decision authority for ransom payment or system isolation
Insufficient cross-team (Legal/Comms/Executive) integration in the IR plan
controls: Documented and rehearsed incident response plan
ITID-91143.detection: Does not test technical detection; validates organizational readiness and decision-making speed for a ransomware scenario.
ITID-91143.response: Update the incident response plan and decision matrix based on identified gaps; schedule a follow-up tabletop after plan updates.
metrics: Time to identify correct decision-maker in scenario
Number of plan gaps identified
Percentage of prior gaps remediated since last tabletop
ITID-91143.notes: A non-technical exercise; should be run at least annually and after any material change to the incident response plan or organizational structure.

playbook.name: Tabletop Ransomware Response Simulation
playbook.description: Discussion-based, no-live-systems exercise walking stakeholders through a simulated ransomware scenario to validate the response plan.

steps.title: Define exercise objectives and select the ransomware scenario
steps.desc: Document the objectives, the specific ransomware scenario narrative (e.g. encrypted file servers, ransom note, data-leak threat), and the participant list.
steps.guidance: This is discussion-based only; confirm explicitly that no live systems are touched.
steps.outcome: Written scenario narrative and participant list agreed with the sponsor.

steps.title: Obtain sponsor sign-off and schedule the session
steps.desc: Secure sponsor sign-off on the scenario and schedule the tabletop session with all required stakeholders (IT, legal, communications, executive).
steps.outcome: Session scheduled with confirmed attendance from required stakeholder roles.

steps.title: Confirm no-live-systems boundary and facilitation ground rules
steps.desc: Explicitly confirm with all participants that the exercise is discussion-only, no production systems will be touched, and set ground rules for open, blame-free discussion.
steps.outcome: Ground rules communicated and acknowledged by participants at session start.

steps.title: Establish a facilitator escalation path for real concerns raised mid-session
steps.desc: Designate a facilitator contact to whom participants can flag any genuine, currently-active concern discovered incidentally during the discussion.
steps.guidance: Occasionally a tabletop surfaces a real, live gap or issue; have a path to route it outside the exercise.
steps.outcome: Escalation path communicated to participants.

steps.title: Present the injected scenario and facilitate stage-by-stage discussion
steps.desc: Walk participants through the ransomware scenario in stages (initial detection, containment decision, ransom-note handling, executive/legal decision points), soliciting real decisions at each stage.
steps.guidance: Inject realistic complications (e.g. backups also encrypted, ambiguous ransom demand) to test decision-making under pressure.
steps.outcome: All scenario stages discussed with documented participant decisions.

steps.title: Capture decision gaps and plan deviations in real time
steps.desc: Record where participants deviated from, or found gaps in, the documented incident response/ransomware playbook during the discussion.
steps.outcome: Gap log capturing each deviation or ambiguity encountered.

steps.title: Consolidate session notes and validate against the existing response plan
steps.desc: Compare the session's decision points and gaps against the current documented ransomware response plan to confirm which sections need updating.
steps.outcome: Consolidated gap analysis mapped to specific response-plan sections.

steps.title: Route plan-update actions into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record each identified plan gap or missing decision authority and route to a tracked remediation backlog with an owner and due date.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per identified gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report summarizing the scenario, key decisions, gaps identified, and recommended plan updates, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91144.def: A planned, rules-of-engagement-bound ransomware simulation exercise using a format not yet mapped to a more specific leaf in this Tier-4 group.
ITID-91144.purpose: Intake bucket for authorized ransomware-related simulation exercises not yet classified into the encryption, phishing-deployment, or tabletop leaves.
scopeIncludes: Novel or combined ransomware simulation formats pending classification
scopeExcludes: Standalone controlled encryption exercise (Ransomware Encryption Exercise leaf)
Phishing-delivered simulation (Deployment via Phishing leaf)
Discussion-based exercise (Tabletop Ransomware Response leaf)
ITID-91144.severity: Apply standard ransomware-simulation severity criteria pending triage and reclassification.
ITID-91144.escalation: Escalate to the CISO for triage and possible reclassification.
indicators: Findings not matching an existing specific leaf's pattern
vectors: Emerging or hybrid ransomware simulation techniques
rootCauses: Simulation format not yet formally categorized in the taxonomy
ITID-91144.detection: Provides general visibility pending reclassification into a more specific leaf.
ITID-91144.response: Triage and reclassify where a clear pattern emerges; otherwise track under general metrics.
metrics: Number of exercises pending reclassification
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91144.notes: Intake/catch-all category; must still use only reversible/non-destructive techniques in an isolated environment.

playbook.description: Baseline authorized, controlled ransomware-style simulation exercise used when the specific sub-type is not otherwise categorized.

steps.title: Define engagement objectives and designate a safe, isolated target
steps.desc: Document the objectives and designate a specific, isolated, non-production target with dummy data for the simulation.
steps.guidance: Use this leaf only when the exercise does not fit the encryption-only, phishing-vector, or tabletop categories specifically.
steps.outcome: Written scope naming the isolated target and dummy dataset.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and executive authorization
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and executive authorization letter explicitly approving the controlled, non-destructive simulation.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and executive authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without explicit executive authorization.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance or kept unaware.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Verify target isolation and confirm dummy-data-only scope
steps.desc: Independently verify the designated target is network-isolated from production and contains only dummy data before execution.
steps.outcome: Isolation and dummy-data-only status independently confirmed and signed off.
steps.abort: If isolation cannot be verified, do not proceed.

steps.title: Establish pre-arranged kill-switch and emergency stop channel
steps.desc: Configure and test a kill-switch mechanism and a direct emergency channel to the client contact.
steps.outcome: Kill-switch tested successfully and emergency channel confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If the kill-switch cannot be demonstrated to work reliably, do not proceed.

steps.title: Execute the controlled, non-destructive simulation
steps.desc: Run the simulated ransomware-style activity against the designated isolated target only.
steps.outcome: Simulation executed against the isolated target with all activity logged.
steps.abort: If activity is detected outside the designated target, trigger the kill-switch immediately.

steps.title: Monitor detection and response telemetry in real time
steps.desc: Track SOC/EDR alerting and response actions triggered by the simulated activity.
steps.outcome: Real-time telemetry log maintained for the full exercise window.

steps.title: Trigger kill-switch, restore target, and verify full reversal

steps.outcome: Target fully restored and independently verified identical to its pre-exercise state.

steps.title: Route detection/response gaps into remediation backlog
