steps.desc: Publish a report covering detection timing, response effectiveness, and recommended improvements, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91211.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise using a dedicated, authorized test account provisioned with standard/baseline privileges to attempt access to resources outside its intended entitlement, testing whether access controls and monitoring detect and block boundary violations.
ITID-91211.purpose: Captures an authorized internal exercise testing whether a standard-privilege test account can exceed its intended least-privilege boundary, to validate access-control enforcement.
scopeIncludes: Testing of standard-user account access-boundary enforcement
Attempts to access resources, shares, or systems outside the account's intended entitlement
Testing of access-review and anomalous-access detection controls
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a specific application misconfiguration for escalation (Misconfigured Internal Application leaf)
ITID-91211.severity: Any successful access to data or systems outside the account's defined entitlement without detection is a Critical finding.
ITID-91211.priority: P1 for undetected access-boundary violation reaching sensitive data; P2 for detected but unblocked access attempts.
ITID-91211.escalation: Escalate to the Identity/IAM team and data owner if the test account accesses sensitive/regulated data outside its entitlement.
indicators: Successful access to files, shares, or systems outside the account's assigned role
No DLP/access-anomaly alert on the out-of-scope access
Absence of periodic access-review flags for excessive entitlement
vectors: Enumeration of accessible network shares/systems beyond assigned role
Attempted access to resources via inherited or stale group memberships
rootCauses: Overly broad group memberships or inherited permissions
Lack of periodic least-privilege access review
Missing DLP/access-anomaly monitoring on internal data stores
ITID-91211.detection: Measures whether the organization's access-control model and monitoring actually enforce and detect least-privilege boundary violations from a standard internal account.
ITID-91211.response: Remediate over-permissioned group memberships; tighten access review cadence; retest.
metrics: Number of out-of-boundary access successes
Time to detect boundary violation
Percentage of excessive entitlements remediated
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91211.notes: Requires a dedicated, clearly labeled test account and written authorization defining the exact boundary being tested; never uses a real employee's credentials.

playbook.name: Simulated Least-Privilege Boundary Test (Authorized Test Account)
playbook.description: Authorized exercise using a dedicated test identity to probe whether least-privilege boundaries can be bypassed from an insider's perspective.

steps.title: Provision a dedicated authorized test account and define objectives
steps.desc: Confirm a dedicated test identity/account is provisioned specifically for this exercise, distinct from any real employee's account, and document the least-privilege boundaries to be tested.
steps.guidance: Never test against a real employee's live account, even with their consent — provision a purpose-built test identity with an equivalent role/privilege baseline.
steps.outcome: Dedicated test account provisioned and boundaries-to-test documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the test account and the internal systems/boundaries in scope.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/HR advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/HR is notified in advance, given the sensitivity of simulating insider behaviour, or kept unaware to test detection.
steps.guidance: At minimum the CISO/sponsor and HR liaison should be aware this is a sanctioned test, to avoid confusion with a real insider investigation.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and data
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude access to real sensitive/regulated data and any system outside the agreed boundary-testing scope.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and HR/legal contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the exercise if it is mistaken for a real insider incident or triggers an HR/legal investigation.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If a real HR/legal investigation is opened against the test account or a real employee is implicated in error, disclose the test immediately.

steps.title: Attempt to access resources beyond the test account's assigned privilege
steps.desc: From the test account, attempt to access systems, files, or functions beyond its assigned least-privilege role.
steps.guidance: Document each attempt and its outcome (blocked/allowed).
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of boundary-test attempts with outcomes.

steps.title: Escalate to broader boundary violations where initial attempts succeed
steps.desc: Where initial access succeeds, attempt further escalation within the agreed scope to establish the full extent of the boundary weakness.
steps.guidance: Stop as soon as the boundary weakness is sufficiently proven; do not go further than necessary.
steps.outcome: Extent of boundary weakness documented with evidence.
steps.abort: If access reaches real sensitive/regulated data, stop immediately and do not view/extract it further.

steps.title: Deactivate test account access and remove test artifacts
steps.desc: Revoke the test account's elevated access obtained during the exercise and remove any artifacts created.
steps.outcome: Test account access reverted to baseline; no residual artifacts remain.

steps.title: Route boundary weaknesses into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record each confirmed boundary weakness with a severity rating and route to a remediation backlog (e.g. RBAC/ACL fixes).
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per weakness.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report detailing boundary weaknesses found and recommended access-control improvements, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91212.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which testers, starting from a standard internal user context, attempt to exploit misconfigurations (e.g., excessive role assignments, insecure default settings, broken function-level authorization) in a specific internal application to gain elevated privileges within that application or the underlying host.
ITID-91212.purpose: Captures an authorized internal exercise exploiting a known or suspected misconfiguration in an internal business application to test whether it enables unauthorized privilege escalation.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of application-specific misconfigurations from a standard internal user context
Testing of application role/permission enforcement
Testing of detection for application-layer privilege escalation
scopeExcludes: General account/group-membership boundary testing not tied to a specific application (Least-Privilege Boundary Test leaf)
ITID-91212.severity: Any successful escalation to administrative function within the application or to the underlying host is a Critical finding.
ITID-91212.priority: P1 for confirmed application-to-host escalation; P2 for in-application privilege escalation without host impact.
ITID-91212.escalation: Escalate to the Application Owner and Application Security team for any confirmed escalation path; escalate to CISO if host-level compromise results.
indicators: Successful assumption of an administrative role within the application from a standard user context
No application or host-level alert on the privilege change
Configuration drift from documented secure baseline
vectors: Exploitation of insecure default role assignments or misconfigured RBAC settings
Abuse of broken function-level authorization exposing admin functions to standard users
rootCauses: Application deployed with insecure default configuration
Lack of periodic configuration-baseline auditing
Missing function-level authorization checks
controls: Secure configuration baseline and drift monitoring
ITID-91212.detection: Measures whether a real application misconfiguration is detectable and whether it can be leveraged beyond the application boundary.
ITID-91212.response: File findings for the application owner to remediate configuration; retest; add configuration check to baseline audits.
metrics: Number of applications with confirmed misconfiguration-based escalation
Time to remediate
Configuration drift detection rate
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91212.notes: Requires prior identification of the target application and written authorization scoping exactly which misconfigurations may be tested.

playbook.name: Simulated Privilege Escalation via Misconfigured Internal Application
playbook.description: Authorized exercise using a dedicated test identity to exploit a misconfigured internal application to escalate privilege.

steps.title: Provision a dedicated authorized test account and identify target application
steps.desc: Confirm a dedicated test identity/account is provisioned for this exercise and document the internal application suspected of misconfiguration.
steps.guidance: Never test against a real employee's live account.
steps.outcome: Dedicated test account provisioned and target application documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the test account and the internal application in scope.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/application-owner advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/application owner is notified in advance or kept unaware to test detection.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and data
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude access to real sensitive/regulated data reachable via the escalated privilege beyond proof-of-concept confirmation.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and application-owner contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the exercise if the misconfiguration exploitation risks application instability or real data exposure.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If application instability or real data exposure occurs, halt immediately.

steps.title: Identify the misconfiguration and confirm escalation path
steps.desc: From the test account, identify the specific misconfiguration in the internal application (e.g. excessive role mapping, insecure direct object reference) and confirm it enables privilege escalation.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration identified and escalation path confirmed.

steps.title: Execute escalation to demonstrate elevated access impact
steps.desc: Use the confirmed misconfiguration to escalate the test account's privilege and demonstrate the resulting access impact.
steps.guidance: Stop as soon as impact is sufficiently proven.
steps.outcome: Elevated access impact demonstrated and evidenced.

steps.title: Revert test account privilege and remove test artifacts
steps.desc: Revoke the escalated privilege obtained during the exercise and remove any artifacts created in the application.
steps.outcome: Test account access reverted to baseline; no residual artifacts remain.

steps.title: Route the misconfiguration into remediation backlog with severity rating
steps.desc: Record the misconfiguration and escalation path with a severity rating and route to the vulnerability-management backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entry created with severity.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report detailing the misconfiguration, escalation path, and recommended fix, and brief the application owner/CISO.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91221.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which a tester attempts to copy designated test data to removable media from a managed endpoint, testing whether device-control policies, DLP, and endpoint monitoring detect and block the transfer.
ITID-91221.purpose: Captures an authorized exercise simulating data exfiltration via removable media (e.g., USB) to test endpoint device-control and DLP effectiveness.
scopeIncludes: Testing of USB/removable-media device-control policy enforcement
Testing of endpoint DLP detection on file copy to removable media
Use of designated non-sensitive test data sets only
scopeExcludes: Exfiltration via cloud upload/email channels (Cloud Upload/Email leaf)
ITID-91221.severity: Successful copy of designated test data to unauthorized removable media without any DLP/device-control alert is a Critical finding.
ITID-91221.priority: P1 for undetected exfiltration of a sensitive-data-classified test set; P2 for detected but unblocked transfer.
ITID-91221.escalation: Escalate to the Data Protection/DLP team and CISO if sensitive-data-classified test files are copied without any alert.
indicators: Successful file copy to removable media from a managed endpoint
No DLP alert on the classified test data transfer
Removable media device-control policy not enforced/blocking
vectors: Direct copy of designated test files to a USB device from an endpoint with removable-media access
Use of an unmanaged/unauthorized removable device on a managed endpoint
rootCauses: Removable-media device control not enforced organization-wide
DLP policies not tuned to the relevant data classification
Endpoint exceptions/exclusions not periodically reviewed
ITID-91221.detection: Measures whether physical-media exfiltration specifically is detected and blocked, distinct from network-based exfiltration channels.
ITID-91221.response: File findings for DLP/device-control tuning; retest after remediation.
metrics: Percentage of endpoints enforcing device-control policy
DLP detection rate for removable-media transfer
Time to detect
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP

steps.title: Decide SOC/DLP-team advance notification

steps.desc: Securely wipe the canary data from the removable media and any endpoint caches, and return or destroy the media per policy.

steps.title: Route DLP/detection gaps into remediation backlog

steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders

ITID-91222.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which a tester attempts to upload or email designated test data to an unsanctioned cloud storage service or personal email account, testing whether CASB, network DLP, and email-egress controls detect and block the transfer.
ITID-91222.purpose: Captures an authorized exercise simulating data exfiltration via cloud upload or personal email to test network DLP, CASB, and email-egress monitoring effectiveness.
scopeIncludes: Testing of upload to unsanctioned/personal cloud storage services
Testing of email-based exfiltration to external/personal addresses
Testing of CASB and network DLP detection and blocking
scopeExcludes: Physical removable-media exfiltration (Removable Media leaf)

Missing egress filtering for unsanctioned cloud/email destinations
vectors: Upload of designated test files to personal cloud storage accounts
Emailing designated test files as attachments to an external/personal address

Network DLP not inspecting encrypted/TLS egress traffic
Email DLP rules not tuned to relevant data classification

Time to detect
Percentage of unsanctioned cloud services blocked

ITID-91231.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which a tester, using a designated test data set, performs bulk/deliberate deletion actions on controlled systems to test whether destructive-action monitoring, backup integrity, and recovery procedures detect and allow recovery from the simulated sabotage.
ITID-91231.purpose: Captures an authorized exercise simulating deliberate, malicious-style data deletion by an insider to test backup, recovery, and destructive-action detection controls.
scopeIncludes: Bulk/deliberate deletion of designated test data on controlled systems
Testing of backup and recovery procedures following the simulated deletion
Testing of destructive-action alerting
scopeExcludes: Service/process disruption sabotage (Disgruntled-Employee Sabotage Scenario leaf)
ITID-91231.severity: Deletion that is not detected in near-real-time or that cannot be fully recovered from backup is a Critical finding.
ITID-91231.priority: P1 for undetected deletion or failed recovery; P2 for detected deletion with a recovery process that exceeds target RTO.
ITID-91231.escalation: Escalate to IT Operations/Backup management and the CISO if the simulated deletion is not detected in near-real-time or recovery fails to meet the target RTO.
indicators: No alert on bulk/mass deletion activity
Backup restoration failing to fully recover the designated test data
Recovery time exceeding the defined RTO
vectors: Bulk deletion of designated test files/records via authorized standard-user or administrative access on a controlled system
rootCauses: No behavioral alerting for mass-deletion patterns
Backup verification/integrity testing not performed regularly
Recovery procedures untested or undocumented
ITID-91231.detection: Measures both detection of destructive insider activity and the organization's actual ability to recover from it.
ITID-91231.response: File findings for deletion-detection gaps and backup/recovery process gaps; retest recovery procedures.
metrics: Time to detect mass deletion
Recovery time versus target RTO
Percentage of data successfully recovered
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91231.notes: Must be performed only against designated test data on controlled/isolated systems with pre-verified backups; never executed against production data.

playbook.name: Simulated Deliberate Data Deletion Exercise
playbook.description: Authorized, fully reversible exercise using a dedicated test account and verified backup to simulate deliberate data deletion by a rogue insider.

steps.title: Provision a dedicated authorized test account and select target dataset
steps.desc: Confirm a dedicated test identity/account is provisioned and select a specific, non-production or clearly bounded target dataset for the deletion exercise.
steps.guidance: Never use a real employee's account or truly irreplaceable data as the target.
steps.outcome: Dedicated test account provisioned and target dataset documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the test account and target dataset.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Decide SOC/backup-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/backup team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test detection and recovery response.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Create and independently verify a backup/snapshot of the target dataset
steps.desc: Take a full backup/snapshot of the target dataset and independently verify it is complete, restorable, and stored separately before any deletion occurs.
steps.guidance: This is a hard gate: do not proceed to deletion until the backup has been test-restored and confirmed intact.
steps.outcome: Backup/snapshot verified restorable via a test restore.
steps.abort: If the backup cannot be verified as restorable, do not proceed with the exercise.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and backup-team contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the exercise and trigger immediate restoration if anything goes wrong.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If deletion scope expands beyond the agreed target, halt immediately and restore from backup.

steps.title: Execute the deliberate deletion from the test account
steps.desc: From the test account, perform the deliberate deletion of the target dataset per the agreed scope.
steps.outcome: Deletion executed against the agreed target dataset only.
steps.abort: If deletion begins to affect data outside the agreed target, halt immediately.

steps.title: Monitor detection and alerting response in real time
steps.desc: Track SOC/backup-monitoring alerting triggered by the deletion activity.
steps.outcome: Real-time detection telemetry log maintained for the exercise window.

steps.title: Restore the target dataset from backup and verify complete recovery
steps.desc: Restore the deleted dataset from the verified backup and independently confirm complete recovery with no data loss.
steps.guidance: Verify via checksum/record-count comparison against the pre-exercise state.
steps.outcome: Target dataset fully restored and independently verified identical to its pre-exercise state.
steps.abort: If restoration is incomplete, escalate immediately to the incident response/backup team.

steps.title: Route detection/recovery gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record detection and recovery-time gaps observed with severity ratings and route to the remediation backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report covering detection timing, recovery time, and recommended improvements, and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91232.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise simulating the behavior pattern of a disgruntled or soon-to-be-departed employee attempting service disruption or access misuse, testing whether offboarding controls, access revocation timing, and behavioral monitoring detect and prevent the simulated sabotage.
ITID-91232.purpose: Captures an authorized exercise simulating a broader disgruntled-employee sabotage scenario (e.g., service disruption, account/access misuse near offboarding) to test offboarding controls and sabotage detection.
scopeIncludes: Simulated service/process disruption attempts on controlled test systems
Testing of access-revocation timing around simulated resignation/termination scenarios
Testing of user-behavior-analytics detection for anomalous pre-departure activity
scopeExcludes: Deliberate bulk data deletion (Deliberate Data Deletion leaf)
ITID-91232.severity: Any successful service disruption on a controlled system, or access retained beyond the defined revocation SLA, is a Critical finding.
ITID-91232.priority: P1 for undetected service disruption or access-revocation SLA breach; P2 for detected anomalous behavior with delayed response.
ITID-91232.escalation: Escalate to HR and the CISO if access-revocation timing fails the defined SLA or if disruption goes undetected.
indicators: Service/process stopped on a controlled test system without alert
Account access remaining active beyond the defined offboarding SLA
No UEBA alert on anomalous pre-departure activity pattern
vectors: Simulated stopping of a designated service/process on a controlled test host
Simulated continued access attempts after a scripted termination event
Simulated bulk download or unusual access pattern preceding a scripted departure
rootCauses: Offboarding process not tightly integrated with access revocation automation
Lack of user-behavior-analytics baselining for pre-departure anomaly detection
No service-disruption alerting on critical processes
ITID-91232.detection: Measures whether offboarding process timing and behavioral analytics would catch a realistic disgruntled-employee sabotage pattern.
ITID-91232.response: File findings for offboarding automation and UEBA tuning gaps; retest after remediation.
metrics: Access-revocation time versus SLA
Time to detect simulated service disruption
UEBA alert rate on scripted pre-departure pattern
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91232.notes: Requires HR coordination and must be run against controlled test systems and scripted scenarios only; never targets a real employee's actual offboarding.

ITID-91311.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team emulates a complete adversary campaign — from reconnaissance through initial access, execution, persistence, privilege escalation, defense evasion, credential access, discovery, lateral movement, collection, command and control, and impact — to test detection, correlation, and response across the entire kill chain rather than any single technique.
ITID-91311.purpose: Captures an authorized, comprehensive red-team exercise emulating a full adversary kill chain across the breadth of the MITRE ATT&CK matrix, to test end-to-end detection and response maturity against a realistic, multi-stage campaign.
scopeIncludes: End-to-end emulation spanning reconnaissance through impact across multiple ATT&CK tactics
Testing of cross-stage detection correlation (not just single-technique detection)
Testing of full incident response process activation from a realistic multi-stage campaign
scopeExcludes: Testing focused on a single ATT&CK technique in isolation (Specific ATT&CK Technique-Focused Purple Team leaf)
Extended-duration low-and-slow persistence-focused campaigns (Long Dwell APT Simulation leaves)
ITID-91311.severity: Any stage of the kill chain reaching a defined crown-jewel/impact objective without detection is a Critical finding, regardless of whether earlier stages were detected.
ITID-91311.priority: P1 for undetected end-to-end campaign reaching the impact objective; P2 for partial detection with slow cross-stage correlation.
ITID-91311.escalation: Escalate to the CISO and executive leadership immediately if the emulated campaign reaches its defined impact objective without detection at any stage.
indicators: No SIEM/SOAR correlation linking activity across multiple kill-chain stages
Individual stage detections that never trigger a consolidated incident
Successful reach of the defined final objective (e.g., simulated data theft or system impact)
vectors: Reconnaissance and initial access via a chosen realistic vector (phishing, external service exploitation)
Execution, persistence, and privilege escalation on compromised test systems
Defense evasion, credential access, discovery, and lateral movement across the scoped environment
Collection, command-and-control, and a defined impact/exfiltration objective
rootCauses: Detection tooling siloed by stage/tool without cross-stage correlation
SOC playbooks not designed to connect low-severity alerts into a single campaign narrative
Insufficient threat-hunting capability to catch what automated correlation misses
controls: SIEM cross-source correlation and use-case coverage
ITID-91311.detection: Provides the most comprehensive available measure of detection and response maturity, spanning the full kill chain rather than any isolated control.
ITID-91311.response: Produce a full campaign timeline report identifying every missed/delayed stage; prioritize remediation of the earliest missed stage; retest the full chain after major remediation.
metrics: Number of kill-chain stages detected versus total stages executed
Time to first detection
Time to full campaign correlation/consolidated incident
Time to containment of the defined impact objective
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91311.notes: Requires the most extensive authorization and scoping of any exercise in this taxonomy, including a signed authorization letter, defined blast-radius boundary, and a pre-agreed safe-word/stop procedure; typically the organization's flagship annual red-team exercise.

playbook.name: Full ATT&CK Kill-Chain Emulation (Recon Through Impact)
playbook.description: Authorized, sophisticated red team engagement emulating a full MITRE ATT&CK kill chain from reconnaissance through impact against a named threat-actor profile.

steps.title: Select the threat-actor profile and map the full ATT&CK technique set
steps.desc: Document the named threat-actor profile (or composite) being emulated and map the specific ATT&CK techniques spanning recon through impact to be executed.
steps.guidance: Base the technique selection on threat intelligence relevant to the organization's sector.
steps.outcome: Written technique-selection basis and full kill-chain technique map.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and executive authorization
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and executive authorization letter covering the full kill-chain scope, given the breadth and duration of this engagement.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and executive authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without executive authorization.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test full-chain detection.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems, techniques, and impact actions
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude systems outside the target environment and forbid genuinely destructive impact-stage actions (e.g. real data destruction), substituting proof-of-concept equivalents.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish engagement-duration boundary and emergency stop channel
steps.desc: Set an explicit end date for the engagement and an abort channel to the sponsor for immediate halt if needed.
steps.outcome: Duration boundary documented and abort channel tested.
steps.abort: If the engagement risks material business disruption, halt immediately.

steps.title: Execute reconnaissance and initial access stages
steps.desc: Perform the recon and initial-access techniques from the mapped kill chain against the agreed target environment.
steps.outcome: Initial access achieved and documented.

steps.title: Execute the remaining kill-chain stages through impact
steps.desc: Progress through execution, persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement, collection, exfiltration, and a proof-of-concept impact action per the mapped techniques.
steps.guidance: Document each stage with timestamps for correlation with SOC detection telemetry.
steps.outcome: Full kill chain executed through a proof-of-concept impact stage, fully documented.
steps.abort: If any stage risks real business impact beyond proof-of-concept, substitute a safe equivalent or halt.

steps.title: Remove all implants, test accounts, and persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Systematically remove every implant, scheduled task, test account, and configuration change made across the full kill chain.
steps.guidance: Maintain a running artifact inventory throughout eradication to make this step tractable.
steps.outcome: All touched hosts confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route detection gaps at each kill-chain stage into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record which stages were detected/undetected by the SOC and route undetected stages to a remediation backlog with severity.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per kill-chain stage gap.

steps.title: Produce comprehensive after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a full kill-chain after-action report mapped to ATT&CK, and brief the CISO/executive sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91312.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team executes a specific, pre-selected ATT&CK technique (or small related set) while working collaboratively and in real time with the blue team/SOC to validate whether the technique is detected, and to tune detection logic where it is not.
ITID-91312.purpose: Captures an authorized, collaborative purple-team exercise focused on a single or small set of specific MITRE ATT&CK techniques, run jointly with the SOC to directly validate and tune detection content.
scopeIncludes: Execution of one or a small pre-defined set of specific ATT&CK techniques
Real-time collaboration between red and blue teams during execution
Immediate detection-content tuning based on results
scopeExcludes: Broad, multi-stage end-to-end campaign emulation (Full ATT&CK Kill-Chain Emulation leaf)
ITID-91312.severity: A complete absence of detection logic for the targeted technique is a Critical finding; partial/noisy detection is High.
ITID-91312.priority: P1 for no detection coverage of the targeted technique; P2 for detection present but not alerting/tuned correctly.
ITID-91312.escalation: Escalate to the SOC Detection Engineering lead for any technique found to have zero detection coverage in a commonly-exploited technique category.
indicators: No SIEM alert generated for the executed technique
Detection rule present but not firing due to logic/tuning gaps
Successful detection and alert generation validating existing coverage
vectors: Execution of a single, pre-agreed ATT&CK technique (e.g., a specific credential-dumping or persistence method) against a designated test system
rootCauses: Detection rule not yet written for the technique
Detection rule written but mistuned or disabled
Technique newly added to the threat model without corresponding detection engineering
mitreTactics: Varies by exercise — mapped to the specific technique(s) selected for the session
mitreTechniques: Selected per session from the current ATT&CK matrix (e.g., T1003 OS Credential Dumping, T1053 Scheduled Task/Job)
ITID-91312.detection: Provides the most precise, technique-level measurement of detection coverage available, directly informing detection engineering backlog priorities.
ITID-91312.response: Write or tune the detection rule immediately during or shortly after the session; validate the fix with a re-run of the same technique.
metrics: Number of techniques with confirmed detection coverage
Number of new/tuned detection rules produced per session
Time from gap identification to rule deployment
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
ITID-91312.notes: Distinguished from the full kill-chain exercise by its narrow, collaborative, detection-engineering-focused format; typically run frequently (monthly/quarterly) rather than annually.

playbook.name: Specific ATT&CK Technique-Focused Purple Team Exercise
playbook.description: Authorized, collaborative exercise emulating a small set of specific MITRE ATT&CK techniques with the blue team actively participating to close detection gaps.

steps.title: Select specific ATT&CK techniques and schedule the joint session
steps.desc: Document the specific ATT&CK technique(s) to be emulated, the technique-selection basis (e.g. recent threat intel, prior gap), and schedule the joint red/blue session.
steps.outcome: Technique selection documented and joint session scheduled.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the specific techniques and target environment.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Confirm blue-team advance knowledge and participation
steps.desc: Confirm the blue team is aware in advance and will actively participate in real time — this is a collaborative purple team exercise, not a covert red team test.
steps.outcome: Blue-team participants confirmed and briefed on session logistics.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and techniques
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude systems outside the agreed target environment and any technique variant not agreed for the session.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and session-facilitator contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the session if the technique causes unintended impact.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: Halt immediately on unintended production impact.

steps.title: Red team executes the technique while blue team observes and responds in parallel
steps.desc: The red team executes the specific ATT&CK technique against the target environment while the blue team simultaneously attempts detection and response, in real time.
steps.guidance: Both teams should be on a shared call/channel for real-time coordination.
steps.outcome: Technique executed and blue-team real-time detection/response observed and logged.
steps.tool: ATT&CK emulation tooling (e.g. Atomic Red Team)

steps.title: Iterate technique variants to probe detection boundary
steps.desc: If time and scope allow, iterate variants of the technique to identify precisely where detection succeeds or fails.
steps.outcome: Detection boundary for the technique documented.

steps.title: Remove test artifacts and confirm environment integrity
steps.desc: Remove any artifacts created by the technique execution and confirm the environment is restored to normal.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route detection gaps into remediation backlog with severity ratings
steps.desc: Record specific detection gaps (e.g. missing log source, tuning needed) with severity and route to the remediation backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per gap.

steps.title: Hold joint red/blue debrief to close detection gaps collaboratively
steps.desc: Conduct a joint debrief session between the red and blue teams to review what worked, what was missed, and agree on detection-engineering follow-ups.
steps.guidance: This joint debrief is the key value of a purple team exercise and must be explicitly held, not skipped.
steps.outcome: Joint debrief held with documented action items.

ITID-91321.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which the red team establishes and maintains simulated persistence mechanisms on designated test systems over an extended period (typically weeks) to test whether long-term anomaly detection, threat hunting, and periodic security review eventually surface the presence.
ITID-91321.purpose: Captures an authorized, extended-duration red-team exercise maintaining simulated persistent access over multiple weeks, to test whether long-dwell adversary presence is eventually detected.
scopeIncludes: Establishment and maintenance of persistence mechanisms over an extended (multi-week) duration
Periodic minimal-footprint check-ins to maintain access
Testing of threat-hunting and long-term anomaly-detection processes
scopeExcludes: Beaconing/C2-channel-specific testing (Simulated Low-and-Slow C2 Beaconing leaf)
ITID-91321.severity: Persistence remaining entirely undetected through the full planned exercise duration is a Critical finding.
ITID-91321.priority: P1 for full-duration undetected persistence; P2 for detection occurring but significantly later than the organization's target dwell-time goal.
ITID-91321.escalation: Escalate to the CISO if simulated persistence exceeds the organization's target maximum dwell time without detection.
indicators: No threat-hunting or periodic review surfacing the persistence mechanism
Persistence artifact remaining active across multiple patch/maintenance cycles
Detection only occurring at planned exercise disclosure rather than through organic discovery
vectors: Low-footprint scheduled-task or service-based persistence established on a designated test system
Periodic minimal check-in activity designed to blend with normal system behavior over weeks
rootCauses: No proactive threat-hunting program covering persistence mechanisms
Baseline configuration drift not periodically reviewed
Alert fatigue causing low-and-slow indicators to be deprioritized
ITID-91321.detection: Measures the organization's actual mean dwell-time-to-detection against realistic long-term adversary persistence, not just point-in-time detection.
ITID-91321.response: Report the realized dwell time against target; strengthen threat-hunting cadence and baseline review where the exercise exceeds target dwell time.
metrics: Realized dwell time (days) versus target maximum dwell time
Detection method that eventually surfaced the persistence (organic vs. disclosed)
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
Long-Dwell Simulation Safety and Authorization SOP
ITID-91321.notes: Requires an explicit extended-duration authorization with defined check-in cadence with the exercise sponsor and an unconditional stop procedure; persistence mechanisms must be fully removed and verified post-exercise.

playbook.name: Multi-Week Simulated Persistent Access Exercise
playbook.description: Authorized, multi-week red team engagement maintaining persistent access to emulate long-dwell adversary behaviour, with strict duration and check-in controls.

steps.title: Define threat-actor TTP profile and target persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Document the named threat-actor TTP profile being emulated and the specific persistence mechanisms and dwell objectives.
steps.outcome: Written technique-selection basis and persistence-objective statement documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and executive authorization with fixed engagement window
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and executive authorization letter that fixes the exact start and end dates of the multi-week engagement.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter naming the fixed engagement window.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without an explicit end date.

steps.title: Decide SOC/blue-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/blue team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test long-dwell detection.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define explicit engagement-duration boundary and periodic sponsor check-in cadence
steps.desc: Document the hard end date for the engagement and establish a recurring check-in cadence (e.g. weekly) with the sponsor to confirm continued authorization.
steps.guidance: A multi-week test must never run indefinitely unnoticed; the check-in is a mandatory control, not optional.
steps.outcome: Duration boundary and check-in schedule documented and agreed.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and sponsor contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel reachable at any point during the multi-week window to halt the exercise immediately.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: Halt immediately on sponsor request or unintended business impact.

steps.title: Establish initial persistent foothold
steps.desc: Gain initial access and establish the persistence mechanism(s) agreed in scope.
steps.outcome: Persistent foothold established and documented.

steps.title: Maintain access and perform periodic low-profile activity across the engagement window
steps.desc: Maintain the foothold across the multi-week window, performing periodic low-and-slow activity consistent with the threat-actor profile, while attending each scheduled sponsor check-in.
steps.guidance: Log all activity with timestamps; do not exceed the agreed end date without renewed authorization.
steps.outcome: Persistent access maintained for the agreed duration with all scheduled check-ins completed.
steps.abort: If any check-in reveals a concern, pause activity pending sponsor decision.

steps.title: Remove all implants and persistence mechanisms at engagement end
steps.desc: At the fixed end date, systematically remove every implant, scheduled task, and configuration change made across the engagement.
steps.guidance: Maintain a running artifact inventory throughout to make this step tractable.
steps.outcome: All touched hosts confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route long-dwell detection gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record which points across the multi-week window were or were not detected, with severity ratings, and route to the remediation backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per detection gap.

steps.title: Produce after-action report and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a report covering the full engagement timeline, detection outcomes, and recommended improvements, and brief the CISO/executive sponsor.
steps.outcome: After-action report delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-91322.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound exercise in which a controlled implant on a designated test system communicates with a red-team-controlled C2 server using infrequent, jittered, low-volume beacon traffic designed to blend with normal network noise, testing whether network detection and threat intelligence correlate the pattern.
ITID-91322.purpose: Captures an authorized red-team exercise simulating low-and-slow command-and-control beaconing to test network detection of covert, infrequent C2 traffic patterns.
scopeIncludes: Controlled implant beaconing to a red-team-controlled C2 infrastructure at low frequency with jitter
Testing of network traffic-analysis and threat-intelligence correlation against the beacon pattern
Testing of DNS/proxy log review processes for anomalous low-volume patterns
scopeExcludes: Persistence-mechanism-focused testing without a C2 beaconing component (Multi-Week Simulated Persistent Access leaf)
ITID-91322.severity: Beacon traffic remaining fully undetected through the exercise duration is a Critical finding.
ITID-91322.priority: P1 for fully undetected beaconing; P2 for detection occurring only via manual hunt rather than automated alerting.
ITID-91322.escalation: Escalate to the Network Security/Threat Intelligence team if automated network detection tooling produces zero alerts on the beacon traffic.
indicators: No network detection/IDS alert on the periodic low-volume beacon traffic
No threat-intelligence match flagging the C2 infrastructure
Beacon pattern only found via manual/ad-hoc log review
vectors: Jittered, low-frequency outbound beacon traffic from a controlled implant to a red-team-operated C2 endpoint
Use of common protocols (HTTPS, DNS) to blend beacon traffic with legitimate traffic
rootCauses: Network detection tuned for high-volume/obvious C2 patterns but not low-and-slow beaconing
Insufficient outbound traffic baselining
Threat-intelligence feeds not integrated with real-time network monitoring
controls: Network traffic analysis / IDS with beaconing-pattern detection
ITID-91322.detection: Measures detection capability specifically against covert, low-volume C2 patterns that evade high-volume-threshold detection logic.
ITID-91322.response: File findings for network detection tuning to catch low-and-slow patterns; retest after remediation.
metrics: Time to detect beacon pattern
Detection method (automated vs. manual hunt)
Volume/frequency threshold at which detection first triggers
sops: Red Team Rules of Engagement SOP
Long-Dwell Simulation Safety and Authorization SOP
ITID-91322.notes: C2 infrastructure must be entirely red-team-controlled and clearly attributable to the exercise; implant must be fully removed and verified post-exercise.
