ITID-92111.def: A planned blue-team exercise in which a known-malicious file, script, or behavior sample (e.g., an EICAR-style test file or a curated commodity-malware sample) is executed in an isolated test environment to measure whether the deployed EDR platform detects and alerts on it.
ITID-92111.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate EDR detection efficacy against a known, curated malware sample.
scopeIncludes: Detonating a known/curated malware sample in an isolated endpoint
Measuring whether an alert fires and how it is classified
Confirming the alert reaches the SIEM/SOC queue
scopeExcludes: Measuring how fast the EDR auto-contains or isolates the host after detection (sibling ITID-92112)
Using a genuinely novel or custom-built sample not present in threat intel feeds (closer to a red-team exercise)
ITID-92111.severity: A complete miss on a well-known, widely-signatured sample is a Critical finding; detection with incorrect severity classification is Medium; detection with delayed alerting only is Low.
ITID-92111.priority: P1 remediation when a well-known sample is missed entirely; P2 when detected but misclassified; P3 for cosmetic/labeling gaps.
ITID-92111.escalation: Escalate to the EDR vendor and the security engineering lead if a widely-known, signature-covered sample goes completely undetected; notify the detection engineering team lead for any misclassification.
indicators: EDR console shows no alert within the expected detection window
Alert generated but assigned an incorrect severity or technique tag
Alert fires but never forwards to the SIEM
vectors: Manual execution of a known-malicious or EICAR-style test file on an isolated test VM
Scripted detonation via an approved test harness
rootCauses: EDR signature/behavioral rule set out of date
Sample executed on an endpoint excluded from EDR policy scope
Cloud-lookup dependency unavailable during the test
ITID-92111.detection: Directly measures baseline EDR detection efficacy for well-characterized malware classes; does not measure containment speed.
ITID-92111.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any missed or misclassified detection; retest after the EDR vendor/engineering team applies a fix.
metrics: Detection rate across the curated sample set
Mean time to alert
Percentage of samples with correct severity classification
ITID-92111.notes: Must be run in an isolated test environment with no network egress to avoid accidental spread; sample set should be refreshed periodically to avoid testing only historically-known signatures.

playbook.name: EDR Detection Rate Test Against Known Malware Sample
playbook.description: Planned exercise that detonates a known, safe malware sample in a controlled environment to measure whether the EDR platform detects and alerts on it.

steps.title: Define test objective and success metric
steps.desc: Document the exercise objective: validate EDR detection coverage against a specific known malware sample/technique, with a target detection rate as the pass/fail metric.
steps.guidance: Select the sample family/technique from recent threat intel or a known gap. Define the metric precisely (e.g. alert fires within 5 minutes) so results are objectively scoreable.
steps.outcome: A written test objective and measurable success criterion is approved before scheduling.

steps.title: Select sample and detonation host
steps.desc: Choose the specific malware sample (or EICAR/Atomic Red Team analogue) and the isolated endpoint it will be detonated on.
steps.guidance: Prefer a de-fanged or simulated sample (e.g. Atomic Red Team, Caldera) unless a live sample is required and approved by security leadership.
steps.outcome: Sample and target host are documented and confirmed non-production.

steps.title: Obtain authorization and stakeholder sign-off
steps.desc: Get written sign-off from the security manager and system owner authorizing the detonation.
steps.guidance: Include the test window, target host, and rollback plan in the authorization request.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization is on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without documented authorization.

steps.title: Isolate detonation host from production network
steps.desc: Confirm the target endpoint sits on an isolated VLAN/sandbox segment with no path to production data or systems.
steps.guidance: Use a dedicated malware analysis VLAN or an air-gapped VM snapshpercentage-restored for the test.
steps.outcome: Detonation host is confirmed network-isolated.
steps.abort: Abort if isolation cannot be verified.

steps.title: Pre-notify SOC and EDR vendor on-call of the test window
steps.desc: Notify SOC shift leads and, if applicable, the managed EDR vendor that alerts from the test host during the window are expected and should not be escalated as a live incident.
steps.guidance: Include the test host hostname/IP and exact time window in the notification.
steps.outcome: SOC acknowledges the notification in writing/ticket.

steps.title: Detonate the sample on the target endpoint
steps.desc: Execute the malware sample on the isolated endpoint per the approved plan.
steps.guidance: Time-stamp the exact execution moment for later correlation against EDR alert timestamps.
steps.outcome: Sample executes and behaves as expected on the test host.
steps.abort: Abort and contain immediately if the sample shows unexpected lateral movement or network beaconing outside the sandbox.

steps.title: Capture EDR telemetry and alert output
steps.desc: Record whether the EDR console generated a detection, the alert severity, and the time-to-alert.
steps.guidance: Screenshot or export the raw alert and process tree from the EDR console for the after-action report.
steps.outcome: Detection outcome (fired/missed) and timing are captured with evidence.

steps.title: Clean up test artifacts and restore host baseline
steps.desc: Remove the malware sample and any dropped artifacts from the test host, and revert the VM to its pre-test snapshot.
steps.guidance: Confirm no residual files, scheduled tasks, or registry changes remain.
steps.outcome: Test host is restored to a clean baseline state.

steps.title: File remediation ticket for any detection gap
steps.desc: If detection failed or was delayed beyond target, open a ticket with the EDR/detection engineering team to tune signatures or behavioral rules.
steps.guidance: Attach the captured telemetry so engineers can reproduce the gap.
steps.outcome: A tracked ticket exists for any identified gap, or the exercise is marked fully passed.

steps.title: Update detection coverage scorecard
steps.desc: Record the test result (pass/fail, time-to-detect) in the ongoing EDR effectiveness scorecard/baseline.
steps.guidance: Trend results over successive tests to show whether coverage is improving.
steps.outcome: Scorecard reflects the latest test result.

steps.title: Publish after-action summary to stakeholders
steps.desc: Circulate a short after-action report to SOC leadership and system owners summarizing results and next steps.
steps.guidance: Include the remediation ticket reference if one was opened.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders are informed and remediation ownership is clear.

ITID-92112.def: A planned exercise measuring the time between a triggered EDR detection and the platform's automated response actions (host isolation, process kill, quarantine) once a known-malicious behavior has already been confirmed as detected.
ITID-92112.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate how quickly and reliably the EDR platform responds to and contains a detected threat, not just whether it detects one.
scopeIncludes: Timing the interval between alert generation and automated host isolation/quarantine
Validating that auto-containment policies fire as configured for a given severity tier
Confirming isolated hosts lose network access as expected
scopeExcludes: Whether the EDR detects the sample at all (sibling ITID-92111)
Manual SOC-analyst response time (covered under SOC drills, ITID-92131/92132)
ITID-92112.severity: Auto-containment failing to trigger at all for a Critical-severity detection is a Critical finding; containment triggering but exceeding the defined SLA window is Medium; minor timing variance within tolerance is Low/informational.
ITID-92112.priority: P1 if auto-containment does not fire when policy requires it; P2 if it fires outside the target time SLA; P3 for logging/reporting gaps around the containment action.
ITID-92112.escalation: Escalate to the EDR platform owner and security engineering if auto-containment fails to trigger on a policy-mandated severity tier; notify IT operations if containment actions risk business disruption.
indicators: Time-to-isolation exceeds the documented SLA
Auto-containment policy does not fire despite a matching detection severity
Host remains network-reachable after the platform reports 'isolated'
vectors: Execution of a pre-confirmed detected malware sample on a test endpoint to trigger the response pipeline
rootCauses: Auto-containment policy misconfigured or disabled for the tested severity tier
Network isolation action blocked by a conflicting firewall/NAC rule
Response action queued but delayed by platform load
ITID-92112.detection: Measures response/containment effectiveness downstream of detection; assumes detection already works and isolates that variable.
ITID-92112.response: File a finding if containment fails or exceeds SLA; retune auto-containment policy thresholds and retest; update the EDR response runbook if manual steps were required.
metrics: Mean time to isolation/containment
Percentage of tests where auto-containment fired as policy-defined
SLA compliance rate over time
ITID-92112.notes: Run only against pre-confirmed detected samples so the test isolates containment timing rather than detection reliability; isolate the test host from production network segments beforehand.

playbook.name: EDR Response Time/Auto-Containment Test
playbook.description: Planned exercise measuring how quickly and effectively the EDR platform's automated isolation/containment response triggers against a simulated compromise.

steps.title: Define auto-containment objective and target SLA
steps.desc: Document which auto-containment capability is being tested (e.g. auto-isolate on ransomware behavior) and the target time-to-isolate SLA.
steps.guidance: Align the SLA target with the vendor's published capability and internal incident response requirements.
steps.outcome: Test objective and SLA target documented and approved.

steps.title: Select trigger behavior and target host
steps.desc: Choose the specific behavior pattern (e.g. mass file encryption simulation) that should trip auto-containment, and the isolated test host.
steps.guidance: Use a benign simulator such as Atomic Red Team's ransomware-behavior tests rather than real ransomware.
steps.outcome: Trigger technique and host are documented as non-production.

steps.title: Obtain authorization sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval from security leadership and the host owner before triggering auto-containment behavior.
steps.guidance: Confirm the EDR policy for the pilot group is set to actually enforce containment, not just alert.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Confirm test host is isolated and expendable
steps.desc: Verify the target endpoint is a disposable VM/sandbox host that can tolerate actual network isolation being triggered.
steps.guidance: Ensure no production workloads or shared drives are mapped to this host.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed safe to be auto-isolated.
steps.abort: Abort if the host cannot be safely isolated.

steps.title: Notify SOC and network team of the test window
steps.desc: Advise SOC on-call and network operations that an automated isolation event is expected from the test host and should not be treated as a live incident or manually reversed mid-test.
steps.guidance: Provide the exact host identifier and time window.
steps.outcome: SOC and network team acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Trigger the containment-worthy behavior and start the clock
steps.desc: Execute the simulated malicious behavior on the test host and log the exact start timestamp.
steps.guidance: Use a stopwatch/logging script correlated to system clock, not memory.
steps.outcome: Behavior executes and timer starts.
steps.abort: Abort and manually isolate if behavior spreads beyond the intended host.

steps.title: Measure time-to-isolate and capture the containment action
steps.desc: Record the timestamp the EDR platform actually isolates the host from network and the specific containment action taken.
steps.guidance: Cross-check the EDR console event log against the trigger timestamp.
steps.outcome: Time-to-isolate is captured and compared to the target SLA.

steps.title: Release host from isolation and restore baseline
steps.desc: Manually release the auto-isolated host, confirm connectivity restored, and revert to a clean snapshot.
steps.guidance: Verify the EDR agent status returns to normal/healthy after release.
steps.outcome: Host is fully restored to normal operating state.

steps.title: Open remediation ticket if SLA was missed
steps.desc: If time-to-isolate exceeded the target SLA or containment failed to trigger, file a ticket with the EDR admin team to tune the policy.
steps.guidance: Include captured timing evidence.
steps.outcome: Ticket opened for any SLA miss, or exercise marked passed.

steps.title: Update auto-containment SLA baseline
steps.desc: Record the measured time-to-isolate in the running baseline/scorecard for this capability.
steps.guidance: Compare against prior test cycles to track improvement or regression.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated with current result.

steps.title: Share findings with EDR policy owners
steps.desc: Distribute results to the team responsible for EDR containment policy tuning.
steps.guidance: Recommend a re-test date if policy changes are made.
steps.outcome: Findings acknowledged and next steps assigned.

ITID-92113.def: A catch-all classification for planned EDR validation exercises that fall outside the detection-rate and response-time/auto-containment test categories, pending reclassification or documentation of a new sub-type.
ITID-92113.purpose: Intake bucket for EDR effectiveness test activity that does not cleanly map to a defined detection-rate or response-time test type.
scopeIncludes: EDR effectiveness activity not yet matched to a specific defined sub-type
Ad hoc or exploratory EDR validation exercises
scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-92111 (detection rate) or ITID-92112 (response time/containment) once identified
ITID-92113.severity: Assess on a case-by-case basis using the general EDR-finding severity framework until the activity is reclassified.
ITID-92113.priority: Triage promptly to confirm whether reclassification to a defined sub-type is appropriate.
ITID-92113.escalation: Escalate to the detection engineering lead for reclassification guidance if volume in this bucket grows.
indicators: Test activity logged without a clear match to an existing EDR test sub-type
vectors: Varies; not yet characterized
rootCauses: Varies; not yet characterized
ITID-92113.detection: Not standardized; depends on the specific activity captured under this catch-all.
ITID-92113.response: Review periodically and reclassify recurring patterns into a formally defined sub-type.
metrics: Volume of records filed under this catch-all over time
ITID-92113.notes: This leaf should stay low-volume; a growing count is a signal to define new Tier-5 EDR test sub-types.

playbook.name: General EDR Effectiveness Test
playbook.description: General-purpose planned exercise to validate overall EDR platform detection and response effectiveness when no more specific test type applies.

steps.title: Define scope of the EDR effectiveness test
steps.desc: Document which EDR capabilities are in scope (detection, alerting, containment, or a mix) and the objective of the exercise.
steps.guidance: Use this general test type only when the exercise spans multiple capabilities or doesn't fit a more specific EDR test.
steps.outcome: Scope and objective documented and approved.

steps.title: Select techniques and test host(s)
steps.desc: Choose the set of techniques/behaviors to exercise and the isolated host(s) they will run on.
steps.guidance: A MITRE ATT&CK-mapped technique list (e.g. via Atomic Red Team) keeps coverage broad and repeatable.
steps.outcome: Technique list and hosts documented as non-production.

steps.title: Obtain authorization sign-off
steps.desc: Get documented approval from security leadership before running the exercise.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Confirm isolated test environment
steps.desc: Verify all test hosts are on an isolated segment with no production connectivity.
steps.outcome: Isolation confirmed for all in-scope hosts.
steps.abort: Abort if isolation cannot be confirmed.

steps.title: Pre-notify SOC of expected test alerts
steps.desc: Advise the SOC shift that alerts from the listed test hosts during the window are exercise-generated and should not be escalated as real incidents.
steps.outcome: SOC acknowledgment on record.

steps.title: Execute the technique set
steps.desc: Run each selected technique/behavior against the test host(s) in sequence.
steps.guidance: Log start/stop time for each technique for correlation.
steps.outcome: All planned techniques executed.
steps.abort: Abort remaining techniques if a test host behaves unexpectedly outside the sandbox.

steps.title: Capture detection/response results per technique
steps.desc: For each technique, record whether EDR detected it, alerted, and/or auto-responded.
steps.guidance: Build a simple pass/fail matrix by technique.
steps.outcome: Results matrix completed for all techniques.

steps.title: Clean up test hosts
steps.desc: Remove all test artifacts and restore hosts to their pre-test snapshot/baseline.
steps.outcome: All test hosts restored to clean state.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets for each technique that was missed or under-detected.
steps.guidance: Prioritize by technique severity/likelihood.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all identified gaps.

steps.title: Update overall EDR coverage scorecard
steps.desc: Record aggregate detection rate across the technique set in the coverage baseline.
steps.outcome: Scorecard updated.

ITID-92121.def: A planned exercise in which a known-malicious or policy-violating event (e.g., a simulated brute-force pattern, a known-bad IOC, or a synthetic log line matching a detection rule) is injected into the log pipeline to confirm the corresponding SIEM correlation rule triggers an alert.
ITID-92121.purpose: Captures the test type used to confirm SIEM correlation rules and alert logic fire correctly when a known-bad event is deliberately injected.
scopeIncludes: Injecting synthetic or replayed known-bad events matched to specific correlation rules
Confirming the expected alert fires with correct fields and severity
Verifying alert routing to the SOC queue/ticketing system
scopeExcludes: Assessing whether required log sources are even being ingested (sibling ITID-92122)
Analyst-side triage performance once the alert exists (covered under SOC drills)
ITID-92121.severity: A rule that fails to fire at all for a known-bad injected event is a Critical finding; a rule that fires with incorrect severity or missing fields is Medium; cosmetic alert-formatting issues are Low.
ITID-92121.priority: P1 for a silent/non-firing correlation rule protecting a high-value use case; P2 for misclassified severity; P3 for formatting/field gaps.
ITID-92121.escalation: Escalate to the detection engineering lead if a rule protecting a Tier-1 use case fails to fire; notify the SOC manager if alert routing itself is broken.
indicators: No alert generated despite a matching injected event
Alert fires with incorrect severity, missing MITRE tagging, or wrong asset attribution
Alert generated but does not reach the SOC queue
vectors: Controlled injection of synthetic or replayed known-bad log events via an approved test log source or event generator
rootCauses: Correlation rule logic drifted from its intended detection use case
Rule disabled or set to a non-alerting mode
Field-mapping mismatch between the log source and the rule's expected schema
ITID-92121.detection: Confirms that a specific, targeted correlation rule is functioning end-to-end; does not assess overall log source coverage.
ITID-92121.response: File a finding and fix ticket for any silent rule; retest after the rule is corrected; update rule documentation and version history.
metrics: Percentage of tested rules firing correctly
Mean time to remediate a broken rule
Count of rules validated per cycle
ITID-92121.notes: Use synthetic/tagged test events wherever possible to avoid polluting production alert metrics; coordinate timing with the SOC to prevent false operational paging.

playbook.name: SIEM Alert Rule Validation Exercise (Known-Bad Event Injection)
playbook.description: Planned exercise that injects known-bad synthetic log events into the SIEM to verify existing correlation rules fire as designed.

steps.title: Select correlation rule(s) to validate and success metric
steps.desc: Identify the specific SIEM detection rule(s) under test and define what constitutes a pass (e.g. alert fires with correct severity within X minutes).
steps.guidance: Prioritize rules tied to high-severity use cases or rules that haven't fired in production recently.
steps.outcome: Rule list and success metric documented.

steps.title: Prepare synthetic known-bad event payloads
steps.desc: Build or source log events that should trigger each target rule (e.g. via a detection-testing framework).
steps.guidance: Tag synthetic events clearly (e.g. a test source IP/hostname) so they can be filtered out later.
steps.outcome: Event payloads prepared and reviewed for correctness.

steps.title: Obtain sign-off to inject test events
steps.desc: Get approval from the SIEM/detection engineering owner to inject synthetic events into the production SIEM pipeline.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Notify SOC of the injection window
steps.desc: Advise SOC analysts that tagged synthetic events will appear during the test window and should not be worked as real incidents.
steps.guidance: Share the exact tag/marker used so analysts can identify test events at a glance.
steps.outcome: SOC acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Confirm injection won't skew production dashboards/metrics
steps.desc: Check that synthetic events can be excluded from live KPI dashboards and won't distort real detection metrics.
steps.guidance: Use a dedicated test index/source if the SIEM supports it.
steps.outcome: Confirmed dashboards can filter or will not be materially affected.
steps.abort: Abort if injection would corrupt production metrics with no way to filter.

steps.title: Inject the synthetic events
steps.desc: Send the prepared known-bad log events into the SIEM ingestion pipeline.
steps.guidance: Inject one rule's events at a time to keep correlation clean.
steps.outcome: Events successfully ingested and visible in raw logs.

steps.title: Verify rule firing and alert accuracy
steps.desc: Confirm whether each target rule fired, with correct severity, entities, and timing.
steps.guidance: Capture the alert record and raw event correlation for evidence.
steps.outcome: Pass/fail recorded per rule.

steps.title: Purge or tag synthetic events post-test
steps.desc: Remove or permanently tag the injected events so they don't pollute historical search/reporting.
steps.outcome: Synthetic events cleaned up or clearly flagged as test data.

steps.title: File tuning tickets for rules that failed to fire
steps.desc: Open detection-engineering tickets for any rule that missed, misfired, or had incorrect severity.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all failures.

steps.title: Update rule validation scorecard
steps.desc: Record pass/fail results in the ongoing SIEM rule validation baseline.
steps.outcome: Scorecard updated.

ITID-92122.def: A planned exercise that audits the SIEM's log ingestion pipeline against the organization's expected log-source inventory to identify gaps in coverage, stale sources, or sources ingesting but not mapped to any detection use case.
ITID-92122.purpose: Captures the test type used to assess whether all expected log sources are actually being ingested into the SIEM and mapped to detection use cases.
scopeIncludes: Comparing the expected log-source inventory against actively ingesting sources
Identifying sources that stopped sending logs (silent failures)
Confirming ingested log sources are mapped to at least one detection use case
scopeExcludes: Whether a specific correlation rule fires correctly on ingested data (sibling ITID-92121)
Log retention/storage capacity assessment (a separate infrastructure concern)
ITID-92122.severity: A missing log source for a Tier-1 critical asset (e.g., domain controllers, EDR, firewall) is a Critical finding; a missing source for a lower-tier asset is Medium; an ingesting-but-unmapped source is Low.
ITID-92122.priority: P1 for critical-asset ingestion gaps; P2 for non-critical gaps; P3 for unmapped-but-ingesting sources.
ITID-92122.escalation: Escalate to the SIEM platform owner and the affected system owner when a critical log source has silently stopped ingesting.
indicators: Expected source absent from the SIEM's active source list
Log volume from a source drops to near-zero without a known cause
Source ingesting but with zero associated detection rules
vectors: N/A — this is a coverage audit, not a simulated technique
rootCauses: Log forwarder agent stopped or was uninstalled during patching
Source decommissioned without updating the SIEM onboarding record
New system deployed without a log-onboarding ticket being filed
Licensing/ingestion quota throttling silently dropping events
ITID-92122.detection: Directly measures breadth of detection coverage by confirming what data actually reaches the SIEM, independent of rule logic.
ITID-92122.response: File a finding and onboarding/remediation ticket for each gap; re-audit after log sources are restored or newly onboarded.
metrics: Percentage of expected log sources actively ingesting
Number of silent ingestion failures detected per cycle
Mean time to restore a failed log source
sops: SIEM Log Source Coverage Audit SOP
ITID-92122.notes: Should be run on a recurring cadence rather than as a one-off, since log source health degrades silently over time as infrastructure changes.

playbook.name: SIEM Log Ingestion/Coverage Gap Assessment
playbook.description: Planned exercise that audits which log sources are actually flowing into the SIEM to identify visibility gaps.

steps.title: Define expected log source inventory and scope
steps.desc: Compile the authoritative list of systems/log sources that should be sending logs to the SIEM (endpoints, firewalls, cloud, identity, etc.).
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against the asset inventory/CMDB.
steps.outcome: Expected source list documented and scoped for this assessment.

steps.title: Define coverage success metric
steps.desc: Set a target ingestion coverage percentage and freshness threshold (e.g. 95% of sources with logs in the last 24h).
steps.outcome: Metric and threshold documented.

steps.title: Notify SIEM/infra owners of the assessment window
steps.desc: Advise SIEM platform and log-source owning teams that a coverage audit is underway so any query load or config checks aren't mistaken for an incident.
steps.outcome: Owners acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Query actual ingestion volume per expected source
steps.desc: Run queries against the SIEM to determine last-seen timestamp and event volume for each expected source.
steps.guidance: Automate this with a saved search/dashboard for repeatability.
steps.outcome: Per-source ingestion data collected.

steps.title: Identify silent, stale, or missing sources
steps.desc: Compare actual ingestion data against the expected source list to flag sources with no data, stale data, or unexpectedly low volume.
steps.outcome: A gap list of silent/stale/missing sources is produced.

steps.title: Root-cause a sample of identified gaps
steps.desc: For a representative sample of gaps, investigate whether the cause is a broken forwarder, misconfiguration, decommissioned asset, or parsing failure.
steps.outcome: Root cause identified for sampled gaps.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for each confirmed gap
steps.desc: Open tickets assigned to the responsible team for each broken or missing log source.
steps.guidance: Prioritize by asset criticality.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all confirmed gaps.

steps.title: Update the source inventory/CMDB reference
steps.desc: Correct the expected source list to reflect decommissioned or renamed assets found during the assessment.
steps.outcome: Inventory reflects current reality.

steps.title: Update log coverage scorecard/baseline
steps.desc: Record the measured coverage percentage against the target metric for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated with current coverage figure.

ITID-92123.def: A catch-all classification for planned SIEM validation exercises that fall outside the alert-rule-validation and log-ingestion-coverage test categories, pending reclassification or documentation of a new sub-type.
ITID-92123.purpose: Intake bucket for SIEM log analysis and detection exercise activity that does not cleanly map to a defined rule-validation or coverage-assessment test type.
scopeIncludes: SIEM exercise activity not yet matched to a specific defined sub-type
Ad hoc SIEM validation or analyst-tooling exercises
scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-92121 (rule validation) or ITID-92122 (ingestion coverage) once identified
ITID-92123.severity: Assess on a case-by-case basis using general SIEM-finding severity framework until the activity is reclassified.
ITID-92123.priority: Triage promptly to confirm whether reclassification to a defined sub-type is appropriate.
ITID-92123.escalation: Escalate to the detection engineering lead for reclassification guidance if volume in this bucket grows.
indicators: Test activity logged without a clear match to an existing SIEM test sub-type
vectors: Varies; not yet characterized
rootCauses: Varies; not yet characterized
ITID-92123.detection: Not standardized; depends on the specific activity captured under this catch-all.
ITID-92123.response: Review periodically and reclassify recurring patterns into a formally defined sub-type.
metrics: Volume of records filed under this catch-all over time
ITID-92123.notes: This leaf should stay low-volume; a growing count is a signal to define new Tier-5 SIEM test sub-types.

playbook.name: General SIEM Log Analysis and Detection Exercise
playbook.description: General-purpose planned exercise validating SIEM log analysis and detection capability when no more specific SIEM test type applies.

steps.title: Define exercise scope and objective
steps.desc: Document what aspect(s) of SIEM log analysis/detection capability are being validated in this general exercise.
steps.guidance: Use this test type only when the exercise doesn't map cleanly to rule validation or ingestion-gap assessment.
steps.outcome: Scope and objective documented and approved.

steps.title: Obtain authorization sign-off
steps.desc: Get approval from the SIEM/detection engineering owner before running the exercise.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Notify SOC of the exercise window
steps.desc: Advise SOC analysts of the test window and how test-related activity/events will be identifiable.
steps.outcome: SOC acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Confirm no impact to production dashboards or SLAs
steps.desc: Verify the exercise activity will not distort live detection metrics or breach SIEM licensing/ingestion limits.
steps.outcome: Confirmed safe to proceed.
steps.abort: Abort if a material production impact is identified.

steps.title: Execute the planned analysis/detection activity
steps.desc: Carry out the defined exercise steps (e.g. query building, log review, correlation testing) against the SIEM.
steps.outcome: Planned activity completed.

steps.title: Capture results and observations
steps.desc: Document findings, including any anomalies, gaps, or unexpected behavior observed during the exercise.
steps.outcome: Findings documented with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Clean up any test data or artifacts
steps.desc: Remove or tag any synthetic data created for the exercise.
steps.outcome: SIEM returned to normal operating state with no residual test data confusion.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for identified gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets for any capability gaps found during the exercise.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened as needed.

steps.title: Document after-action summary
steps.desc: Summarize the exercise outcome and any follow-up actions for stakeholders.
steps.outcome: Summary distributed and filed.

ITID-92131.def: A planned exercise in which simulated or synthetic alerts are pushed into the SOC's live queue to measure analyst triage speed (time to acknowledge/classify) and accuracy (correct severity, correct disposition, correct next action).
ITID-92131.purpose: Captures the test type used to measure how quickly and accurately SOC analysts triage injected or simulated alerts.
scopeIncludes: Injecting synthetic alerts of known ground-truth severity into the analyst queue
Timing analyst acknowledgment and initial triage decision
Scoring triage accuracy against the known-correct disposition
scopeExcludes: Testing whether analysts correctly escalate per procedure once triage is complete (sibling ITID-92132)
Testing the underlying detection rule's own accuracy (covered under SIEM/EDR test ITIDs)
ITID-92131.severity: A high-severity synthetic alert triaged as benign (a 'miss') is a Critical finding; triage exceeding the SLA window is Medium; minor documentation gaps in the triage note are Low.
ITID-92131.priority: P1 for a missed high-severity alert; P2 for SLA breaches; P3 for documentation quality gaps.
ITID-92131.escalation: Escalate to the SOC manager for individual or team-wide triage-accuracy gaps; escalate to the training lead for recurring skill gaps.
indicators: Median triage time within or below the target SLA
High concordance between analyst disposition and ground-truth severity
A high-severity synthetic alert triaged as low/benign is a genuine finding
vectors: Injection of synthetic, pre-scored alerts of varying severity into the live SOC queue via an approved test-case generator
rootCauses: Analyst unfamiliarity with a newer alert type or detection rule
Queue overload masking individual alerts (volume/fatigue effect)
Insufficient documented triage criteria for an ambiguous alert category
mitreTechniques: Varies by injected scenario; drawn from the full ATT&CK matrix to reflect realistic triage variety
ITID-92131.detection: Measures human-layer triage performance downstream of detection; does not assess whether the underlying detection logic is sound.
ITID-92131.response: Provide individualized and team-level feedback; file training-gap findings; retest after coaching or procedural updates.
metrics: Median/95th-percentile triage time
Triage accuracy rate
Missed-alert rate for high-severity synthetic injects
ITID-92131.notes: Synthetic alerts must be clearly tagged internally as test data so they are excluded from production incident metrics.

playbook.name: SOC Analyst Triage Speed/Accuracy Drill
playbook.description: Planned drill that feeds SOC analysts a batch of simulated alerts to measure triage speed and classification accuracy.

steps.title: Define drill objective and scoring metric
steps.desc: Document what is being measured — e.g. mean time to triage and percentage correctly classified (true positive/false positive/benign) — and the target thresholds.
steps.guidance: Base thresholds on current SOC SLAs so results are actionable.
steps.outcome: Objective and scoring rubric documented and approved.

steps.title: Build the simulated alert batch and answer key
steps.desc: Prepare a set of realistic alert scenarios (mix of true positive, false positive, benign) with a known-correct answer key for scoring.
steps.guidance: Vary difficulty and alert types to reflect real SOC queue diversity.
steps.outcome: Alert batch and answer key prepared and reviewed.

steps.title: Notify SOC leadership and schedule the drill
steps.desc: Get SOC manager sign-off on timing so the drill doesn't collide with a real high-volume incident period.
steps.outcome: Drill scheduled with leadership approval.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Isolate drill alerts from the live triage queue
steps.desc: Ensure simulated alerts are injected into a training/sandbox queue, not the live SOC queue that handles real customer/production incidents.
steps.guidance: If a live queue must be used, clearly tag drill alerts so they aren't mistaken for real ones by other shifts.
steps.outcome: Drill alerts are confirmed isolated or clearly tagged.
steps.abort: Abort if isolation/tagging cannot be guaranteed.

steps.title: Brief participating analysts on drill ground rules
steps.desc: Inform participating analysts this is a measured drill, not a real queue, and clarify how results will be used (development, not punitive).
steps.guidance: Emphasize the drill supports training, not performance discipline.
steps.outcome: Analysts briefed and drill ground rules acknowledged.

steps.title: Run the timed triage drill
steps.desc: Present the simulated alert batch to participating analysts and record start/stop times per alert.
steps.outcome: All analysts complete the batch with timing captured.

steps.title: Score results against the answer key
steps.desc: Compare each analyst's classification and timing against the answer key to compute accuracy and speed metrics.
steps.outcome: Scored results produced per analyst and in aggregate.

steps.title: Provide individual and team feedback
steps.desc: Give analysts constructive feedback on missed or slow triages, framed as coaching.
steps.guidance: Avoid public ranking; keep feedback developmental.
steps.outcome: Feedback delivered to all participants.

steps.title: Identify and schedule targeted training for gaps
steps.desc: For alert types with low accuracy scores, schedule follow-up training or playbook updates.
steps.outcome: Training plan created for identified weak areas.

steps.title: Update SOC triage performance baseline
steps.desc: Record aggregate speed/accuracy results in the ongoing SOC performance baseline for trend tracking across drill cycles.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92132.def: A planned exercise measuring whether SOC analysts escalate a simulated confirmed incident to the correct next tier/team, within the required time window, and with the required information included in the handoff.
ITID-92132.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate that analysts correctly follow the defined escalation path once an incident is triaged.
scopeIncludes: Testing escalation-path adherence (right team, right severity threshold)
Timing the interval between triage completion and escalation
Assessing completeness of the escalation handoff (required fields/context)
scopeExcludes: Initial triage speed/accuracy itself (sibling ITID-92131)
Full cross-functional tabletop exercises spanning executive stakeholders (a separate ITID domain)
ITID-92132.severity: A failure to escalate a scenario that meets mandatory escalation criteria is a Critical finding; an escalation that is late but complete is Medium; an escalation that is timely but missing required context is Low/Medium.
ITID-92132.priority: P1 for a missed mandatory escalation; P2 for late escalations; P3 for incomplete handoff documentation.
ITID-92132.escalation: Escalate to the SOC manager for any missed mandatory escalation; escalate to the IR lead if the gap could plausibly have affected a real incident's outcome.
indicators: Escalation occurs within the defined SLA with all required fields
Escalation ticket/handoff missing required context (affected asset, evidence, initial scope)
No escalation logged despite scenario meeting mandatory-escalation criteria
vectors: Injection of a pre-scored simulated incident requiring mandatory escalation, observed end-to-end through the escalation workflow
rootCauses: Escalation criteria not clearly documented or recently changed without analyst retraining
Escalation tooling/ticketing integration failure
Analyst uncertainty about severity threshold triggering escalation
mitreTechniques: Varies by injected scenario; drawn from the full ATT&CK matrix to reflect realistic escalation scenarios
ITID-92132.detection: Measures procedural adherence downstream of triage; does not assess detection or initial triage quality.
ITID-92132.response: File a finding and retrain/update procedures for any missed or incomplete escalation; retest after remediation.
metrics: Escalation SLA compliance rate
Percentage of escalations with complete required context
Missed mandatory-escalation rate
ITID-92132.notes: Coordinate with the IR team beforehand so simulated escalations are not mistaken for real incidents downstream of the SOC.

playbook.name: SOC Escalation Procedure Drill
playbook.description: Planned drill validating that SOC analysts follow the correct escalation path and timing for a simulated high-severity alert.

steps.title: Define escalation scenario and target SLA
steps.desc: Select the escalation scenario to simulate (e.g. suspected active ransomware) and the target time-to-escalate per the IR plan.
steps.guidance: Choose a scenario that exercises the full escalation chain, including out-of-hours paths if relevant.
steps.outcome: Scenario and SLA target documented.

steps.title: Identify escalation chain participants and notify leadership
steps.desc: Confirm who sits in the escalation chain being tested (on-call IR lead, management, etc.) and get sign-off to run the drill against them.
steps.guidance: Decide in advance whether participants will be forewarned (announced) or not (unannounced) and get leadership approval for that choice.
steps.outcome: Escalation chain participants identified and drill approved.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Tag the simulated alert as a drill in all internal systems
steps.desc: Ensure the simulated alert/ticket is clearly marked as a drill in the ticketing system so it isn't mistaken for a real incident by anyone outside the drill scope.
steps.guidance: If unannounced, ensure a designated safety observer can immediately reveal the drill status if real escalation actions (e.g. contacting a regulator or customer) are about to be triggered.
steps.outcome: Drill marking and safety-observer plan in place.

steps.title: Define an abort/reveal condition
steps.desc: Set a clear condition under which the drill is immediately revealed to participants (e.g. before any real external communication is sent).
steps.outcome: Abort/reveal condition documented and understood by the safety observer.
steps.abort: Reveal drill status immediately if a participant is about to take an irreversible real-world action.

steps.title: Inject the simulated high-severity alert
steps.desc: Introduce the scenario alert into the SOC queue at the planned time and begin timing the escalation chain.
steps.outcome: Alert received by the SOC and clock started.

steps.title: Observe and log each escalation step and timestamp
steps.desc: Track when the alert is escalated at each stage of the chain and compare against the target SLA.
steps.guidance: Note any wrong-path escalations or missed steps.
steps.outcome: Full escalation timeline captured.

steps.title: Reveal the drill and debrief participants
steps.desc: Inform all participants the event was a drill and walk through what happened.
steps.guidance: Keep tone supportive; the goal is procedure validation, not blame.
steps.outcome: Participants debriefed.

steps.title: File remediation actions for escalation gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets/tasks to fix any broken escalation paths, missing contact info, or SLA misses found.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update the escalation procedure/runbook
steps.desc: Revise the IR escalation runbook to reflect corrected contacts, paths, or timing expectations.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated.

ITID-92133.def: A catch-all classification for planned SOC drill exercises that fall outside the triage and escalation test categories, pending reclassification or documentation of a new sub-type.
ITID-92133.purpose: Intake bucket for SOC drill activity that does not cleanly map to a defined triage-speed/accuracy or escalation-procedure test type.
scopeIncludes: SOC drill activity not yet matched to a specific defined sub-type
Ad hoc or exploratory SOC readiness exercises
scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-92131 (triage) or ITID-92132 (escalation) once identified
ITID-92133.severity: Assess on a case-by-case basis using the general SOC-drill severity framework until the activity is reclassified.
ITID-92133.priority: Triage promptly to confirm whether reclassification to a defined sub-type is appropriate.
ITID-92133.escalation: Escalate to the SOC manager for reclassification guidance if volume in this bucket grows.
indicators: Test activity logged without a clear match to an existing SOC drill sub-type
vectors: Varies; not yet characterized
rootCauses: Varies; not yet characterized
ITID-92133.detection: Not standardized; depends on the specific activity captured under this catch-all.
ITID-92133.response: Review periodically and reclassify recurring patterns into a formally defined sub-type.
metrics: Volume of records filed under this catch-all over time
ITID-92133.notes: This leaf should stay low-volume; a growing count is a signal to define new Tier-5 SOC drill sub-types.

playbook.name: General SOC Drill
playbook.description: General-purpose planned SOC drill exercising operational readiness when no more specific SOC drill type applies.

steps.title: Define drill scope and objective
steps.desc: Document what SOC capability or process this general drill exercises.
steps.guidance: Use this test type only when the drill doesn't map to a specific triage or escalation drill.
steps.outcome: Scope and objective documented and approved.

steps.title: Obtain SOC leadership sign-off and schedule
steps.desc: Confirm timing with SOC leadership to avoid collision with real incident activity.
steps.outcome: Drill scheduled and approved.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Tag drill activity to prevent confusion with real incidents
steps.desc: Ensure any simulated alerts, tickets, or communications used in the drill are clearly marked as drill artifacts.
steps.outcome: All drill artifacts clearly tagged.

steps.title: Brief participants on drill ground rules
steps.desc: Explain the drill's purpose and how results will be used before starting.
steps.outcome: Participants briefed.

steps.title: Run the drill scenario
steps.desc: Execute the planned SOC drill activity per the scoped scenario.
steps.outcome: Drill scenario completed.

steps.title: Observe and record performance against objectives
steps.desc: Capture qualitative and quantitative observations of how the SOC performed against the drill objective.
steps.outcome: Observations documented.

steps.title: Debrief participants
steps.desc: Reveal drill conclusion and review performance with participants in a supportive, developmental manner.
steps.outcome: Debrief completed.

steps.title: File remediation actions for identified gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets/tasks for any process or tooling gaps identified.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update SOC readiness baseline/runbook

steps.outcome: Baseline/runbook updated.

ITID-92211.def: A planned exercise in which authorized traffic is generated from one network segment/VLAN toward another to confirm that segmentation controls (VLAN ACLs, firewall rules between segments) enforce the intended isolation boundary.
ITID-92211.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate that VLAN and network-segment isolation boundaries actually block traffic they are designed to block.
scopeIncludes: Attempting authorized cross-VLAN/cross-segment traffic against defined boundary rules
Confirming denied traffic is actually blocked (not just logged as should-block)
Validating that permitted exceptions are scoped as narrowly as documented
scopeExcludes: Zero Trust identity-based micro-segmentation controls at the workload/application level (sibling ITID-92212)
Full network penetration testing spanning multiple control layers (a separate assessment type)
ITID-92211.severity: Traffic that should be blocked between a high-value segment (e.g., OT, PCI, domain controller VLAN) and a general-user segment succeeding is a Critical finding; a non-critical segment boundary failure is Medium; an overly broad but non-exploitable exception is Low.
ITID-92211.priority: P1 for boundary failures affecting high-value/regulated segments; P2 for general segment failures; P3 for overly permissive but low-risk exceptions.
ITID-92211.escalation: Escalate to the network engineering lead and CISO for any boundary failure affecting a regulated or high-value segment.
indicators: Test traffic that should be denied is instead permitted through the segment boundary
ACL/firewall rule order allows an unintended path
Logging correctly shows a deny action while the underlying device still forwards traffic
vectors: Authorized cross-segment connection attempts (ping, port scans, protocol-specific traffic) launched from a designated test host in one VLAN/segment toward another
rootCauses: Stale or overly broad ACL/firewall rule left from a prior project
Rule ordering/precedence misconfiguration
Segment boundary control not actually deployed at the point assumed by network diagrams
ITID-92211.detection: Validates whether lateral-movement paths between segments are actually closed, independent of whether an intrusion is ever detected.
ITID-92211.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any unexpected permitted path; retest after the ACL/firewall rule is corrected.
metrics: Percentage of tested boundary rules enforcing as documented
Number of unexpected permitted paths found per cycle
Mean time to remediate a boundary failure
ITID-92211.notes: Coordinate test windows with network operations to distinguish test traffic from a genuine lateral-movement alert.

playbook.name: VLAN/Segment Isolation Boundary Test
playbook.description: Planned exercise that attempts controlled cross-VLAN/segment traffic to verify network segmentation boundaries actually block unauthorized paths.

steps.title: Define segment boundaries under test and success criteria
steps.desc: Identify the specific VLANs/segments and the expected allow/deny traffic rules being validated, with pass/fail criteria per rule.
steps.guidance: Pull the intended segmentation policy from the network design document as the source of truth.
steps.outcome: Boundary list and success criteria documented and approved.

steps.title: Select source/destination test points
steps.desc: Choose specific non-production hosts on each side of the boundary to run connectivity probes from.
steps.guidance: Use dedicated test hosts rather than live production endpoints where possible.
steps.outcome: Test hosts identified and confirmed appropriate.

steps.title: Obtain network and security team authorization
steps.desc: Get sign-off from the network team and security leadership before running cross-segment probes.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Notify SOC and network operations of the test window
steps.desc: Advise SOC and NOC that probe traffic from the identified test hosts is expected and should not be chased as a real intrusion attempt.
steps.guidance: Provide exact source/destination IPs and time window.
steps.outcome: SOC/NOC acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Define a stop condition for the probe traffic
steps.desc: Set a rule for immediately halting probes if any unexpected production disruption is observed.
steps.outcome: Stop condition documented and understood by the test operator.
steps.abort: Halt all probing immediately if production traffic disruption is detected.

steps.title: Run cross-boundary connectivity probes
steps.desc: Execute scoped port/protocol probes from each source test host toward each destination across the segment boundary.
steps.guidance: Use lightweight scanning tools with rate limiting to avoid load impact.
steps.outcome: All planned probes executed and logged.
steps.abort: Abort remaining probes if the stop condition is triggered.

steps.title: Record actual vs expected traffic outcome per rule
steps.desc: Compare which probes were blocked vs allowed against the intended segmentation policy.
steps.outcome: A results matrix of expected vs actual per boundary rule.

steps.title: Remove test traffic artifacts and restore normal monitoring state
steps.desc: Confirm no residual scan processes or firewall rule changes made for testing remain active.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed back to baseline state.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for any unauthorized path found
steps.desc: Open tickets with the network team for any segment boundary that allowed traffic it should have blocked.
steps.guidance: Prioritize by exposure severity (e.g. path to a sensitive segment).
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all confirmed gaps.

steps.title: Update segmentation validation baseline
steps.desc: Record the current test results in the ongoing segmentation assurance baseline for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92212.def: A planned exercise confirming that Zero Trust micro-segmentation policy (workload-to-workload, identity-aware access rules enforced independent of network location) correctly denies unauthorized workload-to-workload or user-to-workload access even when both endpoints sit on the same broad network segment.
ITID-92212.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate identity- and workload-based micro-segmentation controls in a Zero Trust architecture.
scopeIncludes: Testing workload-to-workload access decisions under the Zero Trust policy engine
Confirming identity/device posture signals are actually evaluated (not bypassed)
Testing that lateral access is denied even within the same VLAN when policy prohibits it
scopeExcludes: Traditional VLAN/perimeter-level segmentation boundaries (sibling ITID-92211)
Identity and access management provisioning/deprovisioning testing (a separate domain)
ITID-92212.severity: A policy engine granting access that should be denied under Zero Trust rules is a Critical finding, especially where the workloads share a network segment; a denied-but-slow policy decision (latency issue) is Low.
ITID-92212.priority: P1 for unauthorized access granted between sensitive workloads; P2 for partial policy enforcement gaps; P3 for performance/latency-only issues.
ITID-92212.escalation: Escalate to the Zero Trust/network architecture team and CISO for any unauthorized workload access granted, especially where legacy network segmentation would not have caught it.
indicators: Policy engine denies access consistent with defined micro-segmentation rules
Unauthorized workload-to-workload session established despite policy prohibiting it
Device/identity posture check bypassed or not enforced
vectors: Authorized test connections between workloads/identities with intentionally mismatched policy entitlements, launched from a designated test identity/device
rootCauses: Micro-segmentation policy not applied to a newly provisioned workload
Policy engine fail-open behavior under load or outage
Device posture/identity signal not correctly integrated into the policy decision
ITID-92212.detection: Validates the effectiveness of identity-aware access controls as a lateral-movement barrier beyond what network-layer segmentation alone provides.
ITID-92212.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any unauthorized access granted; retest after policy correction; review fail-open/fail-closed behavior.
metrics: Percentage of workloads with correctly enforced micro-segmentation policy
Unauthorized-access findings per cycle
Policy decision latency
sops: Zero Trust Micro-Segmentation Validation Test SOP
ITID-92212.notes: New workloads onboarded outside the standard provisioning pipeline are the most common source of coverage gaps; cross-check the workload inventory before testing.

playbook.name: Zero Trust Micro-Segmentation Validation Test
playbook.description: Planned exercise validating that zero-trust micro-segmentation policies correctly restrict workload-to-workload traffic to only explicitly allowed paths.

steps.title: Define micro-segmentation policy scope under test
steps.desc: Identify the specific workloads/services and their intended allow-listed communication paths per the zero-trust policy.
steps.guidance: Reference the policy engine's current rule set as the source of truth for intended behavior.
steps.outcome: Scope and expected policy behavior documented.

steps.title: Define success metric
steps.desc: Set the target for percentage of policy rules validated as correctly enforced.
steps.outcome: Success metric documented.

steps.title: Obtain authorization from platform and security owners
steps.desc: Get sign-off from the micro-segmentation platform owner and security leadership.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Use a non-production workload set for policy probing
steps.desc: Confirm the workloads used to generate test traffic are non-production or have an approved maintenance window.
steps.outcome: Test workloads confirmed safe.
steps.abort: Abort if only production workloads are available without a maintenance window.

steps.title: Notify platform on-call of expected policy-engine alerts
steps.desc: Advise the micro-segmentation platform on-call team that test-generated denied/allowed connection logs during the window are expected.
steps.outcome: On-call acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Attempt each allowed and disallowed communication path
steps.desc: Systematically test both paths that should be allowed and paths that should be blocked between workloads.
steps.outcome: All planned path tests executed.

steps.title: Capture policy engine enforcement decisions
steps.desc: Record what the micro-segmentation platform actually allowed or blocked for each tested path.
steps.guidance: Export policy engine logs for evidence.
steps.outcome: Enforcement results captured per path.

steps.title: Restore any temporary test configuration
steps.desc: Remove any temporary tags/labels or policy overrides created solely to support the test.
steps.outcome: Policy configuration confirmed back to production-intended state.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for enforcement gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets for any path that should have been blocked but was allowed (or vice versa, causing operational impact).
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all gaps.

steps.title: Update zero-trust policy validation baseline
steps.desc: Record results in the ongoing micro-segmentation assurance baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92213.def: A catch-all classification for planned segmentation validation exercises that fall outside the VLAN/segment boundary and Zero Trust micro-segmentation test categories, pending reclassification or documentation of a new sub-type.
ITID-92213.purpose: Intake bucket for network segmentation validation activity that does not cleanly map to a defined VLAN-boundary or Zero-Trust micro-segmentation test type.
scopeIncludes: Segmentation validation activity not yet matched to a specific defined sub-type
scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-92211 (VLAN/segment boundary) or ITID-92212 (Zero Trust micro-segmentation) once identified

ITID-92221.def: A planned exercise in which known WAF-bypass payload encodings and evasion techniques are submitted against a protected web application to confirm the WAF rule set still detects and blocks the underlying attack pattern.
ITID-92221.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate whether known WAF bypass techniques can evade the deployed rule set.
scopeIncludes: Submitting known bypass-encoded payloads (e.g., alternate encodings, case variation, parameter pollution) against protected endpoints
Confirming the WAF blocks the underlying malicious pattern despite the evasion attempt
Testing across the WAF's configured rule categories (SQLi, XSS, RCE, etc.)
scopeExcludes: Measuring the WAF's false-positive rate on legitimate traffic (sibling ITID-92222)
Full web application penetration testing beyond WAF-layer bypass techniques
ITID-92221.severity: A successful bypass reaching the application unblocked for a well-known technique class is a Critical finding; a bypass that is logged but not blocked (detect-only mode) is Medium; a bypass requiring an unusual, low-likelihood technique is Low.
ITID-92221.priority: P1 for bypasses of common, well-documented evasion techniques; P2 for detect-only gaps; P3 for edge-case technique gaps.
ITID-92221.escalation: Escalate to the WAF platform owner and application security lead for any successful bypass of a well-known technique class.
indicators: WAF blocks the evasion-encoded payload consistent with its unencoded equivalent
Evasion-encoded payload reaches the backend application unblocked
WAF logs the payload as suspicious but takes no blocking action
vectors: Submission of known WAF-bypass encodings and evasion techniques (e.g., double URL-encoding, comment injection, HTTP parameter pollution) against test endpoints
rootCauses: WAF rule set not updated to cover a newer bypass technique class
Rule set running in monitor/detect-only mode instead of block mode
Custom application logic bypassing the WAF's normalization assumptions
controls: WAF rule set and policy configuration
ITID-92221.detection: Validates the WAF as a compensating control against known exploitation techniques for public-facing applications.
ITID-92221.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any successful bypass; update WAF rules and retest; escalate to application-layer patching if the WAF alone cannot fully mitigate.
metrics: Bypass success rate across the tested technique set
Percentage of rules operating in block vs. monitor mode
Mean time to remediate a confirmed bypass
ITID-92221.notes: Run against a staging/non-production instance where possible; coordinate with application owners to avoid disrupting production traffic.

playbook.name: WAF Rule Bypass Attempt Test
playbook.description: Planned exercise attempting known WAF bypass techniques against a controlled target to verify web application firewall rules cannot be evaded.

steps.title: Define WAF rule set and bypass techniques under test
steps.desc: Identify the specific WAF rules (e.g. SQLi, XSS, path traversal protections) and known bypass technique categories to attempt.
steps.guidance: Reference OWASP WAF bypass technique references for technique selection.
steps.outcome: Rule set and technique list documented and approved.

steps.title: Select a staging/non-production target application
steps.desc: Choose an application instance that mirrors production WAF configuration but is not itself production.
steps.outcome: Target confirmed non-production with matching WAF ruleset.

steps.title: Obtain authorization sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval from the application owner and security leadership before running bypass attempts.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Notify SOC of the test window and source IPs
steps.desc: Advise SOC that WAF-triggering requests from identified test source IPs during the window are expected and not a real attack.
steps.outcome: SOC acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Confirm test target has no real customer traffic/data exposure
steps.desc: Verify the staging target contains only synthetic data and no path to production data stores.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no real data exposure risk.
steps.abort: Abort if the target has any live customer data.

steps.title: Execute bypass technique payloads against the target
steps.desc: Run each selected bypass technique (encoding tricks, parameter pollution, case manipulation, etc.) against the target application.
steps.outcome: All planned bypass attempts executed and logged.

steps.title: Record which payloads were blocked vs bypassed
steps.desc: Capture WAF logs showing block/allow decisions for each attempted payload.
steps.outcome: Results matrix of blocked vs bypassed payloads produced.

steps.title: Clean up test payload traffic and confirm target integrity
steps.desc: Verify the staging application state is unaffected and remove any test artifacts submitted (e.g. test records created via payloads).
steps.outcome: Target confirmed clean and unaffected.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for successful bypasses
steps.desc: Open tickets with the WAF/security engineering team to tighten rules for any technique that successfully bypassed protection.
steps.guidance: Prioritize by exploitability severity.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all confirmed bypasses.

steps.title: Update WAF rule effectiveness baseline
steps.desc: Record results in the ongoing WAF assurance baseline for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92222.def: A planned exercise submitting a representative sample of legitimate application requests (normal user workflows, edge-case-but-valid input) against the WAF to measure the false-positive (legitimate traffic blocked) rate.
ITID-92222.purpose: Captures the test type used to measure how often the WAF incorrectly blocks legitimate application traffic.
scopeIncludes: Submitting known-legitimate request patterns, including valid edge cases, through the WAF
Measuring the rate at which legitimate requests are blocked or challenged
Identifying specific rules responsible for false positives
scopeExcludes: Testing whether malicious/bypass payloads are correctly blocked (sibling ITID-92221)
General application functional/regression testing unrelated to the WAF layer
ITID-92222.severity: A false-positive rate that blocks a critical business workflow (e.g., checkout, login) is a Critical finding; a false-positive rate affecting a non-critical workflow is Medium; isolated single-request false positives are Low.
ITID-92222.priority: P1 for false positives on critical business workflows; P2 for non-critical workflow impact; P3 for isolated edge-case false positives.
ITID-92222.escalation: Escalate to the WAF platform owner and the affected business/application owner for any false positive impacting a critical workflow.
indicators: Legitimate traffic sample passes through the WAF without unexpected blocks
A specific rule repeatedly blocks a known-valid request pattern
Business workflow completion rate drops after a WAF rule update
vectors: N/A — this test submits legitimate traffic patterns, not attack payloads
rootCauses: Overly broad rule pattern matching legitimate input that resembles an attack signature
Rule tuned against a generic ruleset without application-specific exceptions
Recent rule update introduced a regression
controls: WAF rule tuning and exception management
Change control for WAF rule updates
ITID-92222.detection: Assesses the operational cost/precision of the WAF's T1190-related detection rules rather than raw coverage.
ITID-92222.response: File a finding and tuning ticket for confirmed false positives; add application-specific exceptions; retest after tuning.
metrics: False-positive rate by rule and by workflow
Business workflow completion rate through the WAF
Mean time to tune a confirmed false-positive rule
ITID-92222.notes: Best run immediately after any WAF rule set update, since false-positive regressions are most common right after tuning changes.

playbook.name: WAF False-Positive Rate Assessment
playbook.description: Planned exercise sending a batch of legitimate traffic patterns through the WAF to measure how often it incorrectly blocks valid requests.

steps.title: Define legitimate traffic sample and target false-positive threshold
steps.desc: Compile a representative sample of known-legitimate request patterns (including edge cases like special characters in valid input) and set an acceptable false-positive rate threshold.
steps.guidance: Pull sample patterns from real traffic logs or application test suites where possible.
steps.outcome: Traffic sample and threshold documented.

steps.title: Select target application and WAF ruleset version
steps.desc: Identify the specific application and current WAF rule configuration being assessed.
steps.outcome: Target and ruleset version documented.

steps.title: Obtain application owner sign-off
steps.desc: Get approval to send the legitimate-traffic test batch against the target, including in production if that's where the assessment must run.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Notify application support/helpdesk of the test window
steps.desc: Advise application support that a controlled batch of test requests may appear and any resulting blocked-request tickets from the test window can be closed as test-related.
steps.outcome: Support team acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Rate-limit the test traffic to avoid load impact
steps.desc: Ensure the test request volume is throttled so it doesn't degrade application performance for real users.
steps.outcome: Test traffic confirmed within safe rate limits.
steps.abort: Abort if rate limiting cannot be guaranteed.

steps.title: Send the legitimate traffic sample through the WAF
steps.desc: Submit each request in the sample set and record the WAF's allow/block decision.
steps.outcome: All sample requests submitted and logged.

steps.title: Calculate the observed false-positive rate
steps.desc: Compare block decisions against the known-legitimate status of each request to compute the false-positive rate.
steps.outcome: False-positive rate calculated and compared to target threshold.

steps.title: Confirm application state unaffected by test traffic
steps.desc: Verify no unintended data changes or application errors resulted from the test batch.
steps.outcome: Application confirmed unaffected.

steps.title: File tuning tickets for rules causing excess false positives
steps.desc: Open tickets with the WAF team to tune or exempt rules causing legitimate traffic to be blocked above threshold.
steps.outcome: Tuning tickets opened as needed.

steps.title: Update WAF false-positive baseline
steps.desc: Record the measured false-positive rate in the ongoing WAF tuning baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.
