ITID-92231.def: A planned, tightly-scoped exercise generating a controlled volumetric traffic load against a production or production-equivalent environment to validate that upstream/on-prem DDoS mitigation scrubs the load as designed without causing a genuine outage.
ITID-92231.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate that production DDoS mitigation can absorb a controlled volumetric traffic surge without disrupting legitimate service.
scopeIncludes: Generating a pre-agreed, capped volumetric traffic load against a designated target
Confirming mitigation triggers at the expected threshold and traffic is scrubbed
Validating legitimate traffic continues to be served during the test window
scopeExcludes: Application-layer (Layer 7) DDoS and mitigation failover testing (sibling ITID-92232)
Uncapped/unscoped load testing not coordinated with the mitigation provider
ITID-92231.severity: Mitigation failing to trigger or legitimate traffic being dropped during a within-threshold test is a Critical finding; a delayed mitigation trigger is Medium; minor latency degradation within tolerance is Low.
ITID-92231.priority: P1 for mitigation failure or legitimate-traffic impact; P2 for delayed triggering; P3 for latency-only findings.
ITID-92231.escalation: Escalate immediately to the network/infrastructure on-call and the DDoS mitigation provider if the test risks becoming a genuine outage; notify the CISO and business stakeholders before the test window per required sign-off.
indicators: Mitigation engages at or before the documented threshold
Legitimate synthetic transactions continue succeeding throughout the test
Mitigation fails to engage, or legitimate traffic drops during the capped test load
vectors: Controlled, capped volumetric traffic generation (e.g., UDP/ICMP/SYN flood at an agreed rate) against a designated test target during a pre-approved window
rootCauses: Mitigation threshold set too high relative to realistic attack volumes
Traffic routed around the scrubbing path due to a DNS/routing misconfiguration
Provider-side capacity or contractual limit not accounting for current traffic baseline
ITID-92231.detection: Validates the organization's resilience against volumetric denial-of-service techniques at the network layer.
ITID-92231.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any mitigation failure; coordinate with the mitigation provider on threshold tuning; retest after remediation.
metrics: Time to mitigation engagement
Legitimate-traffic success rate during test
Peak absorbed volume without service degradation
ITID-92231.notes: Requires executive sign-off and coordination with the DDoS mitigation provider and business stakeholders before execution to avoid causing a genuine outage; must run within a pre-agreed capped volume and time window.

playbook.name: Controlled Volumetric Load Test Against Production Mitigation
playbook.description: Planned exercise generating a controlled volumetric traffic load against the production DDoS mitigation service to verify it activates and holds as designed.

steps.title: Define target mitigation capability and success threshold
steps.desc: Document which DDoS mitigation capability (e.g. scrubbing activation threshold, traffic absorption capacity) is being tested and the pass criteria.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the DDoS mitigation vendor, since many require advance notice for authorized load testing.
steps.outcome: Objective and threshold documented and approved.

steps.title: Define load profile and test window
steps.desc: Specify the traffic volume/profile to be generated and schedule a low-business-impact window.
steps.guidance: Choose an off-peak window to minimize risk to real users if mitigation is imperfect.
steps.outcome: Load profile and window documented.

steps.title: Obtain authorization from vendor, ISP, and leadership
steps.desc: Get written sign-off from the DDoS mitigation vendor, upstream ISP (if required), and internal leadership before generating load.
steps.guidance: Unauthorized volumetric testing can violate vendor/ISP acceptable use terms — confirm approvals in writing.
steps.outcome: All required signed authorizations on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without full authorization chain.

steps.title: Notify SOC, NOC, and customer support of the test window
steps.desc: Advise all relevant operational teams that a controlled load test is occurring and any resulting alerts or minor customer-facing latency reports are expected.
steps.outcome: All teams acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Define a hard abort threshold and kill switch
steps.desc: Set a specific metric (e.g. real user error rate, latency) that triggers immediate load generation stop, and confirm the operator has a tested kill switch.
steps.outcome: Abort threshold and kill switch confirmed functional before starting.
steps.abort: Stop load generation immediately if the abort threshold is breached.

steps.title: Generate the controlled load ramp
steps.desc: Ramp up traffic generation per the planned load profile while monitoring real-time impact.
steps.guidance: Ramp gradually rather than an instant full-volume spike.
steps.outcome: Load generated per plan with continuous monitoring.
steps.abort: Abort immediately if the kill-switch threshold is hit.

steps.title: Capture mitigation activation and performance data
steps.desc: Record when scrubbing/mitigation activated, how much traffic it absorbed, and any real-user impact observed.
steps.outcome: Mitigation performance data captured.

steps.title: Stop load generation and confirm traffic returns to normal
steps.desc: Halt the test traffic generator and verify production traffic patterns and latency return to baseline.
steps.outcome: Production confirmed back to normal state.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for mitigation shortfalls
steps.desc: Open tickets with the vendor/network team for any capacity or activation-time shortfall identified.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened as needed.

steps.title: Update DDoS resilience baseline
steps.desc: Record measured mitigation capacity and activation time in the ongoing resilience baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92232.def: A planned exercise generating a controlled Layer 7 (application-layer) traffic surge against a protected application to validate that rate-limiting, bot-mitigation, and failover mechanisms engage correctly without a genuine service outage.
ITID-92232.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate application-layer DDoS mitigation and its failover behavior under load.
scopeIncludes: Generating controlled application-layer request floods against a designated test endpoint
Validating rate-limiting/bot-mitigation engagement thresholds
Testing failover to backup capacity or degraded-service modes
scopeExcludes: Network/volumetric-layer DDoS testing (sibling ITID-92231)
General application load/performance testing unrelated to DDoS mitigation
ITID-92232.severity: Failover not engaging or legitimate users being denied service during a within-threshold test is a Critical finding; a delayed failover trigger is Medium; minor latency degradation within tolerance is Low.
ITID-92232.priority: P1 for failover failure or legitimate-user impact; P2 for delayed failover; P3 for latency-only findings.
ITID-92232.escalation: Escalate immediately to the application/infrastructure on-call if the test risks a genuine outage; notify the CISO and application owner before the test window per required sign-off.
indicators: Rate-limiting/bot-mitigation engages at the documented request-rate threshold
Failover to backup capacity completes within the target time window
Legitimate synthetic users continue completing transactions during the test
vectors: Controlled application-layer request flood (e.g., repeated requests to a resource-intensive endpoint) generated at an agreed rate against a designated test target
rootCauses: Rate-limiting threshold not tuned to the application's actual capacity
Bot-mitigation rules bypassed by request patterns mimicking legitimate browser behavior
Failover automation not tested since the last infrastructure change
ITID-92232.detection: Validates the organization's resilience against application-layer denial-of-service techniques and the reliability of automated failover.
ITID-92232.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any failover or mitigation failure; retest after remediation; update the DDoS runbook with observed behavior.
metrics: Time to failover completion
Legitimate-user transaction success rate during test
Rate-limiting engagement accuracy
ITID-92232.notes: Requires executive sign-off and coordination with the application owner before execution; must run within a pre-agreed capped request rate and time window to avoid a genuine outage.

steps.title: Stop flood traffic and confirm endpoint returns to normal

steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed back to normal.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for failover gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets for any delayed or failed mitigation failover identified.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened as needed.

steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92233.purpose: Intake bucket for DDoS resilience testing activity that does not cleanly map to a defined volumetric-load or application-layer-failover test type.

scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-92231 (volumetric load) or ITID-92232 (application-layer failover) once identified

ITID-92311.def: A planned exercise in which threat hunters form a specific hypothesis (e.g., 'an adversary is using LOLBins for defense evasion in our environment') and manually or semi-automatedly search environment telemetry to confirm whether the hypothesized technique would be detected if actually present.
ITID-92311.purpose: Captures the test type used to run a structured, hypothesis-driven threat hunt to validate detection coverage against a specific adversary technique or scenario.
scopeIncludes: Formulating a testable hypothesis tied to a specific ATT&CK technique or adversary TTP
Querying available telemetry sources to search for evidence supporting or refuting the hypothesis
Documenting detection gaps discovered during the hunt
scopeExcludes: Broad IOC-sweep hunts without a specific behavioral hypothesis (sibling ITID-92312)
Automated correlation-rule validation (covered under SIEM test ITIDs)
ITID-92311.severity: A hunt revealing that a plausible, high-likelihood technique would go completely undetected is a Critical finding; a hunt revealing partial/delayed visibility is Medium; a hunt confirming full coverage with only minor tuning opportunities is Low.
ITID-92311.priority: P1 for critical undetected-technique gaps tied to a realistic threat scenario; P2 for partial visibility gaps; P3 for minor tuning opportunities.
ITID-92311.escalation: Escalate to the detection engineering lead for any critical visibility gap; escalate to CTI for hypothesis refinement if the hunt surfaces evidence of genuine suspicious activity requiring investigation as an incident.
indicators: Hunt telemetry query returns sufficient data to confirm the technique would be visible if it occurred
Hunt reveals a telemetry or detection-rule gap for the hypothesized technique
Hunt unexpectedly surfaces activity warranting escalation as a genuine incident
vectors: Manual/semi-automated telemetry querying and pivoting based on a documented hypothesis (no live technique execution against production)
rootCauses: Relevant telemetry source not retained long enough or not queryable
No correlation rule exists yet for the hypothesized technique
Hunt hypothesis too broad/narrow to yield actionable results
mitreTechniques: Varies by hunt hypothesis; drawn from ATT&CK techniques relevant to the specific hypothesis under test
ITID-92311.detection: Directly probes detection coverage for a specific, well-reasoned adversary behavior not necessarily covered by existing automated rules.
ITID-92311.response: File a finding and detection-engineering ticket for any confirmed gap; convert validated hunt logic into a permanent correlation rule where feasible.
metrics: Number of hunts conducted per cycle
Percentage of hunts yielding a new detection rule
Mean time to close a confirmed hunt-identified gap
ITID-92311.notes: Hunt hypotheses should be informed by current threat intelligence relevant to the organization's sector and asset profile.

playbook.name: Hypothesis-Driven Threat Hunt Exercise
playbook.description: Planned exercise where hunters test a specific hypothesis about undetected adversary activity against real environment telemetry.

steps.title: Formulate the hunt hypothesis and objective
steps.desc: Document the specific hypothesis being tested (e.g. 'a known APT technique could be present in our environment undetected') and the data sources needed.
steps.guidance: Base the hypothesis on recent threat intel, a detection gap, or an unusual environment change.
steps.outcome: Hypothesis and required data sources documented and approved.

steps.title: Define scope and success criteria
steps.desc: Set the environment scope (which systems/data sources) and what constitutes a conclusive result (confirmed finding, or confidently ruled out).
steps.outcome: Scope and success criteria documented.

steps.title: Notify SOC leadership of the hunt window
steps.desc: Advise SOC leadership the hunt is starting so any hunter queries against production telemetry aren't misread as unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: SOC leadership acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Confirm hunt queries won't degrade production SIEM/log platform performance
steps.desc: Check that planned queries are scoped and rate-limited so they don't strain shared production analytics infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed safe query load.
steps.abort: Abort or reschedule if query load risks platform degradation.

steps.title: Define escalation path if a real threat is found
steps.desc: Clarify that if the hunt uncovers an actual active compromise (not just a hypothesis validation), it immediately converts to a real incident response, exiting the exercise track.
steps.outcome: Escalation path documented and understood by hunters.
steps.abort: Escalate immediately to incident response if genuine active compromise is found.

steps.title: Execute the hunt queries and analysis
steps.desc: Run the planned queries/analysis techniques against the in-scope data sources to test the hypothesis.
steps.outcome: Hunt analysis completed across all in-scope data sources.

steps.title: Document findings and evidence
steps.desc: Record whether the hypothesis was confirmed, refuted, or inconclusive, with supporting evidence.
steps.outcome: Findings documented with evidence trail.

steps.title: Convert new detection ideas into SIEM/EDR rules
steps.desc: For any detection gap the hunt exposed, work with detection engineering to build a repeatable automated rule so the same activity would be caught in future without manual hunting.
steps.outcome: New or improved detection rule(s) drafted or implemented.

steps.title: File remediation tickets for any confirmed weaknesses
steps.desc: Open tickets for any real vulnerability or misconfiguration uncovered during the hunt (short of a live incident).
steps.outcome: Tickets opened as needed.

steps.title: Publish hunt report and update the hunt hypothesis backlog
steps.desc: Document the full hunt narrative and add follow-on hypotheses to the backlog for future hunt cycles.
steps.outcome: Report published and backlog updated.

ITID-92312.def: A planned exercise in which a curated list of known indicators of compromise (IPs, hashes, domains) from threat intelligence feeds is swept across environment telemetry to confirm whether matches would be surfaced, without a specific behavioral hypothesis driving the search.
ITID-92312.purpose: Captures the test type used to run a broad indicator-of-compromise sweep across the environment to confirm known-bad indicators would be caught.
scopeIncludes: Sweeping current/recent threat intel IOC lists against log, DNS, and endpoint telemetry
Confirming IOC-matching tooling (SIEM watchlists, TIP integration) surfaces true matches
Documenting stale/false-positive-prone IOCs in the sweep list
scopeExcludes: Hypothesis-driven behavioral hunts targeting a specific TTP (sibling ITID-92311)
Threat intel feed integration/enrichment pipeline testing itself (covered under ITID-92321)
ITID-92312.severity: A sweep revealing that a widely-distributed, high-confidence IOC would not be surfaced by existing tooling is a Critical finding; a sweep revealing stale IOC lists causing noise is Medium; minor tuning opportunities are Low.
ITID-92312.priority: P1 for confirmed IOC-matching tooling gaps; P2 for stale/noisy IOC list issues; P3 for minor tuning opportunities.
ITID-92312.escalation: Escalate to the CTI lead and detection engineering if IOC-matching tooling fails to surface a high-confidence match; treat any genuine match found during the sweep as a real incident and escalate immediately per the IR process.
indicators: Sweep confirms known-bad IOCs would be surfaced by current tooling
Sweep reveals IOC-matching tooling gap (e.g., feed not integrated into the SIEM watchlist)
Sweep unexpectedly surfaces a genuine match requiring incident escalation
vectors: Automated or manual matching of curated IOC lists against retained telemetry (no live technique execution)
rootCauses: Threat intel feed not fully integrated into the SIEM/TIP watchlist pipeline
IOC list stale, reducing relevance and increasing noise
Telemetry retention window shorter than the IOC's relevant lookback period
mitreTechniques: Varies by IOC type; typically associated with C2 infrastructure and exfiltration-related indicators
ITID-92312.detection: Validates the mechanical reliability of IOC-based detection as a baseline layer, distinct from behavioral detection coverage.
ITID-92312.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any IOC-matching gap; refresh stale IOC lists; escalate any genuine match as a real incident.
metrics: Percentage of swept IOCs correctly surfaced by tooling
IOC list staleness (age distribution)
Number of genuine matches found per sweep
ITID-92312.notes: Any genuine match discovered during a sweep must be handled through the real incident-response process, not closed out as a test finding.

steps.title: Run the IOC sweep across in-scope telemetry

ITID-92321.def: A planned exercise confirming that subscribed threat intelligence feeds flow correctly into the TIP/SIEM, that enrichment data (reputation scores, actor attribution, context) attaches to relevant alerts, and that the pipeline is not silently failing.
ITID-92321.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate that threat intelligence feeds are correctly integrated into and enriching detection/analysis tooling.
scopeIncludes: Confirming feed data lands in the TIP/SIEM within the expected latency window
Validating enrichment fields populate correctly on relevant alerts/cases
Testing feed deduplication and confidence-scoring logic
scopeExcludes: Manual threat-actor attribution analysis skill assessment (sibling ITID-92322)
IOC-sweep hunting itself (covered under ITID-92312)
ITID-92321.severity: A feed silently failing to ingest for an extended period is a Critical finding; enrichment fields populating incorrectly or incompletely is Medium; minor latency beyond target SLA is Low.
ITID-92321.priority: P1 for silent feed ingestion failure; P2 for incorrect/incomplete enrichment; P3 for latency-only gaps.
ITID-92321.escalation: Escalate to the CTI lead and platform engineering if a feed has silently failed to ingest for longer than the defined tolerance window.
indicators: Feed data observable in the TIP/SIEM within the expected latency window
Enrichment fields correctly populate on test alerts
Feed ingestion volume drops to zero without a known cause
vectors: N/A — this is a pipeline/integration validation, not a simulated technique
rootCauses: Feed API credential expired or rate-limited
Feed schema changed upstream without a corresponding pipeline update
Enrichment rule not mapped to the correct alert field
ITID-92321.detection: Not a detection-technique validation exercise; assesses the health and reliability of the CTI enrichment pipeline itself.
ITID-92321.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any feed or enrichment failure; retest after the pipeline is restored.

Percentage of alerts with correctly populated enrichment fields
Mean time to detect and restore a silent feed failure
ITID-92321.notes: This is a pipeline-integrity exercise, not a detection-technique validation exercise, so no ATT&CK mapping applies.

ITID-92322.def: A planned exercise in which CTI analysts are given a synthetic or historical activity data set and asked to work through the actor-attribution process (TTP comparison, infrastructure overlap, campaign linkage) to assess the quality, speed, and defensibility of their conclusions.
ITID-92322.purpose: Captures the test type used to assess CTI analyst skill and process in attributing an activity to a threat actor using structured analytic techniques.
scopeIncludes: Working a synthetic or de-identified historical case through the attribution methodology
Assessing use of structured analytic techniques (e.g., analysis of competing hypotheses)
Reviewing confidence-level assignment and sourcing rigor
scopeExcludes: Feed integration/enrichment pipeline health testing (sibling ITID-92321)
Live production attribution work on an actual ongoing incident
ITID-92322.severity: A confident, high-impact attribution conclusion that the exercise reveals to be unsupported by the evidence is a Critical finding; process gaps that don't change the conclusion are Medium; minor documentation/sourcing gaps are Low.
ITID-92322.priority: P1 for unsupported high-confidence conclusions; P2 for process gaps; P3 for documentation gaps.
ITID-92322.escalation: Escalate to the CTI lead for any recurring analyst skill gap; escalate to the training lead if the exercise reveals a program-wide methodology gap.
indicators: Analyst attribution conclusion matches the exercise's known-correct answer with appropriately calibrated confidence
Analyst overstates confidence relative to available evidence
Analyst under-documents sourcing/reasoning for the conclusion
vectors: N/A — this is an analytic skills exercise using synthetic/historical data, not a live technique simulation
rootCauses: Analyst unfamiliar with a structured analytic technique (e.g., ACH)
Insufficient reference data/playbook for the attribution methodology
Time pressure leading to premature conclusion
controls: CTI analytic methodology and tradecraft standards
ITID-92322.detection: Not a detection-technique validation exercise; assesses analyst tradecraft quality rather than technical detection coverage.
ITID-92322.response: Provide individualized feedback and coaching; update the CTI methodology playbook if a systemic gap is found.
metrics: Attribution accuracy against known-correct answer
Confidence-calibration accuracy
Time to reach a defensible conclusion
ITID-92322.notes: Uses synthetic or fully de-identified historical data only; no ATT&CK detection-validation mapping applies since this is an analyst tradecraft exercise.

playbook.name: Threat Actor Attribution Analysis Drill
playbook.description: Planned drill giving analysts a simulated intrusion data set to practice and validate threat actor attribution analysis methodology.

steps.title: Define drill objective and scoring rubric
steps.desc: Document what attribution skill/process is being validated and how correctness will be scored against a known-answer scenario.
steps.outcome: Objective and rubric documented and approved.

steps.title: Build the simulated intrusion data set
steps.desc: Construct a realistic but fictional set of TTP/IOC evidence mapped to a known answer for attribution.
steps.guidance: Base it on a real published threat actor profile for realism, without implying it's an actual current incident.
steps.outcome: Data set and answer key prepared.

steps.title: Notify CTI team lead and schedule the drill
steps.desc: Get sign-off on timing so the drill doesn't collide with real CTI workload.
steps.outcome: Drill scheduled and approved.

steps.title: Clearly label the exercise data as fictional/simulated
steps.desc: Mark all drill materials so analysts and any downstream systems don't mistake it for a real attribution case.
steps.outcome: All materials clearly labeled.

steps.title: Run the attribution analysis drill
steps.desc: Have participating analysts work through the simulated evidence and produce an attribution assessment.
steps.outcome: Analysts complete their attribution assessments.

steps.title: Score results against the answer key
steps.desc: Compare each analyst's conclusion and reasoning against the known-correct attribution and methodology checklist.
steps.outcome: Scored results produced.

steps.title: Provide feedback and identify skill gaps
steps.desc: Give analysts constructive feedback on methodology gaps observed.
steps.guidance: Keep feedback developmental, not punitive.
steps.outcome: Feedback delivered.

steps.title: Schedule follow-up training for identified gaps
steps.desc: Arrange targeted training on attribution frameworks/tools where gaps were found.
steps.outcome: Training plan created where needed.

steps.title: Update CTI analyst skills baseline
steps.desc: Record drill outcomes in the ongoing CTI team capability baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92331.def: A planned exercise in which a test account or system is driven through a sequence of statistically anomalous but plausible actions (e.g., login from an unusual location, atypical data access volume, off-hours activity) to confirm the UEBA platform detects the deviation from its learned baseline.
ITID-92331.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate that the UEBA platform correctly flags deviations from an established user/entity behavior baseline.
scopeIncludes: Driving a test identity/entity through scripted anomalous-but-plausible behavior
Confirming the UEBA platform's risk score rises and an alert is generated
Validating the baseline model has sufficient historical data for the test identity
scopeExcludes: Testing for behavior specifically indicative of malicious insider intent (sibling ITID-92332)
General SIEM correlation rule testing not based on statistical baselining (covered under SIEM test ITIDs)
ITID-92331.severity: A clearly anomalous, high-deviation test action failing to raise the entity's risk score is a Critical finding; a delayed or under-weighted risk score increase is Medium; minor scoring calibration issues are Low.
ITID-92331.priority: P1 for a complete miss on a high-deviation action; P2 for delayed/under-weighted scoring; P3 for calibration tuning opportunities.
ITID-92331.escalation: Escalate to the UEBA platform owner and detection engineering lead if a high-deviation test action produces no measurable risk-score change.
indicators: Entity risk score rises measurably in response to the scripted anomalous action
Risk score fails to change despite a clearly anomalous test action
Alert generated but not routed to the SOC queue
vectors: Scripted anomalous-but-authorized actions on a test account (atypical login geography/time, unusual data-access volume) performed in a controlled manner
rootCauses: Test identity lacks sufficient baseline history for the model to detect deviation
Behavioral model thresholds tuned too loosely
Relevant telemetry (e.g., data access logs) not feeding into the UEBA platform
controls: UEBA platform configuration and baseline tuning
ITID-92331.detection: Validates the organization's ability to detect compromised-credential and insider-risk behaviors that evade purely signature-based detection.
ITID-92331.response: File a finding and tuning ticket for any missed deviation; retest after model/threshold tuning.
metrics: Percentage of scripted anomalies correctly flagged
Mean time to risk-score elevation
False-negative rate over successive test cycles
ITID-92331.notes: Use a dedicated, clearly-labeled test identity with sufficient baseline history so results are not confounded by cold-start effects.

playbook.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) Baseline Deviation Test
playbook.description: Planned exercise generating a controlled behavioral deviation to verify the UEBA platform detects the anomaly against its learned baseline.

steps.title: Define the deviation scenario and detection objective
steps.desc: Choose a specific behavioral deviation pattern (e.g. unusual login time/location, atypical data access volume) and the detection metric being validated.
steps.outcome: Scenario and objective documented and approved.

steps.title: Select a test user/entity account
steps.desc: Identify a dedicated test account with an established baseline in the UEBA platform to generate the deviation from.
steps.guidance: Do not use a real employee's live account without their knowledge and HR/legal awareness.
steps.outcome: Test account confirmed appropriate for use.

steps.title: Obtain sign-off from UEBA platform owner and privacy/HR stakeholders
steps.desc: Get written approval, including confirming the test does not raise employee-monitoring or privacy concerns.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Notify SOC of the test window
steps.desc: Advise SOC analysts the test account's anomalous activity is expected and exercise-generated.
steps.outcome: SOC acknowledges notification.

steps.title: Generate the deviation behavior on the test account
steps.desc: Perform the planned atypical action (e.g. off-hours login, bulk file access) using the test account.
steps.outcome: Deviation behavior generated as planned.

steps.title: Verify UEBA platform flags the deviation
steps.desc: Confirm whether and how quickly the platform generated a risk score increase or alert for the test account.
steps.outcome: Detection outcome and timing captured.

steps.title: Reset the test account baseline if skewed
steps.desc: Confirm the test activity doesn't permanently distort the account's behavioral baseline, resetting if needed.
steps.outcome: Test account baseline confirmed clean.

steps.title: File tuning tickets for missed or delayed detection
steps.desc: Open tickets with the UEBA platform team for any detection gap found.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened as needed.

steps.title: Update behavioral detection baseline
steps.desc: Record results in the ongoing UEBA effectiveness baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92332.def: A planned exercise simulating specific insider-threat behavior patterns (e.g., mass data staging before a resignation date, access to systems outside job function, bulk download preceding departure) to confirm the environment's controls and analytics flag the pattern as a genuine insider-risk indicator.
ITID-92332.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate detection of behavior patterns specifically associated with malicious insider activity.
scopeIncludes: Simulating known insider-threat behavior patterns on a test/authorized account
Confirming DLP, UEBA, or access-review controls flag the pattern combination
Validating that flagged cases route to the appropriate insider-threat review process
scopeExcludes: General statistical baseline-deviation testing not tied to a known insider-threat pattern (sibling ITID-92331)
External-attacker credential-compromise simulations (covered under other ITID domains)
ITID-92332.severity: A complete miss on a well-established insider-threat pattern (e.g., mass exfiltration ahead of resignation) is a Critical finding; partial detection missing key context is Medium; minor workflow-routing gaps are Low.
ITID-92332.priority: P1 for missed high-confidence insider-threat patterns; P2 for partial detection; P3 for routing/workflow gaps.
ITID-92332.escalation: Escalate to the insider-threat program lead and HR/legal liaison for any missed high-confidence pattern, given the sensitivity of insider-threat findings.
indicators: Simulated insider-threat pattern correctly flagged and routed to the insider-threat review process
Pattern combination not flagged despite matching known indicators
Flag generated but not routed to the correct review workflow
vectors: Scripted, authorized simulation of insider-threat indicator combinations (e.g., staged bulk downloads, off-hours access outside job scope) on a designated test account
rootCauses: DLP/UEBA rules not tuned to correlate multiple weak signals into a single insider-risk case
HR-triggered risk signals (e.g., resignation date) not integrated into the security analytics pipeline
Insider-threat case-routing workflow misconfigured
ITID-92332.detection: Validates detection of low-and-slow, context-dependent insider-threat patterns that single-signal detections typically miss.
ITID-92332.response: File a finding and tuning ticket for any missed pattern; retest after correlation-rule tuning; ensure findings route through the sanctioned insider-threat case process.
metrics: Percentage of simulated insider-threat patterns correctly flagged
Mean time to case creation
Percentage of cases correctly routed to insider-threat review
ITID-92332.notes: Requires HR/legal coordination and sign-off given the sensitivity of simulating insider-threat behavior, even against an authorized test account; findings must be handled with the same confidentiality as real insider-threat cases.

steps.outcome: Signed authorization from all required stakeholders on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without full sign-off.

steps.title: Execute the simulated insider-risk behavior

steps.outcome: Behavior executed as planned.

steps.title: Verify detection controls flag the activity
steps.desc: Confirm whether DLP/UEBA/insider-risk tooling generated an alert and capture timing.
steps.outcome: Detection outcome and timing captured.

steps.title: Clean up test data and confirm account state restored
steps.desc: Remove any synthetic data moved/accessed during the test and confirm the test account is returned to normal state.
steps.outcome: Test environment restored to clean state.

steps.title: File tuning tickets for detection gaps
steps.desc: Open tickets for any missed or delayed detection.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened as needed.

steps.title: Update insider-risk detection baseline
steps.desc: Record results in the ongoing insider threat detection baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-92333.purpose: Intake bucket for behavioral anomaly testing activity that does not cleanly map to a defined UEBA-baseline or insider-behavior test type.

scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-92331 (UEBA baseline) or ITID-92332 (insider behavior) once identified

ITID-93111.def: A collaborative exercise in which a red team executes attack actions in real time while an instrumented stopwatch (timestamped action log cross-referenced against SIEM/alert timestamps) captures the elapsed time between each action and its corresponding detection, if any. The exercise is run to produce a defensible mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) figure per technique, not to grade analyst judgment or response process.
ITID-93111.purpose: Captures a live-fire purple-team exercise whose primary measurement objective is detection speed: how quickly the SOC detects red-team activity as it happens, end to end from action to alert.
scopeIncludes: Timestamped correlation of red-team action logs against SIEM/EDR alert generation timestamps
Per-technique and aggregate MTTD measurement
Live, real-time execution (not tabletop or after-the-fact log review)
scopeExcludes: Grading of analyst triage quality, escalation decisions, or cross-team coordination (see Real-Time Analyst Response Coordination Exercise)
Automated, unattended technique sweeps run on a recurring schedule (see Continuous Purple Teaming leaves)
ITID-93111.severity: A technique that generates no detection at all within the exercise window is a Critical finding; a technique detected but outside the organization's target MTTD threshold is a High finding.
ITID-93111.priority: P1 remediation for any technique with zero detection where the technique targets a Tier-0/Tier-1 asset; P2 for MTTD threshold misses elsewhere.
ITID-93111.escalation: Detection engineering lead and SOC manager are notified of the MTTD scorecard immediately after the exercise; CISO is notified of any zero-detection findings against critical assets.
indicators: Consistent, precise timestamp correlation is achievable between red-team logs and SIEM alerts
Alert generated within target MTTD window for the technique class
A genuine finding: elapsed time between action and alert exceeds the documented MTTD target for that technique
vectors: Time-stamped execution of individual, discrete ATT&CK techniques (one at a time, to isolate detection latency per technique) such as credential dumping, scheduled task creation, and outbound C2 beacon simulation
rootCauses: Detection rule exists but has excessive correlation/aggregation windows that delay alert firing
Log source ingestion lag between endpoint/network sensor and SIEM
No rule exists for the technique at all
ITID-93111.detection: Directly quantifies detection speed (MTTD) per technique, distinct from whether the technique is detected at all; feeds the detection-latency dimension of the coverage scorecard.
ITID-93111.response: File a detection-engineering ticket for any technique missing its MTTD target; retest the specific technique after rule tuning or log-pipeline remediation, not the full exercise.
metrics: Mean time to detect (MTTD) per technique
Percentage of techniques detected within target MTTD
Log ingestion latency by source
sops: Live-Fire Purple Team Exercise Execution SOP
Rules of Engagement and Blast-Radius Boundary SOP
ITID-93111.notes: Requires synchronized, drift-corrected clocks between red-team tooling and the SIEM to produce a defensible MTTD figure; must not be run against production without a documented rollback plan and signed rules of engagement.

playbook.name: Live-Fire Detection Time Measurement Exercise
playbook.description: Collaborative purple team exercise measuring the time from red team technique execution to blue team detection, with the blue team aware and participating in real time.

steps.title: Select techniques to time and schedule the joint exercise session
steps.desc: Document the specific techniques to be timed for detection and schedule the joint red/blue session in advance.
steps.outcome: Technique list and joint session schedule documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed Rules of Engagement and authorization letter
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE and authorization letter covering the techniques and target environment.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Confirm blue-team advance knowledge and real-time participation
steps.desc: Confirm the blue team knows in advance and will actively monitor for detection in real time during the exercise.
steps.guidance: This is collaborative by design; the blue team's advance knowledge is the defining feature versus a covert red team test.
steps.outcome: Blue-team participants confirmed and briefed.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and techniques
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude systems outside the agreed target environment.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and session-facilitator contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the session if unintended impact occurs.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: Halt immediately on unintended production impact.

steps.title: Red team executes each technique with a synchronized timestamp
steps.desc: Execute each selected technique in sequence, recording a precise start timestamp for each.
steps.guidance: Use a shared clock/timestamp source for red and blue teams.
steps.outcome: Each technique executed with a logged start timestamp.

steps.title: Blue team detects and responds in real time; record detection timestamp
steps.desc: Blue team monitors in real time and records the timestamp at which each technique is first detected and when a response action is initiated.
steps.outcome: Detection and response timestamps recorded for each technique.

steps.title: Remove test artifacts and confirm environment integrity
steps.desc: Remove any artifacts created during technique execution and confirm the environment is restored to normal.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Calculate detection/response time metrics and route gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Calculate mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-respond per technique, and route any technique exceeding target thresholds to the remediation backlog with severity.
steps.outcome: Timing metrics calculated and remediation backlog entries created for out-of-threshold techniques.

steps.title: Hold joint red/blue debrief to close detection-timing gaps
steps.desc: Conduct a joint debrief reviewing the timing results and agreeing on detection-engineering follow-ups to reduce time-to-detect.
steps.guidance: This joint debrief is mandatory for a purple team exercise.
steps.outcome: Joint debrief held with documented action items.

ITID-93112.def: A collaborative exercise in which a red team executes attack actions in real time while observers evaluate how on-shift analysts triage the resulting alerts, escalate to senior analysts or incident commanders, and coordinate with adjacent teams (IT operations, threat intel, management), measured against the organization's documented IR escalation SLAs.
ITID-93112.purpose: Captures a live-fire purple-team exercise whose primary measurement objective is the SOC's human response workflow: triage, escalation, and cross-team coordination once an alert has fired, rather than raw detection speed.
scopeIncludes: Analyst triage-quality and escalation-path evaluation once an alert has already fired
Cross-team handoff and communication cadence during a live simulated incident
Adherence to documented escalation SLAs and on-call procedures
scopeExcludes: Raw alert-generation timing/MTTD measurement (see Live-Fire Detection Time Measurement Exercise)
Unattended, no-human-in-the-loop automated technique runs (see Continuous Purple Teaming leaves)
ITID-93112.severity: Failure to escalate a critical alert within the documented SLA is a Critical finding; an escalation that reaches the wrong team or is mis-triaged is a High finding.
ITID-93112.priority: P1 remediation for SLA breaches on Tier-0/Tier-1 asset alerts; P2 for miscommunication or handoff gaps that did not breach SLA.
ITID-93112.escalation: SOC manager and IR lead are notified of coordination-gap findings; CISO is notified if an escalation path failure would have delayed executive notification of a real major incident.
indicators: Alert triaged and escalated within documented SLA by the correct on-call role
Clear, timestamped handoff notes between shift or team boundaries
A genuine finding: alert sat untriaged past SLA, or was escalated to the wrong queue/team
vectors: Multi-stage live attack chains designed to generate a sequence of alerts across several tools (EDR, SIEM, cloud security) that require cross-tool correlation and escalation, not a single isolated technique
rootCauses: Escalation runbook is outdated or ambiguous about ownership
On-call rotation coverage gap
Alert routed to the wrong queue due to misconfigured case-management rules
Insufficient cross-team communication channels defined in advance
ITID-93112.detection: Does not measure whether a technique is detected; measures whether a detection, once it fires, is correctly acted on within process SLAs.
ITID-93112.response: File a process/runbook ticket for any SLA breach or misrouted escalation; retest the specific workflow after runbook or routing-rule updates.
metrics: Mean time to triage
Mean time to escalate
Percentage of alerts escalated to correct team/role
SLA adherence rate
sops: Live-Fire Purple Team Exercise Execution SOP
ITID-93112.notes: Best run with a mixed cast of on-shift analysts (not only senior staff) to produce a realistic measure of day-to-day response capability; requires signed rules of engagement.

steps.title: Confirm blue-team advance knowledge and real-time participation

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and techniques

steps.outcome: Coordination workflow timing and adherence documented.

steps.title: Remove test artifacts and confirm environment integrity
steps.desc: Remove any artifacts created during technique execution and confirm the environment is restored to normal.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route coordination-workflow gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record workflow gaps or delays observed with severity ratings and route to the remediation backlog.

ITID-93113.def: A live-fire red/blue exercise measuring real-time detection capability whose specific measurement focus (timing versus process) has not been determined or does not map cleanly to a defined sibling leaf.
ITID-93113.purpose: Intake bucket for real-time attack detection exercises that do not cleanly fit the detection-timing or analyst-coordination sub-categories, or that have not yet been reclassified.
scopeIncludes: Live-fire detection exercises pending classification into a specific sub-type
Exercises that blend timing and coordination objectives without a dominant focus
scopeExcludes: Exercises clearly focused on MTTD measurement (use ITID-93111)
Exercises clearly focused on analyst response coordination (use ITID-93112)
ITID-93113.severity: Apply the severity guidance of the most applicable sibling leaf once findings are categorized; treat undetected critical-asset activity as Critical pending reclassification.
ITID-93113.priority: Triage for reclassification within one review cycle; do not leave findings permanently under this catch-all code.
ITID-93113.escalation: SOC manager reviews all records filed under this code at least quarterly to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf.
indicators: Record awaiting classification triage
Exercise design did not specify a single dominant measurement objective
vectors: Varies; captured from the live-fire exercise as executed pending reclassification
rootCauses: Exercise scoping did not designate a primary objective
New exercise format not yet mapped to an existing taxonomy leaf
controls: Taxonomy governance / periodic ITID review process
ITID-93113.detection: Indeterminate until reclassified; treat as a placeholder for coverage-scorecard purposes.
ITID-93113.response: Reclassify into a specific sibling leaf as soon as the exercise's dominant objective is clear; do not use as a permanent home for findings.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
sops: ITID Taxonomy Governance and Review SOP
ITID-93113.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; SOC leadership should periodically reclassify entries into ITID-93111 or ITID-93112 rather than allowing this bucket to accumulate.

ITID-93121.def: A collaborative red/blue exercise in which the red team is granted a starting foothold on a specific workstation (e.g., credentials or an agent pre-installed on an endpoint) to test detection and response for post-compromise, host-centric activity, bypassing the need to simulate initial access.
ITID-93121.purpose: Captures a purple-team exercise that begins from a pre-positioned, already-compromised endpoint foothold rather than simulating initial access.
scopeIncludes: Testing local privilege escalation, host-based persistence, and lateral movement originating from a single compromised endpoint
Detection of endpoint-to-endpoint pivoting behavior
scopeExcludes: Exercises beginning from a compromised identity/domain account with no specific endpoint foothold (see Assumed Breach Test Starting from Compromised Domain Account)
Full kill-chain exercises that include the initial-access phase
ITID-93121.severity: A failure to detect lateral movement or privilege escalation originating from the seeded workstation within the expected window is a Critical finding.
ITID-93121.priority: P1 remediation for any missed detection of a foothold-to-domain-admin path; P2 for delayed-but-eventual detection.
ITID-93121.escalation: Escalate to security engineering leadership if the exercise reveals an undetected path from the seeded workstation to a Tier-0 asset.
indicators: No SOC alert generated despite red-team lateral movement activity from the seeded host
Alert generated but not triaged within SLA
EDR agent on the seeded host correctly flags local privilege escalation attempts
vectors: Simulated pass-the-hash and local token theft from the compromised starting workstation
Simulated local privilege escalation via known misconfiguration or unpatched vulnerability
Simulated internal reconnaissance and lateral movement toward domain controllers
rootCauses: Insufficient endpoint-to-endpoint network monitoring
EDR detection rules tuned only for external-facing initial access, not internal post-compromise activity
Local admin rights not scoped tightly enough
controls: Internal network monitoring and EDR on domain-joined endpoints
ITID-93121.detection: Directly measures detection coverage for internal/post-compromise activity originating from a single endpoint, independent of initial-access detection.
ITID-93121.response: File findings for any undetected path; retest after detection rules are tuned or endpoint hardening is applied.
metrics: Percentage of red-team actions detected
Mean time to detect from foothold to critical-asset compromise
ITID-93121.notes: Requires signed rules-of-engagement and a defined blast-radius boundary before execution; the seeded workstation must be clearly documented as non-production or isolated where possible.

ITID-93122.def: A collaborative red/blue exercise in which the red team is granted a standing set of valid domain-account credentials (e.g., a standard user or service account) to test detection and response for identity-centric abuse, credential misuse, and privilege escalation, independent of any specific compromised device.
ITID-93122.purpose: Captures a purple-team exercise that begins from a pre-positioned, already-compromised domain/identity credential rather than an endpoint foothold, to test detection of identity-centric abuse.
scopeIncludes: Testing detection of anomalous authentication patterns, credential abuse, and identity-based privilege escalation (e.g., group membership abuse, Kerberoasting) from a seeded account
Cloud/SaaS identity abuse when the seeded account has cloud access
scopeExcludes: Exercises beginning from a specific compromised endpoint with no emphasis on identity abuse (see Assumed Breach Test Starting from Compromised Workstation)
Full kill-chain exercises that include the initial-access phase
ITID-93122.severity: A failure to detect anomalous use of the seeded account (e.g., impossible-travel logins, privilege abuse) within the expected window is a Critical finding.
ITID-93122.priority: P1 remediation for any missed detection of account-to-domain-admin privilege escalation; P2 for delayed detection of lower-impact identity abuse.
ITID-93122.escalation: Escalate to identity/access management leadership and security engineering if the exercise reveals an undetected path from the seeded account to elevated privileges or sensitive data access.
indicators: No identity-provider or SIEM alert generated despite anomalous authentication behavior from the seeded account
UEBA/identity analytics correctly flags atypical access patterns
Alert generated but not triaged within SLA
vectors: Simulated Kerberoasting or AS-REP roasting against the seeded account
Simulated abuse of excessive group memberships or delegated permissions
Simulated anomalous sign-in patterns (impossible travel, atypical resource access) from the seeded credential
rootCauses: Identity/UEBA analytics not tuned to the organization's baseline behavior
Excessive standing privileges granted to the seeded account class
No conditional-access or risk-based authentication policy in place
mitreTechniques: T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
controls: Identity threat detection and response (ITDR) / UEBA
Privileged access review and least-privilege enforcement
ITID-93122.detection: Directly measures detection coverage for identity-centric, credential-based attack techniques, independent of endpoint-based detection.
ITID-93122.response: File findings for any undetected identity abuse path; retest after UEBA tuning or privilege-scoping remediation.
metrics: Percentage of identity-abuse actions detected
Mean time to detect anomalous authentication
ITID-93122.notes: Requires signed rules-of-engagement and explicit written authorization to use the seeded credential; the account must be flagged as a known test account to relevant IAM teams before execution.

ITID-93131.def: A collaborative, walkthrough-paced exercise (not a timed live-fire test) in which red-team operators narrate and demonstrate a specific attack technique action by action, while blue-team defenders explain the detection and response logic that applies at each step, with the goal of building shared understanding rather than measuring speed or grading performance.
ITID-93131.purpose: Captures a low-tempo, educational purple-team drill in which the red team demonstrates a technique step by step and the blue team explains, in real time, how the current tooling would (or would not) respond.
scopeIncludes: Slow-paced, narrated technique demonstrations with pause-and-discuss checkpoints
Knowledge-transfer sessions covering how existing detections work (or why they don't) for a given technique
scopeExcludes: Timed, unannounced live-fire exercises (see Real-Time Attack Detection Exercise leaves)
Drills specifically structured around closing a previously identified detection gap (see Detection Gap Remediation Collaborative Drill)
ITID-93131.severity: Findings from a walkthrough drill are informational/Medium by default since the exercise is educational in nature; escalate to High only if the walkthrough reveals a completely absent detection for a technique already known to be in active use by threat actors targeting the organization's sector.
ITID-93131.priority: P3 for general knowledge-transfer gaps; P2 if the walkthrough surfaces a concrete, previously unknown detection gap.
ITID-93131.escalation: Detection engineering lead is notified of any concrete gap surfaced during the walkthrough for prioritization into the backlog.
indicators: Blue team can correctly articulate, in real time, which detection would fire at each step
A genuine finding: blue team cannot explain expected detection behavior for a step, indicating a documentation or tooling gap
vectors: Any single ATT&CK technique selected for the session, demonstrated in a controlled, narrated, stepwise fashion (e.g., a specific persistence mechanism or defense-evasion trick)
rootCauses: Detection logic exists but is undocumented, so analysts cannot articulate it
Analysts have not previously been exposed to the technique being demonstrated
Detection content and analyst training materials are out of sync
mitreTechniques: T1547 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
ITID-93131.detection: Surfaces gaps in analyst understanding of existing detections and in detection-logic documentation, rather than raw technical detection coverage.
ITID-93131.response: Update analyst-facing detection documentation and training materials for any gap surfaced; escalate genuine technical detection gaps to detection engineering for rule creation.
metrics: Number of techniques covered per quarter
Number of documentation gaps closed following walkthroughs
sops: Adversarial Tactics and Defense Drill Facilitation SOP
ITID-93131.notes: Low blast-radius by design since pace is controlled and narrated; still requires a documented scope agreement even though formal rules-of-engagement sign-off may be lighter-weight than a live-fire exercise.

steps.outcome: Technique executed step by step with joint observation completed.

ITID-93132.def: A follow-up collaborative exercise, scoped to a single previously identified detection gap, in which the red team re-executes the same technique that originally went undetected after the blue team has tuned or created a detection rule, to confirm closure of the gap before it is marked resolved.
ITID-93132.purpose: Captures a targeted collaborative drill run specifically to confirm that a previously identified detection gap has been closed, by having the red team repeat the exact technique after blue-team remediation.
scopeIncludes: Retesting of a single, specific, previously documented finding
Confirmation that a newly created or tuned detection rule fires as expected
scopeExcludes: First-pass, exploratory demonstrations of a technique not tied to a prior finding (see Joint Red/Blue Technique Walkthrough Drill)
Broad-scope live-fire exercises covering many techniques at once
ITID-93132.severity: If the retest shows the gap is still open, treat it at the same severity as the original finding, escalated one level due to the missed remediation deadline.
ITID-93132.priority: P1 for any confirmed-still-open gap on a Tier-0/Tier-1 asset finding; otherwise inherits the priority of the original finding.
ITID-93132.escalation: Detection engineering lead and the finding owner are notified of the retest result; CISO is notified if a Critical finding fails retest.
indicators: New/tuned detection rule fires correctly on retest, confirming closure
A genuine finding: the rule still does not fire, or fires with unacceptable delay, indicating incomplete remediation
vectors: The exact technique and execution path from the original finding, replayed as closely as possible to ensure a valid comparison
rootCauses: Detection rule was tuned for a narrower condition than the actual technique variant used
Rule was deployed to the wrong log source or sensor scope
Remediation ticket was closed without an actual retest
ITID-93132.detection: Directly confirms (or refutes) closure of a specific previously identified coverage gap.
ITID-93132.response: Mark the finding formally closed only after a successful retest; reopen and re-escalate if the retest fails.
metrics: Gap closure confirmation rate on first retest
Mean time from finding to confirmed closure
sops: Detection Gap Remediation and Retest SOP
ITID-93132.notes: Should be scheduled promptly after remediation is reported complete; delayed retesting undermines the finding-closure metric.

ITID-93211.def: An automated exercise in which a BAS platform executes a fixed, pre-approved library of attack-simulation modules against production or production-representative infrastructure on a defined recurring schedule (e.g., weekly, monthly), with results reviewed by detection engineering rather than orchestrated live by a human red-team operator.
ITID-93211.purpose: Captures a recurring, scheduled, unattended run of a commercial or open-source breach-and-attack-simulation (BAS) platform against a fixed library of techniques, used to establish a stable, repeatable coverage baseline.
scopeIncludes: Recurring, schedule-driven BAS platform runs against a stable, agreed technique library
Automated pass/fail scoring of each simulation module against existing detections
scopeExcludes: Rotating or expanding technique sets designed to broaden coverage over time (see Continuous Automated ATT&CK Technique Rotation Test)
Human-operated, improvisational red-team exercises
ITID-93211.severity: A technique module that fails to trigger any detection on two or more consecutive scheduled runs is a Critical finding, since it indicates a persistent, unaddressed gap rather than a transient anomaly.
ITID-93211.priority: P1 for persistent gaps against Tier-0/Tier-1 assets; P2 for a single-run failure pending confirmation on the next scheduled run.
ITID-93211.escalation: Detection engineering is notified automatically via the BAS platform's alerting integration for any failed module; SOC manager receives the aggregate scorecard after each run.
indicators: Scheduled run completes and produces a full pass/fail scorecard across the fixed technique library
A genuine finding: a module that previously passed now fails, indicating detection drift or an environment change
vectors: N/A — this is not itself an attack vector description; rather, it describes technique/method breadth

The platform executes a curated, fixed library of safe-simulation modules spanning common ATT&CK techniques such as credential dumping simulation, C2 beacon simulation, and data exfiltration simulation
rootCauses: Detection rule regression following a SIEM/EDR platform update
Log source stopped forwarding due to an infrastructure change
BAS module simulation no longer matches the real-world technique signature after a vendor tooling update
ITID-93211.detection: Establishes a stable, repeatable baseline of detection coverage across a fixed technique set, and highlights detection drift over time (a technique that used to be detected but no longer is).
ITID-93211.response: Investigate and remediate any failed module before the next scheduled run; file a detection-engineering ticket for persistent failures.
metrics: Percentage of BAS modules passing per run
Detection-drift rate (previously-passing modules that now fail)
Mean time to remediate a failed module
sops: BAS Platform Operations and Maintenance SOP
ITID-93211.notes: Must be run against a documented, approved environment scope with safe-simulation modules only (no live malware); BAS platform credentials and agents require the same change-control rigor as any production tooling.

playbook.name: Scheduled Automated Breach-and-Attack-Simulation (BAS) Platform Run
playbook.description: Automated, platform-driven purple teaming run executing a scheduled library of adversary techniques via a BAS tool, tracked over time via scorecard trending.

steps.title: Define the technique library and run schedule
steps.desc: Document the BAS platform's configured technique library scope and the recurring run schedule (e.g. weekly automated run).
steps.outcome: Technique library scope and schedule documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed authorization for standing automated execution
steps.desc: Secure standing authorization from the CISO/sponsor covering the BAS platform's ongoing, recurring execution against the target environment.
steps.guidance: Because this runs on a schedule rather than as a one-off, authorization should explicitly cover the recurring nature.
steps.outcome: Signed standing authorization on file before the schedule is activated.
steps.abort: Do not activate the schedule without standing authorization.

steps.title: Confirm SOC awareness of the automated schedule
steps.desc: Confirm the SOC is aware the BAS platform runs on a recurring schedule so its alerts are not mistaken for a real incident.
steps.outcome: SOC awareness confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Configure platform safety limits and out-of-scope exclusions
steps.desc: Configure the BAS platform's exclusion list for out-of-scope hosts/segments and confirm technique safety settings (non-destructive mode).
steps.outcome: Platform configuration confirmed to exclude out-of-scope systems and use safe technique variants.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop for the automated schedule
steps.desc: Confirm an administrator can immediately pause or disable the scheduled run if it causes unexpected impact.
steps.outcome: Schedule pause/disable capability tested and confirmed.
steps.abort: Disable the schedule immediately if unexpected production impact occurs.

steps.title: Execute the scheduled automated technique run
steps.desc: Allow the BAS platform to execute its configured technique library against the target environment per schedule.
steps.outcome: Scheduled run completed with results captured by the platform.

steps.title: Review automated detection/prevention scoring for the run
steps.desc: Review the platform's automated scoring of which techniques were detected, prevented, or missed by existing controls.
steps.outcome: Run-level detection/prevention scorecard reviewed.

steps.title: Confirm platform cleanup of any run artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm the BAS platform automatically cleaned up any test artifacts left on target systems after the run.
steps.outcome: Target systems confirmed clean of run artifacts.

steps.title: Route missed-technique findings into remediation backlog and update trend scorecard
steps.desc: Record missed/uncontrolled techniques into the remediation backlog with severity, and update the running trend scorecard rather than a one-off report.
steps.guidance: Continuous purple teaming value comes from trend tracking across runs, not a single after-action report.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created and trend scorecard updated for this run.

steps.title: Review trend scorecard movement and brief stakeholders periodically
steps.desc: Periodically review the trend scorecard's movement across recent runs (improving/degrading control coverage) and brief the CISO/sponsor, rather than producing a single after-action report per run.
steps.outcome: Periodic trend briefing delivered to stakeholders.

ITID-93212.def: An automated exercise in which the set of techniques tested is intentionally rotated, expanded, or reprioritized on each run (e.g., cycling through the full ATT&CK matrix over a quarter, or weighting toward newly published techniques) rather than executing a static fixed library, so that over time the exercise validates detection coverage across a rotating set of ATT&CK techniques spanning multiple tactics.
ITID-93212.purpose: Captures a continuous automated exercise that deliberately rotates through an expanding or shifting subset of ATT&CK techniques over time, in order to broaden detection-coverage measurement beyond a fixed baseline library.
scopeIncludes: Automated runs where the technique set changes run-over-run by design
Coverage-breadth tracking across the full ATT&CK matrix over a defined time horizon (e.g., quarterly full-matrix coverage)
scopeExcludes: Runs against a fixed, unchanging technique library on a recurring schedule (see Scheduled Automated BAS Platform Run)
Human-operated, improvisational red-team exercises
ITID-93212.severity: A newly rotated-in technique with no corresponding detection is a Medium-to-High finding depending on the technique's prevalence in current threat intelligence; a previously-covered technique that regresses on re-rotation is a Critical finding.
ITID-93212.priority: P1 for regressions on Tier-0/Tier-1-relevant techniques; P2 for net-new coverage gaps surfaced by rotation.
ITID-93212.escalation: Detection engineering receives the rotation results automatically; threat intelligence team is looped in when a rotated-in technique corresponds to an active, in-the-wild campaign relevant to the organization's sector.
indicators: Cumulative ATT&CK matrix coverage percentage increases over successive rotation cycles
A genuine finding: a technique newly rotated into the cycle produces no detection
vectors: N/A — describes technique/method breadth, not a single vector
A rotating, expanding set of simulation modules spanning multiple tactics, prioritized using current threat-intelligence prevalence data, cycling to eventually cover the full applicable ATT&CK matrix
rootCauses: Detection content roadmap has not kept pace with the rotating technique set
Newly published ATT&CK techniques lack corresponding detection engineering effort
Coverage prioritization was not weighted against the organization's actual threat profile
controls: Detection engineering roadmap prioritized by threat intelligence
ITID-93212.detection: Explicitly measures and grows breadth of ATT&CK matrix coverage over time; the key output is a cumulative coverage-percentage trendline, not a single-run pass/fail.
ITID-93212.response: Feed rotation results into the detection engineering backlog, prioritized by threat-intelligence relevance; retest a technique on its next scheduled rotation after remediation.
metrics: Cumulative percentage of ATT&CK techniques with validated detection coverage
Coverage growth rate per quarter
Regression rate on re-rotated techniques
sops: BAS Platform Operations and Maintenance SOP
ITID-93212.notes: Rotation schedule and prioritization logic should be reviewed at least annually against updated threat-intelligence priorities; must be run only against approved scope with safe-simulation modules.

steps.outcome: Technique rotation set and schedule documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed authorization for standing automated execution

steps.outcome: Signed standing authorization on file before the schedule is activated.

steps.outcome: Schedule pause/disable capability tested and confirmed.

steps.outcome: Cycle-level detection/prevention scorecard reviewed.

steps.desc: Confirm the platform automatically cleaned up any test artifacts left on target systems after the cycle.
steps.outcome: Target systems confirmed clean of run artifacts.

steps.title: Route missed-technique findings into remediation backlog and update coverage trend
steps.desc: Record missed/uncontrolled techniques into the remediation backlog with severity, and update the rotating coverage trend across cycles.

ITID-93213.def: An automated BAS/emulation exercise whose technique-selection model (fixed library versus rotating set) has not been determined or does not map cleanly to a defined sibling leaf.
ITID-93213.purpose: Intake bucket for automated adversary emulation runs that do not cleanly fit the fixed-schedule or rotating-technique sub-categories, or that have not yet been reclassified.
scopeIncludes: Automated emulation runs pending classification into a specific sub-type
scopeExcludes: Runs clearly using a fixed, static technique library on a schedule (use ITID-93211)
Runs clearly using a rotating/expanding technique set (use ITID-93212)
ITID-93213.severity: Apply the severity guidance of the most applicable sibling leaf once findings are categorized.
ITID-93213.priority: Triage for reclassification within one review cycle; do not leave findings permanently under this catch-all code.
ITID-93213.escalation: SOC manager reviews all records filed under this code at least quarterly to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf.
indicators: Record awaiting classification triage
vectors: Varies; captured from the run as executed pending reclassification
rootCauses: Run configuration did not clearly indicate a fixed versus rotating technique model
New BAS platform integration not yet mapped to an existing taxonomy leaf
controls: Taxonomy governance / periodic ITID review process
ITID-93213.detection: Indeterminate until reclassified; treat as a placeholder for coverage-scorecard purposes.
ITID-93213.response: Reclassify into a specific sibling leaf as soon as the run's technique-selection model is clear.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
sops: ITID Taxonomy Governance and Review SOP
ITID-93213.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; SOC leadership should periodically reclassify entries into ITID-93211 or ITID-93212 rather than allowing this bucket to accumulate.
