ITID-93221.def: A controlled test in which synthetic indicator data (e.g., a fabricated malicious hash, IP, or domain matching a known detection rule's pattern) is injected directly into production log streams or the SIEM ingestion pipeline, to validate that the alerting pipeline — from log ingestion through rule match, alert generation, case creation, and notification — functions correctly in production, independent of whether a real endpoint or network action occurred.
ITID-93221.purpose: Captures a live threat-injection test in which synthetic malicious indicators (e.g., benign IOCs formatted as real threat data) are inserted directly into the production monitoring/SIEM data pipeline to validate that alerting, correlation, and case-management processes function end to end, without any actual attack behavior on endpoints or networks.
scopeIncludes: Direct injection of synthetic indicator/log data into the production SIEM or log pipeline
End-to-end validation of alert generation, case creation, and notification plumbing
scopeExcludes: Injection of actual simulated network/endpoint traffic that traverses real sensors (see Synthetic Attack Traffic Injection Test)
Any exercise involving live, human-operated red-team actions
ITID-93221.severity: Failure of the injected synthetic indicator to produce an alert, case, or notification through the full pipeline is a Critical finding, since it indicates a break in production alerting plumbing that would silently suppress real alerts.
ITID-93221.priority: P1 for any full pipeline break (no alert/case/notification at all); P2 for partial breaks (e.g., alert fires but case creation or notification fails).
ITID-93221.escalation: SOC manager and detection engineering lead are notified immediately of any pipeline break, since a silent failure here means real detections may also be silently failing.
indicators: Synthetic indicator correctly triggers a rule match, alert, case, and notification end to end

A genuine finding: the indicator matches the rule logic but no alert, case, or notification is produced, indicating a plumbing failure (e.g., broken SOAR integration, misconfigured notification channel)
vectors: N/A — this test injects synthetic indicator data rather than performing any attack action; it validates pipeline plumbing, not attacker tradecraft
rootCauses: SOAR/case-management integration silently failed after a platform update
Notification channel (email/paging/chat webhook) misconfigured or expired credential
Detection rule logic drifted from the tested indicator pattern
ITID-93221.detection: Does not measure adversary-technique detection coverage; measures the health and reliability of the alerting/notification pipeline itself, a prerequisite for any detection to matter operationally.
ITID-93221.response: Treat any pipeline break as an operational incident requiring immediate fix, since it may be masking real missed detections; retest after the fix to confirm end-to-end plumbing health.
metrics: Pipeline end-to-end success rate
Mean time to detect a pipeline break
Mean time to remediate a pipeline break
ITID-93221.notes: Must use clearly-tagged synthetic indicators that cannot be mistaken for a real threat by downstream consumers (e.g., threat-intel sharing platforms); requires coordination with SOC leadership to avoid false alarm fatigue among on-call analysts.

playbook.name: Live Malicious Indicator Injection into Production Monitoring
playbook.description: Automated exercise injecting synthetic malicious indicators (IOCs) directly into production monitoring pipelines to validate alerting without touching live systems.

steps.title: Define the indicator set and injection points
steps.desc: Document the synthetic malicious indicators (e.g. known-bad IPs, hashes, domains) to be injected and the monitoring pipeline points where they will be introduced.
steps.outcome: Indicator set and injection points documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed authorization for injection into production monitoring
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE/authorization letter explicitly covering injection into the production monitoring pipeline, given the sensitivity of touching live monitoring infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned authorization.

steps.title: Confirm SOC awareness of the injection exercise
steps.desc: Confirm the SOC is aware that synthetic indicators will be injected so alerts are not mistaken for a real incident, or deliberately kept unaware to test triage rigor.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Confirm indicators are clearly tagged as synthetic and isolated from real telemetry paths
steps.desc: Explicitly confirm the injected indicators are tagged (e.g. a test marker field) so they cannot be confused with genuine threat intel, and cannot trigger real automated blocking actions against production traffic.
steps.outcome: Written confirmation that injected data cannot trigger real automated response actions.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop and monitoring-team contact channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the injection and purge indicators if they begin to affect real detection/response automation.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If the injected indicators trigger a real automated block or a real incident ticket, halt and purge immediately.

steps.title: Inject the synthetic indicators into the monitoring pipeline
steps.desc: Introduce the tagged synthetic indicators into the defined injection points within the production monitoring pipeline.
steps.outcome: Indicators injected and logged with timestamps.

steps.title: Monitor whether alerting/triage correctly surfaces the injected indicators
steps.desc: Track whether the SOC's alerting and triage workflow correctly surfaces and investigates the injected indicators.
steps.outcome: Alerting/triage response documented for each injected indicator.

steps.title: Purge synthetic indicators from all monitoring systems
steps.desc: Remove the injected synthetic indicators from all monitoring systems and confirm no residual test data remains.
steps.outcome: Synthetic indicators confirmed purged from all systems.

steps.title: Route alerting/triage gaps into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record alerting or triage gaps observed with severity ratings and route to the remediation backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per gap.

steps.title: Produce findings summary and brief stakeholders
steps.desc: Publish a summary of alerting/triage effectiveness and brief the SOC lead/CISO.
steps.outcome: Findings summary delivered and briefing completed.

ITID-93222.def: A controlled test in which synthetic attack traffic (e.g., simulated C2 beacon patterns, scan traffic, or malicious file execution in a sandboxed context) is generated and allowed to traverse real network and endpoint sensors, to validate that the sensors themselves detect and forward the activity correctly, complementing pipeline-plumbing tests by validating sensor-level detection.
ITID-93222.purpose: Captures a live threat-injection test in which simulated malicious network or endpoint traffic is actually generated and sent through real sensors (network taps, EDR agents), rather than injecting indicator data directly into the SIEM, to validate that sensors themselves correctly observe and report the activity.
scopeIncludes: Generation of synthetic-but-real traffic/activity observed by live network or endpoint sensors
Validation of sensor-level detection logic (not just downstream pipeline plumbing)
scopeExcludes: Direct injection of fabricated indicator data into the SIEM without any real sensor observation (see Live Malicious Indicator Injection into Production Monitoring)
Full human-operated red-team exercises with objective-driven attack chains
ITID-93222.severity: A sensor's failure to observe and forward synthetic malicious traffic that matches its documented detection capability is a Critical finding.
ITID-93222.priority: P1 for sensor blind spots on network segments or endpoint populations covering Tier-0/Tier-1 assets; P2 elsewhere.
ITID-93222.escalation: Detection engineering and infrastructure/network teams are notified of any sensor blind spot; SOC manager receives the aggregate sensor-health report.
indicators: Synthetic traffic is correctly observed, parsed, and forwarded by the relevant network/endpoint sensor
A genuine finding: traffic traverses the sensor's coverage zone but is not observed or logged, indicating a sensor placement or configuration gap
vectors: Simulated C2 beacon and DNS tunneling traffic patterns
Simulated port-scan and network reconnaissance traffic
Simulated malicious file execution in a sandboxed/contained context to test EDR observation
rootCauses: Network sensor (e.g., NDR/IDS) has a coverage gap on a specific segment or VLAN
EDR agent not deployed or misconfigured on a subset of endpoints
TLS/encrypted traffic inspection gap preventing payload-level detection
controls: Network detection and response (NDR) sensor placement
ITID-93222.detection: Directly measures sensor-level observation coverage (as opposed to pipeline plumbing or human-analyst response), identifying physical/logical blind spots in sensor deployment.
ITID-93222.response: File a sensor-deployment or configuration ticket for any blind spot; retest after sensor coverage is extended or reconfigured.
metrics: Percentage of network segments with confirmed sensor coverage
Percentage of endpoints with confirmed EDR observation
Mean time to remediate a sensor blind spot
ITID-93222.notes: Synthetic traffic must be generated using contained, non-destructive methods and clearly tagged/documented in advance to avoid triggering an unnecessary real incident response; requires coordination with network and endpoint teams.

ITID-93223.purpose: Intake bucket for live threat injection tests that do not cleanly fit the pipeline-injection or sensor-traffic sub-categories, or that have not yet been reclassified.

ITID-93231.def: An ad hoc, threat-intelligence-driven exercise validating whether existing detective and preventive controls are effective against a specific emerging technique — for example, one newly observed in an active campaign targeting the organization's sector or a technique enabled by a newly disclosed vulnerability — run outside the normal rotation cadence due to urgency.
ITID-93231.purpose: Captures a targeted validation exercise run specifically because a new or emerging attack technique (surfaced via threat intelligence) needs an urgent, out-of-cycle check against current controls, rather than as part of a routine rotation.
scopeIncludes: Out-of-cycle, urgency-driven validation of a single emerging technique tied to current threat intelligence
Rapid-turnaround control-effectiveness assessment ahead of the next scheduled rotation cycle
scopeExcludes: Routine, cadence-driven scorecard validation across the broader control set (see Continuous Security Posture Scorecard Validation)
Techniques already covered by the standard rotation schedule with no particular urgency
ITID-93231.severity: No detection or prevention capability against an actively-exploited emerging technique relevant to the organization's sector is a Critical finding requiring expedited remediation.
ITID-93231.priority: P1 for any emerging technique tied to an active campaign against the organization's sector with no coverage; P2 for emerging techniques with partial coverage.
ITID-93231.escalation: CISO and threat intelligence lead are notified immediately of any Critical finding, given the active-threat context driving the test.
indicators: Control or detection correctly identifies/blocks the emerging technique when tested
A genuine finding: the emerging technique bypasses current controls entirely
vectors: The specific emerging technique or exploit chain identified in current threat intelligence, simulated as closely as safely possible to the observed real-world variant
rootCauses: Detection content has not yet been created for a newly disclosed technique
Preventive control (e.g., patch, WAF rule) not yet deployed for a newly disclosed vulnerability
Threat-intel-to-detection-engineering feedback loop is too slow
controls: Threat intelligence ingestion and prioritization process
Expedited detection-engineering/patch pipeline for emerging threats
ITID-93231.detection: Provides a rapid, point-in-time answer to whether the organization has coverage against a specific, currently relevant emerging technique.
ITID-93231.response: Expedite detection-content or patch deployment for any gap found; retest as soon as remediation is deployed given the active-threat context.
metrics: Time from threat-intel alert to control validation test
Percentage of emerging techniques with confirmed coverage within SLA
ITID-93231.notes: Run under expedited approval given the time-sensitive nature; must still follow a lightweight documented scope agreement to avoid unauthorized testing against production.

playbook.name: Control Effectiveness Validation Against Emerging Threat Technique
playbook.description: Automated/platform-driven purple teaming run validating existing controls against a newly published or emerging adversary technique.

steps.title: Identify the emerging technique and controls to validate
steps.desc: Document the newly published/emerging ATT&CK technique (e.g. from recent threat intel) and the specific controls expected to defend against it.
steps.outcome: Technique and control-validation basis documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed authorization for the validation run
steps.desc: Secure a signed RoE/authorization letter covering the technique and target environment.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file before execution.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned authorization.

steps.title: Confirm SOC advance notification decision
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC is notified in advance or kept unaware to test genuine readiness against the emerging technique.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems and safe technique variant
steps.desc: Explicitly exclude systems outside the agreed target environment and confirm a non-destructive variant of the emerging technique is used.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list and safe-variant confirmation appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop channel
steps.desc: Set up an abort channel to halt the run if unintended impact occurs.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: Halt immediately on unintended production impact.

steps.title: Execute the emerging technique against the target environment
steps.desc: Execute the emerging technique's proof-of-concept variant against the target environment.
steps.outcome: Technique executed and logged.

steps.title: Validate whether existing controls detect or prevent the technique
steps.desc: Assess whether the expected controls detected or prevented the technique as designed.
steps.outcome: Control effectiveness outcome documented (effective/ineffective).

steps.title: Remove test artifacts and confirm environment integrity
steps.desc: Remove any artifacts created during execution and confirm the environment is restored to normal.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of test artifacts.

steps.title: Route control gaps into remediation backlog and update coverage trend
steps.desc: Record any control gap found with severity and update the running control-coverage trend against emerging techniques.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created and coverage trend updated.

steps.title: Brief stakeholders on emerging-threat readiness
steps.desc: Brief the CISO/sponsor on the organization's readiness against the emerging technique and recommended control updates.
steps.outcome: Briefing completed with documented recommendations.

ITID-93232.def: A recurring, scheduled exercise that validates and refreshes the organization's overall security-posture scorecard by aggregating results from purple-team and BAS activity across the full monitored control set, producing a trended, board-reportable posture score over time.
ITID-93232.purpose: Captures the routine, cadence-driven validation of the organization's overall security posture scorecard — an aggregate, recurring assessment across the full control set rather than a single urgent technique.
scopeIncludes: Aggregation and validation of scorecard inputs across all purple-team/BAS activity for the review period
Trend analysis of posture score over successive review cycles
scopeExcludes: Single-technique, urgency-driven ad hoc validation tied to specific threat intelligence (see Control Effectiveness Validation Against Emerging Threat Technique)
Raw execution of individual exercises (this leaf validates the scorecard produced from them, not the underlying exercises themselves)
ITID-93232.severity: A quarter-over-quarter decline in the aggregate posture score, or any control category falling below its defined minimum threshold, is a Critical finding requiring executive-level review.
ITID-93232.priority: P1 for scorecard categories below minimum threshold on Tier-0/Tier-1-relevant controls; P2 for declining trends not yet below threshold.
ITID-93232.escalation: CISO and executive leadership receive the posture scorecard each review cycle; board-level reporting occurs at the cadence defined by governance policy.
indicators: Scorecard is successfully compiled from complete, valid underlying exercise data for the review period
A genuine finding: a category score declines or a data source is missing/stale, undermining scorecard validity
vectors: N/A — this leaf aggregates and validates results across many prior exercises rather than executing a new attack simulation itself
rootCauses: Underlying exercise data incomplete due to a missed scheduled run
Scorecard weighting/methodology not updated to reflect current threat priorities
Control category genuinely regressed due to infrastructure or process change
controls: Security posture scorecard methodology and governance
Aggregate reporting pipeline across purple-team/BAS data sources
ITID-93232.detection: Provides an aggregate, trended view of overall detection and control coverage across the organization, built from the results of the underlying purple-team exercise leaves.
ITID-93232.response: Investigate any missing or stale data source before publishing the scorecard; drive remediation of any declining category through the standard detection-engineering/control-owner backlog.
metrics: Aggregate security posture score
Quarter-over-quarter trend by control category
Percentage of scorecard inputs sourced from complete, on-schedule exercise data
sops: Security Posture Scorecard Methodology and Governance SOP
ITID-93232.notes: Scorecard methodology should be reviewed and, if needed, recalibrated at least annually to remain aligned with current threat priorities and control inventory.

playbook.name: Continuous Security Posture Scorecard Validation
playbook.description: Automated, platform-driven purple teaming run validating and updating a continuous security posture scorecard against a broad control set.

steps.title: Define the scorecard control set and validation schedule

steps.outcome: Control set and schedule documented.

steps.title: Obtain signed authorization for standing automated execution

steps.outcome: Signed standing authorization on file before the schedule is activated.
steps.abort: Do not activate the schedule without standing authorization.

steps.title: Confirm SOC awareness of the automated schedule
steps.desc: Confirm the SOC is aware of the recurring schedule so its alerts are not mistaken for a real incident.
steps.outcome: SOC awareness confirmed and documented.

steps.title: Configure platform safety limits and out-of-scope exclusions
steps.desc: Configure the platform's exclusion list for out-of-scope hosts/segments and confirm non-destructive technique variants are used.
steps.outcome: Platform configuration confirmed to exclude out-of-scope systems and use safe technique variants.

steps.title: Establish emergency stop for the scorecard validation schedule
steps.desc: Confirm an administrator can immediately pause or disable the scheduled validation run if it causes unexpected impact.
steps.outcome: Schedule pause/disable capability tested and confirmed.
steps.abort: Disable the schedule immediately if unexpected production impact occurs.

steps.title: Execute the scheduled control-set validation run
steps.desc: Allow the platform to execute the full control-set validation against the target environment.
steps.outcome: Scheduled run completed with results captured.

steps.title: Compute updated posture scorecard from run results
steps.desc: Compute the updated security posture score from this run's detection/prevention results.
steps.outcome: Updated posture scorecard computed.

steps.title: Confirm platform cleanup of any run artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm the platform automatically cleaned up any test artifacts left on target systems.
steps.outcome: Target systems confirmed clean of run artifacts.

steps.title: Route scorecard regressions into remediation backlog
steps.desc: Record any control that regressed or remained weak in the scorecard, with severity, and route to the remediation backlog.
steps.outcome: Remediation backlog entries created per regression.

steps.title: Review scorecard trend movement and brief stakeholders periodically
steps.desc: Periodically review the posture scorecard's trend across recent runs and brief the CISO/sponsor.
steps.outcome: Periodic trend briefing delivered to stakeholders.

ITID-93233.def: A defense strategy validation exercise whose driver (urgent emerging-threat check versus routine scorecard cadence) has not been determined or does not map cleanly to a defined sibling leaf.
ITID-93233.purpose: Intake bucket for defense strategy validation activity that does not cleanly fit the emerging-threat or posture-scorecard sub-categories, or that has not yet been reclassified.
scopeIncludes: Validation activity pending classification into a specific sub-type
scopeExcludes: Activity clearly driven by an urgent emerging-threat check (use ITID-93231)
Activity clearly part of the routine posture-scorecard cadence (use ITID-93232)

ITID-93233.priority: Triage for reclassification within one review cycle; do not leave findings permanently under this catch-all code.
ITID-93233.escalation: SOC manager reviews all records filed under this code at least quarterly to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf.

New validation format not yet mapped to an existing taxonomy leaf
controls: Taxonomy governance / periodic ITID review process
ITID-93233.detection: Indeterminate until reclassified; treat as a placeholder for coverage-scorecard purposes.
ITID-93233.response: Reclassify into a specific sibling leaf as soon as the activity's dominant driver is clear.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
sops: ITID Taxonomy Governance and Review SOP
ITID-93233.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; SOC leadership should periodically reclassify entries into ITID-93231 or ITID-93232 rather than allowing this bucket to accumulate.

steps.title: Review detection/prevention results

steps.outcome: Results reviewed and documented.

steps.title: Confirm platform cleanup of any run artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm the platform automatically cleaned up any test artifacts left on target systems.
steps.outcome: Target systems confirmed clean of run artifacts.

steps.title: Route gaps into remediation backlog and update trend
steps.desc: Record gaps found with severity and update the running trend.

ITID-94111.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers are provisioned with valid application credentials at one or more privilege levels to systematically assess the application for vulnerabilities reachable only from an authenticated session, such as broken access control, session management flaws, and privilege escalation within the app.
ITID-94111.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test of a web application performed with valid, provisioned user credentials to assess vulnerabilities exploitable by an authenticated user or account-compromise scenario.
scopeIncludes: Testing from the perspective of one or more authenticated user roles
Assessment of access-control enforcement between roles/tenants
Session management and authenticated-workflow testing
scopeExcludes: Testing performed with no credentials/from an anonymous perspective (Unauthenticated/Black-Box leaf)
ITID-94111.severity: Any confirmed vertical or horizontal privilege escalation, or cross-tenant data access, from an authenticated low-privilege session is a Critical finding.
ITID-94111.priority: P1 for confirmed privilege escalation or cross-tenant access; P2 for session-management flaws without direct data exposure.
ITID-94111.escalation: Escalate to the Application Owner and CISO for any confirmed privilege escalation or cross-tenant/cross-user data exposure.
indicators: Successful access to functionality or data reserved for a higher privilege role
Successful access to another tenant's/user's data while authenticated as a standard user
Session tokens not properly invalidated or predictable
vectors: Manipulation of role/permission parameters within an authenticated session
Testing of object-level authorization across authenticated user contexts
Session-fixation or token-predictability testing
rootCauses: Authorization checks not consistently enforced server-side for every role/tenant boundary
Session management not following secure token generation/invalidation practices
Insufficient testing of authenticated workflows during the development lifecycle
ITID-94111.detection: Measures vulnerabilities reachable specifically from an authenticated attacker or compromised-account perspective, complementing black-box external testing.
ITID-94111.response: File findings by severity for developer remediation with defined SLAs; retest after fixes; feed findings into the SDLC.
metrics: Number of critical/high findings per assessment
Percentage of findings remediated within SLA
Repeat-finding rate across assessment cycles
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
Web Application Penetration Test Methodology SOP
ITID-94111.notes: Requires dedicated test accounts provisioned at each role/privilege level being tested; must not use real customer/employee credentials.

playbook.name: Authenticated Web Application Penetration Test
playbook.description: Formal authenticated (grey-box) penetration test of a web application, delivering a technical findings report with severity ratings.

steps.title: Define scope and obtain signed authorization/Rules of Engagement
steps.desc: Document the target application, URLs, and functionality in scope, the authenticated test account roles to be used, and secure a signed RoE and authorization letter.
steps.guidance: This is a hard legal requirement for a real pentest and must always be completed before testing begins.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file naming the application and test account roles.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Provision dedicated test accounts for each role to be tested
steps.desc: Provision dedicated test accounts covering each privilege role required for authenticated testing (e.g. standard user, admin).
steps.guidance: Never use a real employee's live account.
steps.outcome: Dedicated test accounts provisioned per role.

steps.title: Decide SOC/application-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/application owner is notified in advance or kept unaware.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope systems/techniques and emergency-contact protocol
steps.desc: Explicitly define systems/techniques out of scope (e.g. denial-of-service testing, third-party integrations) and establish an emergency-contact/stop-work protocol.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list and emergency-contact protocol appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Test the emergency stop-work channel
steps.desc: Verify the emergency-contact channel is reachable before testing begins.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If production impact occurs, halt immediately via the stop-work protocol.

steps.title: Perform authenticated technical testing across the OWASP-aligned test methodology
steps.desc: Execute authenticated testing (e.g. injection, broken access control, session management, business logic) against the application using each provisioned test role.
steps.guidance: Follow a recognized methodology (e.g. OWASP Testing Guide/ASVS).
steps.outcome: Full test methodology executed with findings documented per test case.

steps.title: Validate and exploit confirmed vulnerabilities to demonstrate impact
steps.desc: Where a vulnerability is confirmed, demonstrate impact via a controlled proof-of-concept.
steps.outcome: Confirmed vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept evidence.

steps.title: Clean up test accounts and artifacts created during testing
steps.desc: Remove or disable the dedicated test accounts and any test data/artifacts created in the application.
steps.outcome: Test accounts and artifacts removed; application confirmed clean.

steps.title: Deliver technical findings report with CVSS-style severity ratings
steps.desc: Publish a technical findings report detailing each vulnerability with a CVSS-style severity rating and remediation guidance.
steps.outcome: Findings report delivered with severity ratings per finding.

steps.title: Hand off findings to vulnerability-management for remediation tracking
steps.desc: Route each finding into the vulnerability-management/remediation-tracking process with an owner and due date, and brief the application owner/CISO.
steps.outcome: Remediation tracking handoff completed and briefing delivered.

ITID-94112.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers approach the application with no provisioned credentials or internal documentation, systematically probing the externally reachable attack surface to identify vulnerabilities exploitable without any prior access.
ITID-94112.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test of a web application performed with no prior credentials or internal knowledge, to assess the externally exposed attack surface as a genuine external attacker would encounter it.
scopeIncludes: Testing from an anonymous/unauthenticated external perspective
Enumeration of the externally reachable application attack surface
Testing of pre-authentication functionality (registration, password reset, login)
scopeExcludes: Testing performed with provisioned application credentials (Authenticated leaf)
ITID-94112.severity: Any confirmed unauthenticated remote code execution, authentication bypass, or exposure of sensitive data without credentials is a Critical finding.
ITID-94112.priority: P1 for confirmed unauthenticated compromise or bypass; P2 for information disclosure without direct compromise.
ITID-94112.escalation: Escalate to the Application Owner and CISO for any confirmed unauthenticated compromise or authentication bypass.
indicators: Successful authentication bypass without valid credentials
Sensitive information disclosed via pre-authentication endpoints
Exploitable vulnerability reachable without any account
vectors: Enumeration and exploitation of pre-authentication endpoints (login, registration, password reset)
Testing of publicly reachable application components for injection, misconfiguration, or logic flaws with no credentials
rootCauses: Pre-authentication functionality insufficiently hardened relative to authenticated functionality
Excessive information disclosure in error messages or public endpoints
Missing rate limiting on authentication-adjacent endpoints
ITID-94112.detection: Measures the externally exposed attack surface as encountered by a genuine external attacker with zero prior access, distinct from insider/authenticated-perspective testing.
ITID-94112.response: File findings by severity for developer remediation with defined SLAs; retest after fixes.
metrics: Number of critical/high findings per assessment
Percentage of findings remediated within SLA
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
Web Application Penetration Test Methodology SOP
ITID-94112.notes: Testers must not use any internal documentation, source code, or credentials to simulate a genuine unauthenticated external attacker's starting position.

steps.title: Deliver technical findings report with CVSS-style severity ratings
steps.desc: Publish a technical findings report detailing each vulnerability with a CVSS-style severity rating and remediation guidance.

ITID-94113.def: A planned, rules-of-engagement-bound web application penetration test of a scope not yet mapped to a more specific leaf in this Tier-4 group.

ITID-94121.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers assess internet-facing IP ranges, services, and remote-access infrastructure (VPN, RDP gateways, exposed management interfaces) for exploitable vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, without a social-engineering component.
ITID-94121.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test of the organization's internet-facing network perimeter to assess vulnerabilities in externally reachable infrastructure, services, and remote-access points.
scopeIncludes: Scanning and exploitation testing of internet-facing IP ranges and services
Assessment of remote-access infrastructure (VPN, RDP, exposed admin interfaces)

scopeIncludes: Testing of IAM policy chains for privilege escalation paths from a defined low-privilege starting identity
Assessment of cross-account/cross-service trust relationship misconfigurations
Mapping of the full privilege-escalation attack path for remediation

ITID-94132.severity: Any confirmed escalation path from a standard low-privilege identity to administrative/root cloud access is a Critical finding.

Overly permissive wildcard IAM policies enabling unintended permission chains
Misconfigured cross-account trust relationships allowing unauthorized assumption of privileged roles
vectors: Enumeration and chaining of excessive IAM permissions (e.g., permission-modification rights) to self-escalate privilege
Abuse of misconfigured cross-account or service-to-service trust/role-assumption relationships
rootCauses: Overly broad or wildcard IAM policies not scoped to least privilege
Lack of periodic IAM policy/permission-chain auditing
Cross-account trust relationships configured without adequate condition restrictions
ITID-94132.detection: Measures whether cloud IAM specifically, as distinct from workload/network configuration, contains exploitable privilege-escalation paths.
ITID-94132.response: File a full attack-path report for IAM remediation with defined SLA; retest the specific escalation path after remediation.

Percentage of wildcard/overly-broad policies remediated

ITID-94212.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers request and attempt to crack Kerberos service tickets (Kerberoasting) and perform related AD credential-dumping techniques from a standard domain-joined foothold, testing service account password strength and credential-attack detection.
ITID-94212.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test focused specifically on Kerberos-based and other AD credential attack techniques, to test service account hygiene and credential-attack detection.
scopeIncludes: Kerberoasting and related Kerberos ticket-based credential attacks against service accounts
Testing of OS/LSASS credential-dumping techniques on domain-joined test systems
Testing of SIEM detection for Kerberos anomaly and credential-dumping indicators
scopeExcludes: Full attack-path mapping to Domain Admin not centered on credential attacks (AD Attack Path Mapping and Exploitation Test leaf)
ITID-94212.severity: Any cracked service account password with high privilege, or undetected credential-dumping activity, is a Critical finding.
ITID-94212.priority: P1 for cracked high-privilege service account credentials; P2 for weak but unprivileged service account credentials, or detected-but-delayed alerting.
ITID-94212.escalation: Escalate to Infrastructure Security and the CISO for any cracked service account password holding elevated AD privilege.
indicators: Service account Kerberos tickets successfully cracked offline
No SIEM alert on abnormal Kerberos ticket-request volume/pattern (Kerberoasting indicator)
No EDR alert on LSASS memory access/credential-dumping activity
vectors: Requesting service tickets for accounts with Service Principal Names (SPNs) and attempting offline password cracking
Credential dumping from LSASS or other in-memory credential stores on domain-joined test systems
rootCauses: Service accounts configured with weak or non-rotated passwords
Service accounts holding excessive privilege beyond their functional need
Lack of detection tuning for Kerberos ticket-request anomalies and LSASS access patterns
mitreTechniques: T1558.003 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
controls: Strong, rotated service account passwords / Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA)
ITID-94212.detection: Measures both the strength of service account credential hygiene and detection coverage for Kerberos/credential-dumping attack techniques specifically.
ITID-94212.response: File findings for service account password/privilege remediation and detection tuning; retest after remediation.
metrics: Number of service account passwords cracked
Time to detect Kerberoasting/credential-dumping activity
Percentage of service accounts migrated to gMSA
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
ITID-94212.notes: Cracked credentials must be reported confidentially and rotated immediately; cracking performed offline against captured tickets, not via live account lockout-risking brute force.

steps.title: Provision a dedicated low-privilege test domain account

steps.outcome: Dedicated low-privilege test domain account provisioned.

steps.title: Decide SOC advance notification

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and emergency-contact protocol

steps.outcome: Remediation tracking handoff completed and briefing delivered.

ITID-94221.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers assess database access-control enforcement and attempt injection-based exploitation (via the application layer or direct database access where in scope) to determine whether unauthorized data access or extraction is possible.
ITID-94221.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test assessing database access controls and injection-based exploitation paths, to determine whether an attacker could reach or extract database contents beyond their authorized scope.
scopeIncludes: Testing of database-layer access-control enforcement (roles, row-level security)
Injection-based exploitation paths reaching the database via the application or direct connection
Assessment of least-privilege enforcement for database accounts
scopeExcludes: Encryption-at-rest configuration validation (Database Encryption-at-Rest Validation Test leaf)
ITID-94221.severity: Any confirmed unauthorized extraction of sensitive-classified data via injection or access-control bypass is a Critical finding.
ITID-94221.priority: P1 for confirmed sensitive data extraction; P2 for access-control weaknesses without confirmed extraction.
ITID-94221.escalation: Escalate to the Data Protection team and CISO for any confirmed extraction of sensitive-classified data.
indicators: Successful extraction of database content via injection or access-control bypass
Database accounts holding excessive privilege beyond their functional need
Absence of row-level security or field-level access controls where required
vectors: Injection-based exploitation reaching the database through the application layer
Direct testing of database account privilege boundaries and row/field-level access controls where in scope
rootCauses: Database accounts provisioned with excessive privilege
Lack of parameterized queries at the application layer
Missing row-level or field-level access control enforcement
ITID-94221.detection: Measures whether database access-control and injection-defense layers would prevent unauthorized data extraction if the application layer were compromised.
ITID-94221.response: File findings for database privilege and application remediation with defined SLAs; retest after fixes.
metrics: Number of critical/high findings per assessment
Percentage of database accounts remediated to least privilege
Time to remediation
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
ITID-94221.notes: Direct database testing must be performed against non-production replicas/test instances unless explicit written authorization extends scope to production.

playbook.name: Database Access Control and Injection Penetration Test

steps.title: Define scope (database instance/schema) and obtain signed authorization/Rules of Engagement
steps.desc: Document the exact database instance/schema in scope, confirming it is a test/staging instance where possible, and secure a signed RoE and authorization letter.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file naming the exact scope.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Provision dedicated low-privilege test database accounts
steps.desc: Provision dedicated test database accounts at each privilege level required for access-control testing.
steps.guidance: Never use a real application's production service account credentials directly.
steps.outcome: Dedicated test database accounts provisioned.

steps.title: Decide SOC/DBA-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/DBA team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test database activity monitoring.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and emergency-contact protocol
steps.desc: Explicitly forbid destructive queries beyond proof-of-concept and extraction of real production data, and establish an emergency-contact/stop-work protocol.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list and emergency-contact protocol appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Test the emergency stop-work channel
steps.desc: Verify the emergency-contact channel is reachable before testing begins.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.

steps.title: Test database access controls at each privilege level
steps.desc: Attempt to access data/objects beyond each test account's assigned privilege to identify access-control weaknesses.
steps.outcome: Access-control weaknesses documented with evidence.

steps.title: Test for and exploit injection vulnerabilities
steps.desc: Test application/database interfaces for SQL/NoSQL injection and, where confirmed, demonstrate impact via controlled proof-of-concept.
steps.outcome: Confirmed injection vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept evidence.

steps.title: Verify database integrity and remove test artifacts/accounts

steps.title: Deliver technical findings report with CVSS-style severity ratings

ITID-94222.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test/validation exercise assessing whether database encryption-at-rest is correctly configured, whether key management practices are sound, and whether data would remain unreadable to an attacker who gained storage-layer or backup access.
ITID-94222.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test validating that database encryption-at-rest controls are correctly implemented and effective, to determine whether stored data would remain protected in the event of unauthorized storage-layer access.
scopeIncludes: Validation of encryption-at-rest configuration for production and backup database storage
Assessment of key management practices (rotation, access control, storage of encryption keys)
Testing whether storage/backup-layer access without database-layer credentials exposes readable data
scopeExcludes: Application/database-layer access-control and injection testing (Database Access Control and Injection Penetration Test leaf)
ITID-94222.severity: Any sensitive-classified database found without effective encryption-at-rest, or with encryption keys inadequately protected, is a Critical finding.
ITID-94222.priority: P1 for confirmed absence of effective encryption on sensitive-classified data; P2 for key management weaknesses without confirmed data exposure.
ITID-94222.escalation: Escalate to the Data Protection team and CISO for any sensitive-classified database found without effective encryption-at-rest.
indicators: Database or backup storage readable without decryption despite an assumed encryption-at-rest control
Encryption keys stored alongside or with excessive access to the encrypted data
Backup storage lacking the same encryption standard as production
vectors: Assessment of storage/backup media for readability without proper decryption access
Review of key management configuration for excessive access or weak key-rotation practices
rootCauses: Encryption-at-rest enabled at the platform level but not verified as actually protecting the specific data store
Encryption keys managed with excessive access or inadequate rotation
Backup storage excluded from the same encryption standard as production
controls: Key management service with access control and rotation
Data classification and encryption standard enforcement
ITID-94222.detection: Measures the effectiveness of encryption-at-rest as a defense-in-depth control against storage/backup-layer compromise, independent of access-control or injection defenses.
ITID-94222.response: File findings for encryption/key-management remediation with defined SLAs; retest after fixes.
metrics: Percentage of sensitive-classified databases with validated encryption-at-rest
Percentage of backups with validated encryption
Time to remediation
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
ITID-94222.notes: Validation should be coordinated with the Data Protection/Key Management team; must not extract or retain actual sensitive data during the validation process.

ITID-94231.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers, starting from a standard local user session on a target system, attempt to exploit local misconfigurations, unpatched vulnerabilities, or insecure service configurations to escalate to local administrator/root privilege on that single system.
ITID-94231.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test assessing whether a standard local user on a target system can escalate to local administrator/root privilege, to test endpoint hardening.
scopeIncludes: Escalation attempts confined to a single target system's local privilege boundary
Testing of local service misconfigurations, unquoted paths, weak file/registry permissions, and unpatched local vulnerabilities
Does not require or test cross-system/domain-wide escalation
scopeExcludes: Escalation paths spanning multiple systems or reaching domain-wide privilege (Domain Privilege Escalation Path Penetration Test leaf)
ITID-94231.severity: Any confirmed escalation to local administrator/root from a standard user session is a High finding, or Critical if the system is classified as a high-value asset.
ITID-94231.priority: P1 for confirmed escalation on a high-value/crown-jewel system; P2 for confirmed escalation on a standard system.
ITID-94231.escalation: Escalate to the system/asset owner and Infrastructure Security for any confirmed escalation on a high-value asset.
indicators: Successful escalation to local administrator/root from a standard user session
Insecure service configurations (weak permissions, unquoted service paths) present
Unpatched local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities present
vectors: Exploitation of weak file/folder/registry permissions on privileged service binaries or paths
Exploitation of unpatched local operating system or application vulnerabilities
Abuse of misconfigured scheduled tasks or services running with elevated privilege
rootCauses: Endpoint hardening baseline not consistently enforced
Delayed local/OS patch management
Services configured to run with excessive privilege unnecessarily
ITID-94231.detection: Measures whether endpoint hardening and patch management prevent local privilege escalation on an individual system, the foundational building block of broader escalation chains.
ITID-94231.response: File findings for endpoint hardening/patch remediation with defined SLAs; retest after fixes.
metrics: Number of systems with confirmed local escalation paths
Percentage of systems meeting hardening baseline
Time to remediation
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
ITID-94231.notes: Testing confined to explicitly designated target systems; must not be used to pivot beyond the authorized single-system scope (that is covered by the Domain Privilege Escalation Path leaf).

steps.title: Provision a dedicated standard-privilege local test account
steps.desc: Provision a dedicated, standard-privilege local test account on each target host as the starting point.
steps.guidance: Never use a real employee's live local account.
steps.outcome: Dedicated standard-privilege test account provisioned per host.

steps.title: Decide SOC/EDR-team advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC/EDR team is notified in advance or kept unaware to test host-based detection.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and emergency-contact protocol

steps.title: Test the emergency stop-work channel
steps.desc: Verify the emergency-contact channel is reachable before testing begins.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
