ITID-94232.def: A rules-of-engagement-bound penetration test in which testers, having established local privilege escalation or a domain-joined foothold, attempt to chain that access across systems and trust boundaries to reach domain-wide elevated privilege, testing whether local compromise can cascade into broader domain compromise.
ITID-94232.purpose: Captures an authorized penetration test assessing whether privilege escalation on an individual system can be chained into domain-wide elevated privilege, testing the organization's segmentation and tiering between local and domain trust boundaries.
scopeIncludes: Escalation chains spanning multiple systems and crossing local-to-domain trust boundaries
Testing of credential reuse, delegation, and trust-relationship abuse across systems
Documentation of the full cross-system attack path
scopeExcludes: Escalation confined to a single local system (Local Privilege Escalation Penetration Test leaf)
ITID-94232.severity: Any confirmed chaining of local access into domain-wide elevated privilege is a Critical finding.
ITID-94232.priority: P1 for confirmed cross-system escalation to domain-wide privilege; P2 for partial chaining without reaching domain-wide privilege.
ITID-94232.escalation: Escalate immediately to the CISO and Infrastructure Security team for any confirmed local-to-domain escalation chain.
indicators: Successful escalation from local system compromise to domain-wide elevated privilege
Reused local administrator credentials across multiple systems enabling lateral chaining
Insufficient network/administrative segmentation between system tiers
vectors: Reuse of harvested local administrator credentials across multiple systems
Abuse of delegation or trust relationships to pivot from local compromise toward domain-wide access
Chaining of local escalation techniques with lateral movement to reach higher-tier systems
rootCauses: Local administrator credentials not unique per system (shared/reused local admin passwords)
Lack of network segmentation/tiering between workstation, server, and domain-controller tiers
Insufficient monitoring of cross-tier authentication patterns
controls: Unique local administrator credentials per system (e.g., LAPS)
ITID-94232.detection: Measures whether the organization's segmentation between local and domain trust boundaries actually contains a local compromise, the key differentiator from single-system local escalation testing.
ITID-94232.response: File a full cross-system attack-path report with prioritized remediation of the weakest segmentation link; retest the path after remediation.
metrics: Number of confirmed cross-system escalation paths found
Number of systems sharing reused local administrator credentials
Time to remediation
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
ITID-94232.notes: Starting foothold and target domain privilege level must be explicitly pre-authorized; testing must avoid account lockouts and unnecessary disruption to production authentication systems.

playbook.name: Domain Privilege Escalation Path Penetration Test
playbook.description: Formal penetration test escalating from a standard domain user to Domain Admin (or equivalent) privilege via chained domain misconfigurations.

steps.title: Define scope (domain boundary) and obtain signed authorization/Rules of Engagement
steps.desc: Document the domain boundary in scope for domain privilege escalation testing and secure a signed RoE and authorization letter.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file naming the exact scope.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Provision a dedicated standard-privilege test domain account
steps.desc: Provision a dedicated, standard-privilege test domain account as the starting foothold.
steps.guidance: Never use a real employee's live domain account.
steps.outcome: Dedicated standard-privilege test domain account provisioned.

steps.title: Decide SOC advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC is notified in advance or kept unaware to test domain-escalation detection.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and emergency-contact protocol
steps.desc: Explicitly forbid actions risking real account lockouts or production Group Policy changes beyond proof-of-concept, and establish an emergency-contact/stop-work protocol.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list and emergency-contact protocol appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Test the emergency stop-work channel
steps.desc: Verify the emergency-contact channel is reachable before testing begins.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If production impact occurs, halt immediately.

steps.title: Map domain privilege escalation paths from the test account
steps.desc: From the test account, map possible domain privilege escalation paths (e.g. ACL abuse, GPO misconfiguration, delegation abuse) toward Domain Admin.
steps.outcome: Candidate escalation path(s) identified and documented.

steps.title: Execute the identified escalation path to confirm domain compromise
steps.desc: Execute the mapped domain escalation path using a controlled proof-of-concept to confirm Domain Admin-equivalent access is achievable.
steps.guidance: Stop as soon as domain compromise is sufficiently proven.
steps.outcome: Elevated domain access confirmed and evidenced.

steps.title: Revert any AD changes and remove the test account
steps.desc: Revert any ACL/group membership changes made during the exercise and remove the dedicated test account.
steps.outcome: AD environment confirmed reverted; test account removed.

steps.title: Deliver technical findings report with CVSS-style severity ratings
steps.desc: Publish a technical findings report detailing the escalation path(s) found with severity ratings and remediation guidance.
steps.outcome: Findings report delivered with severity ratings per finding.

steps.title: Hand off findings to vulnerability-management for remediation tracking
steps.desc: Route each finding into the vulnerability-management process with an owner and due date, and brief the AD/domain team/CISO.
steps.outcome: Remediation tracking handoff completed and briefing delivered.

ITID-94233.def: A planned, rules-of-engagement-bound privilege escalation test of a scope not yet mapped to a more specific leaf in this Tier-4 group.
ITID-94233.purpose: Intake bucket for authorized privilege escalation test exercises not yet classified into the local or domain-path leaves.
scopeIncludes: Novel or combined privilege escalation test formats pending classification
scopeExcludes: Single-system local escalation testing (Local Privilege Escalation Penetration Test leaf)
Cross-system domain escalation-path testing (Domain Privilege Escalation Path Penetration Test leaf)
ITID-94233.severity: Apply standard privilege escalation test severity criteria pending triage and reclassification.
ITID-94233.escalation: Escalate to Infrastructure Security for triage and possible reclassification.
indicators: Findings not matching an existing specific leaf's pattern
vectors: Emerging or hybrid privilege escalation test techniques
rootCauses: Assessment scope not yet formally categorized in the taxonomy
ITID-94233.detection: Provides general privilege escalation test visibility pending reclassification.
ITID-94233.response: Triage and reclassify where a clear pattern emerges; otherwise track under general metrics.
metrics: Number of findings pending reclassification
sops: Penetration Test Scope and Authorization SOP
ITID-94233.notes: Intake/catch-all category; reclassify as soon as the assessment scope is clear.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Privilege Escalation Testing
playbook.description: Baseline formal privilege escalation penetration test used when no more specific local/domain sub-type applies.

steps.title: Define scope (target hosts/domain boundary) and obtain signed authorization/Rules of Engagement
steps.desc: Document the target hosts/domain boundary in scope for privilege escalation testing and secure a signed RoE and authorization letter.
steps.outcome: Signed RoE and authorization letter on file naming the exact scope.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without a countersigned RoE.

steps.title: Provision a dedicated standard-privilege test account
steps.desc: Provision a dedicated, standard-privilege test account (local or domain, as applicable) as the starting foothold.
steps.guidance: Never use a real employee's live account.
steps.outcome: Dedicated standard-privilege test account provisioned.

steps.title: Decide SOC advance notification
steps.desc: Deliberately decide whether the SOC is notified in advance or kept unaware.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and communicated as appropriate.

steps.title: Define out-of-scope actions and emergency-contact protocol
steps.desc: Explicitly forbid actions risking instability or real user impact beyond proof-of-concept, and establish an emergency-contact/stop-work protocol.
steps.outcome: Written out-of-scope list and emergency-contact protocol appended to the RoE.

steps.title: Test the emergency stop-work channel
steps.desc: Verify the emergency-contact channel is reachable before testing begins.
steps.outcome: Abort channel tested and confirmed reachable.
steps.abort: If instability or production impact occurs, halt immediately.

steps.title: Enumerate privilege escalation vectors from the foothold
steps.desc: From the test account, enumerate misconfigurations or vulnerabilities that could enable privilege escalation.
steps.outcome: Candidate escalation vectors identified and documented.

steps.title: Execute the escalation to confirm elevated access
steps.desc: Execute the identified escalation vector(s) to confirm elevated privilege is achievable, using a controlled proof-of-concept.
steps.guidance: Stop as soon as elevated access is sufficiently proven.
steps.outcome: Elevated access confirmed and evidenced.

steps.title: Revert configuration changes and remove test account
steps.desc: Undo any configuration changes made to achieve escalation and remove the dedicated test account.
steps.outcome: Touched systems confirmed reverted and clean; test account removed.

steps.title: Deliver technical findings report with CVSS-style severity ratings
steps.desc: Publish a technical findings report detailing the escalation vector(s) found with severity ratings and remediation guidance.
steps.outcome: Findings report delivered with severity ratings per finding.

steps.title: Hand off findings to vulnerability-management for remediation tracking
steps.desc: Route each finding into the vulnerability-management process with an owner and due date, and brief the system owner/CISO.
steps.outcome: Remediation tracking handoff completed and briefing delivered.

ITID-95111.def: A planned, authorized exercise in which a tailored phishing email crafted around a specific pretext (as opposed to a generic bulk campaign) is sent to a targeted individual or small group to measure susceptibility, reporting behavior, and control efficacy, filed here when no more specific spear-phishing sub-type has been defined.
ITID-95111.purpose: Intake/general bucket for targeted spear-phishing simulation activity run under the security awareness program.
scopeIncludes: Crafting and sending a pretext-tailored phishing email to a targeted individual/group
Measuring click-through, credential-entry, and reporting rates
Testing whether email security controls (filtering, banners) engage as expected
scopeExcludes: Voice-based social engineering tests (vishing, covered under ITID-95121/95122)
Physical media-based tests (USB drop, covered under ITID-95131/95132)
ITID-95111.severity: An executive or privileged user entering credentials on the simulated page is a Critical finding; a click without credential entry is Medium; a report-without-click is a positive control outcome, not a finding.
ITID-95111.priority: P1 for credential entry by a privileged/high-value target; P2 for click-through without credential entry; P3 for delayed reporting behavior.
ITID-95111.escalation: Escalate to the CISO for any executive/privileged-account credential entry; notify the awareness program lead for department-level trend findings.
indicators: Click-through rate at or below program baseline
Reporting rate at or above program baseline
Credential entry rate above zero on a privileged-account target — a genuine finding
vectors: Pretext-tailored phishing email referencing role-specific or organizationally plausible context, sent from an approved simulation platform
rootCauses: Insufficient or outdated awareness training for the targeted population
Email security controls not flagging the simulation domain as expected (a control-tuning artifact, not a true gap, if the simulation platform is allow-listed)
No easy one-click reporting mechanism available to the user
ITID-95111.detection: Validates human-layer resistance to targeted phishing and the effectiveness of the easy-reporting control, complementing technical email-filtering controls.
ITID-95111.response: Provide targeted coaching/training to individuals who clicked or entered credentials; track department-level trends for program adjustment; retest at the next scheduled interval.
metrics: Click-through rate
Credential-entry rate
Reporting rate
Trend over successive campaigns
ITID-95111.notes: Requires prior sign-off from HR/legal and clear internal communication boundaries so simulations are not mistaken for disciplinary entrapment; simulation infrastructure should be allow-listed appropriately to avoid conflating email-filter tuning with awareness-training results.

playbook.name: General Targeted Spear Phishing Simulation (Awareness Program Context)
playbook.description: Planned, authorized spear phishing simulation targeting a specific employee population to measure and improve susceptibility to targeted social engineering.

steps.title: Define target population and objective
steps.desc: Identify the specific employee group being tested and the awareness objective (e.g. measure click/report rate for a targeted pretext).
steps.outcome: Target population and objective documented.

steps.title: Draft the phishing pretext and obtain Legal/HR/Communications sign-off
steps.desc: Design the email pretext and get explicit written approval from Legal, HR, and Communications before targeting real employees, given the reputational/trust sensitivity of this test type.
steps.guidance: Avoid pretexts that exploit personal crises, medical topics, or job-loss fear — these have historically caused significant employee distress.
steps.outcome: Pretext approved by all required stakeholders and documented.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without Legal, HR, and Communications sign-off.

steps.title: Notify security leadership and schedule the campaign
steps.desc: Get final sign-off on timing from security leadership.
steps.outcome: Campaign scheduled and approved.

steps.title: Coordinate with IT helpdesk on the campaign window
steps.desc: Notify helpdesk of the simulation window and provide them talking points so real employee-reported tickets about the email are handled smoothly without confusion.
steps.outcome: Helpdesk briefed and ready.

steps.title: Prepare supportive, non-punitive post-click messaging
steps.desc: Draft the landing page/message shown to anyone who clicks, and confirm no punitive language or disciplinary consequence is implied.
steps.guidance: Frame the message as a learning moment, not a failure notice.
steps.outcome: Non-punitive messaging drafted and approved.

steps.title: Send the simulated phishing campaign
steps.desc: Deploy the approved email to the target population via the phishing simulation platform.
steps.outcome: Campaign sent successfully.

steps.title: Capture click, report, and credential-entry metrics
steps.desc: Track who clicked, who reported the email to security, and who entered credentials (if applicable).
steps.outcome: Full metrics captured per recipient.

steps.title: Deliver supportive just-in-time training to anyone who clicked
steps.desc: Automatically route anyone who clicked or entered credentials to brief, supportive training content.
steps.guidance: Reinforce that this is developmental, not disciplinary.
steps.outcome: Training delivered to all applicable participants.

steps.title: Recognize employees who correctly reported the email
steps.desc: Send positive reinforcement to employees who identified and reported the simulated phish.
steps.outcome: Positive reinforcement sent.

steps.title: Update phishing susceptibility baseline
steps.desc: Record click/report rates in the ongoing awareness program baseline for trend tracking.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

steps.title: Brief leadership on results and next campaign focus
steps.desc: Share aggregate (non-individually-punitive) results with leadership and plan the next campaign's focus area.
steps.outcome: Leadership briefed and next steps agreed.

ITID-95121.def: A planned exercise in which testers place phone calls to employees impersonating the internal IT help desk (e.g., requesting a password reset, MFA code, or remote-access approval) to measure susceptibility and adherence to identity-verification procedures.
ITID-95121.purpose: Captures the test type used to assess employee resistance to a vishing pretext impersonating the internal help desk.
scopeIncludes: Placing calls using a help-desk-impersonation pretext to a sample of employees
Attempting to elicit credentials, MFA codes, or unauthorized remote-access approval
Measuring whether the employee follows the required caller-verification procedure
scopeExcludes: Executive-impersonation pretexts targeting privileged decision-makers (sibling ITID-95122)
Email-based phishing simulations (covered under ITID-95111)
ITID-95121.severity: An employee providing an MFA code or granting unauthorized remote access is a Critical finding; providing a password without MFA bypass is High/Medium; failing to log/report a suspicious call without disclosing anything is Low.
ITID-95121.priority: P1 for MFA/remote-access compromise during the test; P2 for password disclosure; P3 for non-reporting without disclosure.
ITID-95121.escalation: Escalate to the CISO immediately if the test tester successfully obtains an MFA code or live remote-access session, since this represents a real exploitable process gap.
indicators: Employee correctly follows caller-verification procedure and declines to provide sensitive information
Employee discloses a password or other credential to the caller
Employee grants remote access or reads back an MFA code
vectors: Phone-based pretexting impersonating internal IT/help-desk staff, using publicly available or organizationally plausible context to build credibility
rootCauses: No formal caller-identity-verification procedure exists or is not enforced
Employees not trained on help-desk impersonation as a specific vishing pattern
Help desk's real caller ID/process is easily spoofable or mimicked
controls: Help desk authentication policy for sensitive requests
ITID-95121.detection: Validates the human-process control layer that technical MFA/authentication controls rely on when a caller attempts social-engineering bypass.
ITID-95121.response: Provide targeted coaching for employees who disclosed information; escalate any successful MFA/remote-access compromise as a process-gap finding requiring immediate procedural fix; retest after remediation.
metrics: Percentage of calls resulting in disclosure
Percentage of calls where verification procedure was correctly followed
MFA/remote-access compromise rate
ITID-95121.notes: Requires HR/legal sign-off; testers must record calls only where legally permitted and must debrief participants promptly after the call.

playbook.name: Vishing Test Targeting Help Desk Impersonation Scenario
playbook.description: Planned, authorized voice phishing simulation impersonating an employee to test whether the help desk follows identity verification procedure.

steps.title: Define scenario and objective
steps.desc: Document the impersonation pretext (e.g. caller claims to be a locked-out employee requesting a password reset) and the specific verification procedure being tested.
steps.outcome: Scenario and objective documented.

steps.title: Obtain Legal/HR/Communications and helpdesk management sign-off
steps.desc: Get explicit written approval given the test targets real help desk staff and simulates deception of a real person.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization from all required stakeholders on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without full sign-off.

steps.title: Select test call targets and schedule
steps.desc: Identify which help desk shift/agents will be called and when.
steps.outcome: Targets and schedule documented.

steps.title: Define a safe-word/abort signal for the caller
steps.desc: Establish a way for the test caller to immediately reveal the test if the interaction risks real harm (e.g. agent becomes distressed) or an actual account change is about to occur.
steps.outcome: Abort signal defined and understood by the tester.
steps.abort: Reveal the test immediately if a real account change is about to be made or the agent is distressed.

steps.title: Prepare supportive post-test messaging for participants
steps.desc: Draft a non-punitive debrief message for any agent who completed the requested action, framing it as a coaching opportunity.
steps.outcome: Supportive messaging prepared and approved.

steps.title: Place the test call and attempt the pretext
steps.desc: Execute the planned impersonation call against the target help desk agent.
steps.outcome: Call completed per plan.
steps.abort: Abort per the defined safe-word condition.

steps.title: Record whether verification procedure was followed
steps.desc: Document whether the agent correctly verified identity before taking the requested action.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded (procedure followed / bypassed).

steps.title: Reveal the test and debrief the agent supportively
steps.desc: Inform the agent this was an authorized test and walk through the correct procedure, framed as coaching not discipline.
steps.outcome: Agent debriefed supportively.

steps.title: Undo any real account action taken during the test
steps.desc: Reverse any password reset or account change that was actually performed during the test call.
steps.outcome: Any real account state changes reverted.

steps.title: Update help desk verification procedure if a gap was found
steps.desc: Revise the identity-verification runbook/training if the test revealed a procedural weakness.
steps.outcome: Procedure updated if needed.

steps.title: Update vishing resilience baseline
steps.desc: Record the result in the ongoing social engineering resilience baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-95122.def: A planned exercise in which testers place phone calls impersonating a senior executive (e.g., CEO/CFO) to pressure a targeted employee (typically in finance, HR, or IT) into an urgent, policy-bypassing action such as a wire transfer, gift-card purchase, or emergency access grant.
ITID-95122.purpose: Captures the test type used to assess resistance to a vishing pretext impersonating an executive to pressure urgent, unauthorized action.
scopeIncludes: Placing calls using an executive-impersonation pretext with urgency/authority pressure
Attempting to elicit a policy-bypassing financial or access action
Measuring whether the employee follows required out-of-band verification for executive requests
scopeExcludes: Help-desk-impersonation pretexts targeting general credential/MFA disclosure (sibling ITID-95121)
Email-based business email compromise simulations (covered under phishing test ITIDs)
ITID-95122.severity: An employee proceeding with a simulated financial transfer or unauthorized access grant is a Critical finding; an employee hesitating but not fully verifying before proceeding is Medium; correct verification behavior is a positive outcome, not a finding.
ITID-95122.priority: P1 for a completed simulated unauthorized transaction/access grant; P2 for partial procedural lapses that did not reach completion; P3 for minor process-documentation gaps.
ITID-95122.escalation: Escalate to the CISO and CFO/finance leadership immediately if the test reveals an employee would have completed an unauthorized wire transfer or access grant.
indicators: Employee correctly pauses and applies out-of-band verification before acting on the urgent request
Employee proceeds with the requested action without independent verification
Employee reports the suspicious call through the correct channel
vectors: Phone-based pretexting impersonating a senior executive, combined with urgency and authority pressure to bypass normal verification
rootCauses: No mandatory out-of-band verification policy for high-value financial/access requests
Employees not trained to recognize authority-pressure social engineering
Executive impersonation made easier by publicly available voice samples or org-chart information
controls: Out-of-band verification policy for financial/access requests
ITID-95122.detection: Validates the human-process and financial-control layer that mitigates business-email-compromise-style social engineering distinct from purely technical controls.
ITID-95122.response: Provide targeted coaching for employees who proceeded without verification; escalate any completed simulated transaction as a critical process-gap finding requiring an immediate control fix; retest after remediation.
metrics: Percentage of calls resulting in a completed unauthorized action
Percentage of calls where out-of-band verification was correctly applied
Reporting rate
ITID-95122.notes: Requires explicit executive and legal sign-off before impersonating a named executive, even in a controlled test; debrief targeted employees and their managers promptly to avoid reputational or trust impact.

playbook.name: Vishing Test Targeting Executive Impersonation Scenario
playbook.description: Planned, authorized voice phishing simulation impersonating an executive to test whether staff follow verification procedure for high-pressure authority-based requests.

steps.title: Define scenario and objective
steps.desc: Document the executive-impersonation pretext (e.g. urgent wire transfer or credential request) and the verification procedure being tested.
steps.outcome: Scenario and objective documented.

steps.title: Obtain sign-off from the impersonated executive, Legal, HR, and Communications
steps.desc: Get explicit written approval, including from the actual executive whose identity will be simulated, given the sensitivity of this scenario.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization from all required stakeholders on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without full sign-off, including the impersonated executive's consent.

steps.title: Select test call targets and schedule
steps.desc: Identify which staff (e.g. finance, EA pool) will be called and when.
steps.outcome: Targets and schedule documented.

steps.title: Define a hard cap on financial/action impact
steps.desc: Ensure the scenario cannot result in an actual funds transfer or irreversible action — cap the test at the point where the target would take the harmful action.
steps.outcome: Hard cap defined and understood by the tester.
steps.abort: Stop before any real transaction or irreversible action is initiated.

steps.title: Prepare supportive post-test messaging for participants
steps.desc: Draft a non-punitive debrief message emphasizing that authority-pressure pretexts are specifically designed to be difficult to resist.
steps.outcome: Supportive messaging prepared and approved.

steps.title: Place the test call and attempt the pretext
steps.desc: Execute the planned executive-impersonation call against the target.
steps.outcome: Call completed per plan, stopping at the defined hard cap.
steps.abort: Abort per the defined hard cap.

steps.title: Record whether verification procedure was followed
steps.desc: Document whether the target correctly verified the request through an independent channel before proceeding.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded.

steps.title: Reveal the test and debrief the participant supportively
steps.desc: Inform the target this was an authorized test and review the correct verification procedure in a coaching-focused conversation.
steps.outcome: Participant debriefed supportively.

steps.title: Confirm no real financial or system action occurred
steps.desc: Double-check no real transaction, transfer, or account change resulted from the test.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no real-world impact.

steps.title: Update financial verification procedure if a gap was found
steps.desc: Revise the payment/verification runbook if the test revealed a procedural weakness.
steps.outcome: Procedure updated if needed.

steps.title: Update vishing resilience baseline
steps.desc: Record the result in the ongoing social engineering resilience baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-95123.def: A catch-all classification for planned vishing exercises that fall outside the help-desk-impersonation and executive-impersonation test categories, pending reclassification or documentation of a new sub-type.
ITID-95123.purpose: Intake bucket for vishing testing activity that does not cleanly map to a defined help-desk or executive impersonation test type.
scopeIncludes: Vishing testing activity not yet matched to a specific defined sub-type
scopeExcludes: Any activity that clearly fits ITID-95121 (help desk) or ITID-95122 (executive) once identified
ITID-95123.severity: Assess on a case-by-case basis using the general vishing-finding severity framework until the activity is reclassified.
ITID-95123.priority: Triage promptly to confirm whether reclassification to a defined sub-type is appropriate.
ITID-95123.escalation: Escalate to the awareness program lead for reclassification guidance if volume in this bucket grows.
indicators: Test activity logged without a clear match to an existing vishing test sub-type
vectors: Varies; not yet characterized
rootCauses: Varies; not yet characterized
ITID-95123.detection: Not standardized; depends on the specific activity captured under this catch-all.
ITID-95123.response: Review periodically and reclassify recurring patterns into a formally defined sub-type.
metrics: Volume of records filed under this catch-all over time
ITID-95123.notes: This leaf should stay low-volume; a growing count is a signal to define new Tier-5 vishing test sub-types.

playbook.name: General Vishing Testing
playbook.description: General-purpose planned voice phishing simulation when no more specific vishing scenario applies.

steps.title: Define scenario and objective
steps.desc: Document the pretext and the verification behavior being tested.
steps.outcome: Scenario and objective documented.

steps.title: Obtain Legal/HR/Communications sign-off
steps.desc: Get explicit written approval given the test targets real employees.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without full sign-off.

steps.title: Define an abort/reveal condition
steps.desc: Establish when the test caller must immediately reveal the test to prevent real harm or irreversible action.
steps.outcome: Abort condition documented.
steps.abort: Reveal the test immediately if real harm or an irreversible action is imminent.

steps.title: Prepare supportive post-test messaging
steps.desc: Draft non-punitive debrief messaging for participants regardless of outcome.
steps.outcome: Messaging prepared and approved.

steps.title: Place the test call and attempt the pretext
steps.desc: Execute the planned call against the target.
steps.outcome: Call completed per plan.
steps.abort: Abort per the defined condition.

steps.title: Record the outcome
steps.desc: Document whether the target followed correct procedure.
steps.outcome: Outcome recorded.

steps.title: Reveal the test and debrief supportively
steps.desc: Inform the participant of the test and review correct procedure in a coaching-focused conversation.
steps.outcome: Participant debriefed.

steps.title: Confirm no real-world impact occurred
steps.desc: Verify no real account or financial action resulted from the test.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no impact.

steps.title: Update verification procedure and resilience baseline
steps.desc: Revise relevant runbooks and update the social engineering resilience baseline.
steps.outcome: Procedure and baseline updated as needed.

ITID-95131.def: A planned exercise in which branded USB devices (often marked with an enticing label such as a department name or 'confidential') are deliberately left in parking lots, lobbies, or other common areas to measure whether employees pick them up and connect them to a corporate device.
ITID-95131.purpose: Captures the test type used to assess employee resistance to picking up and plugging in an unknown USB device found in a physical common area.
scopeIncludes: Placing branded/labeled USB devices in designated common-area drop locations
Measuring pickup and connection rates via a passive callback/beacon mechanism
Measuring reporting rate to security when a device is found
scopeExcludes: Devices specifically instrumented with a tracked beacon file to measure file-open/click-through behavior (sibling ITID-95132)
Digital phishing/vishing simulations (covered under other Tier-4 test types)
ITID-95131.severity: A device connected to a networked corporate endpoint with no reporting is a Critical finding; a device connected in an isolated/air-gapped manner (if detectable) is Medium; a device found and correctly reported unopened is a positive outcome, not a finding.
ITID-95131.priority: P1 for connection to a networked production endpoint; P2 for connection to an isolated test asset; P3 for pickup without connection or reporting.
ITID-95131.escalation: Escalate to the CISO if a device is connected to a networked corporate endpoint, since this mirrors a real removable-media attack vector.
indicators: Device found and reported to security without being connected
Device connected to a corporate endpoint (detected via the passive callback mechanism)
Endpoint control (e.g., removable-media policy) blocks the device automatically upon connection
vectors: Physical placement of a labeled/branded USB device in a common area frequented by employees, using curiosity or a plausible pretext label as bait
rootCauses: No enforced removable-media/USB restriction policy on endpoints
Employees not trained on physical media as a social-engineering vector
No easy physical-security reporting channel for found devices
controls: Security awareness training on physical social engineering
ITID-95131.detection: Validates both the human-behavior layer (reporting unknown media) and the technical control layer (USB restriction policy enforcement) against a physical initial-access vector.
ITID-95131.response: Provide coaching/awareness reinforcement for individuals who connected a device; file a finding if endpoint removable-media controls did not block the connection; retest after control/training updates.
metrics: Pickup rate
Connection rate
Reporting rate
Endpoint-control block rate
ITID-95131.notes: Devices must be pre-loaded only with inert, clearly-labeled test payloads and no functional exploit code; requires legal/HR sign-off given the physical and potentially individually-identifiable nature of the test.

playbook.name: Branded USB Drop Test in Parking Lot/Common Area
playbook.description: Planned exercise placing branded USB drives in common areas to measure whether employees plug in unknown removable media.

steps.title: Define objective and drop locations
steps.desc: Document the awareness objective and the specific common areas/locations where devices will be placed.
steps.outcome: Objective and locations documented.

steps.title: Prepare inert USB devices with benign tracking payload
steps.desc: Configure USB drives with a harmless beacon file/document (no malicious payload) that only reports a plug-in event.
steps.guidance: Never use an actual malicious payload, even for internal testing.
steps.outcome: Devices prepared and verified inert.

steps.title: Obtain Legal/HR/Communications/facilities sign-off
steps.desc: Get explicit written approval given devices will be placed for real employees to find, including facilities approval for the physical drop.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization from all required stakeholders on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without full sign-off.

steps.title: Notify IT helpdesk and security guards of the test window
steps.desc: Advise helpdesk and physical security staff so found devices reported to them are handled per the test plan and not treated as a real security incident.
steps.outcome: Helpdesk and security staff briefed.

steps.title: Confirm no real malicious capability on the devices
steps.desc: Double-check the devices contain only the inert beacon payload with no autorun or executable malware.
steps.outcome: Devices confirmed inert prior to placement.
steps.abort: Abort if any device is found to contain unintended executable content.

steps.title: Place the devices at planned drop locations
steps.desc: Distribute the prepared USB devices at the approved locations at the scheduled time.
steps.outcome: Devices placed as planned.

steps.title: Monitor and log plug-in/beacon events

ITID-95132.def: A planned exercise in which a USB device pre-loaded with a tracked beacon file (a file that phones home upon opening, without executing any real payload) is placed for discovery, to measure not just whether the device is connected but whether the bait file inside is actually opened.
ITID-95132.purpose: Captures the test type used to measure file-open/click-through behavior once a dropped USB device is connected, via a tracked beacon file.
scopeIncludes: Measuring the file-open/click-through rate once a device has been connected
Distinguishing 'connected but did not open the file' from 'opened the tracked file'
Confirming the beacon callback mechanism itself works reliably as a measurement tool
scopeExcludes: Simple pickup/connection-rate measurement without file-open tracking (sibling ITID-95131)
Devices carrying any functional exploit or malicious payload (out of scope for authorized testing)
ITID-95132.severity: A tracked file opened on a networked production endpoint with no reporting is a Critical finding; opened on an isolated asset is Medium; connected but not opened is a lower-severity partial finding.
ITID-95132.priority: P1 for file-open on a networked production endpoint; P2 for file-open on an isolated asset; P3 for connection-without-open behavior.
ITID-95132.escalation: Escalate to the CISO if the tracked file is opened on a networked corporate endpoint, since opening an unknown file mirrors real payload-execution risk.
indicators: Beacon callback confirms the file was never opened despite device connection
Beacon callback confirms the file was opened, indicating a genuine behavioral finding
No beacon callback received at all, indicating a possible device-loss or tooling issue rather than a real result
vectors: Physical placement of a USB device containing a tracked, inert beacon file (e.g., a decoy document) designed to callback on open, using a plausible file name as bait
rootCauses: Endpoint auto-run/auto-open behavior not disabled by policy
Employees not trained to treat unknown files as suspicious even after connecting a device out of curiosity
No file-execution restriction on removable media
controls: File execution restriction on removable media
Security awareness training on physical social engineering
ITID-95132.detection: Validates the deeper behavioral layer beyond simple device connection — whether users take the additional step of opening an unknown file — against a physical initial-access and execution vector.
ITID-95132.response: Provide targeted coaching for individuals who opened the tracked file; file a finding if endpoint controls did not restrict auto-run/execution; retest after control/training updates.
metrics: File-open rate among connected devices
Beacon callback reliability rate
Trend over successive test cycles
ITID-95132.notes: The beacon file must be strictly inert (no macros/executable payload) and reviewed by application security before use; requires legal/HR sign-off.

ITID-95211.def: A planned exercise confirming that SAST tooling executes automatically on every relevant CI build/pull request, correctly scans the intended code paths, and surfaces known-vulnerable code patterns (e.g., a deliberately introduced test vulnerability) as expected.

scopeIncludes: Confirming SAST scan triggers automatically on the defined CI events (PR, merge, scheduled build)
Validating scan completes within pipeline time budget and does not silently fail
Confirming a deliberately introduced known-vulnerable code pattern is flagged
scopeExcludes: Manual triage of findings and false-positive review quality (sibling ITID-95212)

ITID-95211.severity: The SAST scan silently failing or not triggering at all in the CI pipeline is a Critical finding; the scan running but missing a well-known vulnerability class is High/Medium; minor scan-configuration gaps are Low.
ITID-95211.priority: P1 for a silently failing/non-triggering pipeline integration; P2 for missed known-vulnerability-class detection; P3 for configuration tuning gaps.
ITID-95211.escalation: Escalate to the engineering lead and application security lead if the SAST scan is silently failing across builds, since this represents an unmonitored gap in the secure-development pipeline.
indicators: SAST scan triggers and completes on every relevant CI event
Deliberately introduced known-vulnerable code pattern is correctly flagged
Scan silently skipped, times out, or fails without blocking the build or alerting the team
vectors: N/A — this is a secure-development/vulnerability-management practice, not a detection-validation exercise; it doesn't map to ATT&CK adversary behavior.
rootCauses: CI pipeline configuration change inadvertently removed or disabled the SAST step
Scan tool license/quota exhausted, causing silent skips
Scan scope excludes newer repositories or microservices not added to the tooling's inventory
controls: SAST tool coverage and license management

Mean time to detect a silent pipeline failure
Detection rate for the seeded known-vulnerable pattern

ITID-95231.def: A planned exercise confirming that the SBOM-generation tooling produces an accurate, complete dependency inventory for a given software artifact and that the generated SBOM is correctly cross-checked against vulnerability databases (e.g., NVD, OSV) to surface known-vulnerable dependencies.
ITID-95231.purpose: Captures the test type used to validate that SBOM generation correctly captures dependency inventory and cross-checks it against known vulnerability data.
scopeIncludes: Generating an SBOM for a designated build/artifact and cross-checking it against a known-vulnerable dependency seeded into the test build
Confirming the vulnerability cross-check surfaces the seeded known-CVE dependency
Validating SBOM generation runs automatically as part of the build pipeline
scopeExcludes: Manual audit of SBOM completeness/accuracy against the actual build manifest (sibling ITID-95232)
Source-code-level static analysis (covered under SAST test ITIDs)
ITID-95231.severity: The vulnerability cross-check failing to flag a seeded known-CVE dependency is a Critical finding; the SBOM generation step silently failing in the pipeline is High; minor metadata-completeness gaps are Low.
ITID-95231.priority: P1 for a missed seeded known-CVE dependency; P2 for silent SBOM-generation pipeline failure; P3 for metadata gaps.
ITID-95231.escalation: Escalate to the engineering lead and application security lead if the vulnerability cross-check fails to flag a well-known, seeded CVE-affected dependency.
indicators: SBOM generates successfully and includes the seeded known-vulnerable dependency
Vulnerability cross-check correctly flags the seeded dependency's known CVE
SBOM generation step silently skipped or fails without blocking the build
vectors: N/A — this is a secure-development/vulnerability-management practice, not a detection-validation exercise; it doesn't map to ATT&CK adversary behavior.
rootCauses: SBOM tool not updated to the latest vulnerability database feed
Build pipeline configuration change inadvertently removed the SBOM-generation step
Transitive dependencies not fully resolved by the SBOM tool
ITID-95231.detection: Not applicable in ATT&CK terms; this test validates the software supply-chain visibility and vulnerability cross-check tooling reliability.
ITID-95231.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any missed vulnerability or pipeline failure; retest after tooling/pipeline is corrected.
metrics: Percentage of builds with a successfully generated SBOM
Detection rate for the seeded known-CVE dependency
Mean time to detect a silent pipeline failure
sops: SBOM Generation and Vulnerability Cross-Check SOP
ITID-95231.notes: This is a secure-development/vulnerability-management practice, not a detection-validation exercise; it doesn't map to ATT&CK adversary behavior. Seed a known-CVE test dependency in a disposable build only, never in a production-bound artifact.

playbook.name: SBOM Generation and Dependency Vulnerability Cross-Check
playbook.description: Planned exercise generating a software bill of materials for an application and cross-checking its components against known vulnerability databases.

steps.title: Define the application/build in scope
steps.desc: Identify the specific application version/build for which the SBOM will be generated and cross-checked.
steps.outcome: Scope documented.

steps.title: Obtain engineering lead sign-off
steps.desc: Get approval before running SBOM generation tooling against the build/pipeline.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.

steps.title: Confirm generation runs in a non-disruptive pipeline stage
steps.desc: Verify SBOM generation won't block or delay a release-critical build if run inline.
steps.outcome: Confirmed non-disruptive.

steps.title: Generate the SBOM
steps.desc: Run the SBOM generation tool against the in-scope build to produce a full component/dependency inventory.
steps.outcome: SBOM generated successfully.

steps.title: Cross-check components against vulnerability databases
steps.desc: Match each SBOM component/version against known vulnerability feeds (e.g. NVD) to identify at-risk dependencies.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability cross-check completed with a findings list.

steps.title: Prioritize findings by exploitability and exposure
steps.desc: Triage identified vulnerable dependencies by severity, exploitability, and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable.
steps.outcome: Prioritized findings list produced.

steps.title: Open remediation tickets for vulnerable dependencies
steps.desc: File tickets with owning engineering teams to upgrade or patch vulnerable components.
steps.outcome: Tickets opened for all prioritized findings.

steps.title: Update dependency risk baseline
steps.desc: Record the SBOM cross-check results in the ongoing supply-chain risk baseline.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-95232.def: A planned exercise in which a security or engineering reviewer manually compares a generated SBOM against the actual dependency manifest of a build (package lockfiles, container layers) to confirm no dependencies were omitted, mislabeled, or misversioned.
ITID-95232.purpose: Captures the test type used to manually audit whether a generated SBOM is complete and accurate against the actual build manifest.
scopeIncludes: Manually reconciling the generated SBOM against the build's actual dependency manifest
Checking for omitted transitive dependencies, incorrect version pinning, or mislabeled components
Assessing SBOM format compliance (e.g., SPDX/CycloneDX schema conformance)
scopeExcludes: Automated vulnerability cross-checking against a generated SBOM (sibling ITID-95231)
General code-quality or dependency-freshness review unrelated to SBOM accuracy
ITID-95232.severity: A significant class of dependencies (e.g., an entire package ecosystem or container layer) omitted from the SBOM is a Critical finding; individual mislabeled/misversioned components are Medium; formatting/schema nonconformance is Low.
ITID-95232.priority: P1 for systemic omission of a dependency class; P2 for individual component inaccuracies; P3 for schema/formatting gaps.
ITID-95232.escalation: Escalate to the engineering lead and application security lead if a systemic class of dependencies is found missing from the SBOM, since this undermines supply-chain visibility broadly.
indicators: Manual reconciliation confirms the SBOM matches the actual build manifest
SBOM omits a class of dependencies (e.g., OS-layer packages in a container image)
SBOM lists incorrect versions relative to the actual resolved dependency
vectors: N/A — this is a secure-development/vulnerability-management practice, not a detection-validation exercise; it doesn't map to ATT&CK adversary behavior.
rootCauses: SBOM tool does not support a specific package ecosystem or container base layer
Build process resolves dependencies dynamically in a way the SBOM tool cannot capture
SBOM generated from source manifest rather than the actual resolved/locked dependency tree
ITID-95232.detection: Not applicable in ATT&CK terms; this test validates the accuracy and completeness of software supply-chain inventory records.
ITID-95232.response: File a finding and remediation ticket for any completeness/accuracy gap; expand SBOM tool coverage or adjust the generation process; re-audit after remediation.
metrics: Percentage of dependencies correctly represented in the SBOM
Number of omitted dependency classes found per audit
Schema conformance rate
sops: SBOM Completeness and Accuracy Audit SOP
ITID-95232.notes: This is a secure-development/vulnerability-management practice, not a detection-validation exercise; it doesn't map to ATT&CK adversary behavior. Best performed on a representative sample of builds spanning different languages/ecosystems, since SBOM tooling gaps are often ecosystem-specific.

steps.title: Confirm audit uses a read-only copy of the build artifact
steps.desc: Verify the audit process only inspects the build artifact and does not modify or redeploy it.
steps.outcome: Confirmed read-only audit process.

steps.title: Independently enumerate actual components in the build
steps.desc: Use an independent tool/method to enumerate the real components present in the build artifact.
steps.outcome: Independent component list produced.

steps.title: Compare independent list against the existing SBOM
steps.desc: Identify any discrepancies — missing, extra, or mismatched-version components.
steps.outcome: Discrepancy list produced.

ITID-96111.def: A planned disaster-recovery exercise simulating a ransomware encryption event, in which the recovery team performs a complete restore of affected systems from backup into a production-equivalent environment, measuring actual recovery time and data loss against documented RTO/RPO targets.
ITID-96111.purpose: Captures a full, end-to-end ransomware recovery exercise that restores production-equivalent systems entirely from backup, to validate the organization's ability to recover without paying a ransom or relying on threat-actor-provided decryption.
scopeIncludes: Full-scope restore of servers, applications, and data from backup following a simulated ransomware scenario
End-to-end RTO/RPO measurement against documented targets
Validation that restored systems are fully functional and free of the simulated malicious payload
scopeExcludes: Restores performed in a deliberately isolated/air-gapped clean-room environment specifically to validate backup integrity before any production restore (see Isolated/Clean-Room Restore Environment Recovery Exercise)
Database-specific point-in-time or failover recovery drills not tied to a ransomware scenario (see Database Recovery Drill leaves)
ITID-96111.severity: Actual recovery time exceeding the documented target RTO is a Critical finding; actual data loss exceeding the documented target RPO is a Critical finding.
ITID-96111.priority: P1 remediation for any RTO/RPO miss on systems supporting critical business functions; P2 for non-critical systems.
ITID-96111.escalation: IT operations leadership and the business continuity owner are notified of the exercise outcome; CISO and executive sponsor are notified of any Critical RTO/RPO miss on critical systems.
indicators: Restored systems pass functional and integrity validation within the documented RTO window
A genuine finding: actual recovery time exceeded the target RTO, or restored data was older than the target RPO
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation; the ransomware encryption event is assumed as the starting scenario, not executed
rootCauses: Backup retention policy misconfigured, resulting in insufficient recovery points
Backup infrastructure itself undersized for the restore throughput required to meet RTO
Restore runbook untested or out of date, causing manual delays
Dependency mapping between systems incomplete, causing restore sequencing errors
ITID-96111.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96111.response: File a remediation ticket for any RTO/RPO miss, prioritizing backup infrastructure or process fixes; retest the specific system class after remediation.
metrics: Actual RTO vs. target RTO
Actual RPO vs. target RPO
Percentage of systems successfully restored to full functionality
ITID-96111.notes: The scenario is planned against T1486/T1490 as the assumed attacker technique that necessitated recovery, not as a technique the exercise itself validates detection of; must not be run against production without a documented rollback plan and a clearly bounded, pre-approved target environment.

playbook.name: Full-Restore-from-Backup Ransomware Recovery Exercise
playbook.description: Planned exercise simulating a ransomware event by fully restoring a system from backup in an isolated environment to validate the recovery process and RTO.

steps.title: Define the simulated ransomware scenario and RTO/RPO targets
steps.desc: Document which system(s) the scenario simulates being encrypted and the target recovery time/point objectives being validated.
steps.outcome: Scenario and targets documented and approved.

steps.title: Obtain system owner and DR lead sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval for the restore exercise, confirming which backup set will be used.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Provision an isolated clean-room restore environment
steps.desc: Set up a network-isolated environment for the restore so it cannot overwrite or interfere with real production data.
steps.outcome: Isolated environment confirmed ready.
steps.abort: Abort if isolation cannot be guaranteed.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders this is a drill, not a real incident
steps.desc: Advise IT operations, application owners, and relevant on-call staff that this is a planned drill so any restore-related alerts aren't escalated as a real event.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Execute the full restore from the selected backup set
steps.desc: Perform the restore into the isolated environment, timing the process from start to completion.
steps.outcome: Restore completed with timing captured.

steps.title: Validate restored data integrity and completeness
steps.desc: Check that restored data matches expectations (checksums, record counts, application functionality) with no corruption.
steps.outcome: Data integrity confirmed or issues documented.

steps.title: Measure achieved RTO/RPO against targets
steps.desc: Compare actual restore time and data recency against the defined RTO/RPO targets.
steps.outcome: RTO/RPO achievement documented.

steps.title: Tear down the isolated test environment
steps.desc: Decommission the clean-room restore environment and securely wipe any restored data copies.
steps.outcome: Test environment torn down.

steps.title: File remediation actions for any RTO/RPO miss or data integrity issue
steps.desc: Open tickets/tasks to fix backup process, infrastructure capacity, or documentation gaps found.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update the ransomware recovery runbook
steps.desc: Revise the DR runbook with corrected steps, timings, or contact information based on the exercise.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated.

ITID-96112.def: A planned disaster-recovery exercise in which backup data is restored into a network-isolated, sandboxed clean-room environment (rather than directly into production or a production-equivalent environment) to verify backup integrity and confirm the absence of dormant ransomware, webshells, or other latent compromise artifacts prior to trusting the backup for a real restore.
ITID-96112.purpose: Captures a ransomware recovery exercise performed specifically in an isolated or air-gapped clean-room environment, to validate that backups themselves are clean and free of latent malware before any production restore is attempted.
scopeIncludes: Restore of backup data into an isolated/air-gapped environment for integrity and malware-freedom validation
Scanning and forensic verification of restored data before it is trusted for production use
scopeExcludes: Full restores performed directly into a production-equivalent environment without an intermediate clean-room validation step (see Full-Restore-from-Backup Ransomware Recovery Exercise)
ITID-96112.severity: Discovery of latent malware, a webshell, or other compromise artifact within a backup set is a Critical finding, since it indicates the backup itself cannot be safely trusted for recovery.
ITID-96112.priority: P1 remediation for any compromised backup set, including immediate isolation of that backup generation and root-cause investigation into how the compromise entered the backup chain.
ITID-96112.escalation: CISO and backup/infrastructure leadership are notified immediately of any compromised backup finding, since it may indicate an active, undetected intrusion predating the backup.
indicators: Restored data in the clean room passes malware/integrity scanning and is certified safe for production restore
A genuine finding: the clean-room scan discovers a compromise artifact within the backup set itself
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation; scenario assumes a prior ransomware event, but the exercise itself performs validation, not attack execution
rootCauses: Backup snapshots were taken after the initial compromise but before detection, capturing the malicious payload
Insufficient backup generation depth, leaving no clean recovery point prior to compromise
Clean-room environment itself lacks adequate isolation, risking cross-contamination
controls: Immutable/offline backup copies with sufficient generational depth
ITID-96112.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability and backup integrity, not detection coverage.
ITID-96112.response: Quarantine any compromised backup generation and identify a clean recovery point; retest with the next backup generation once identified.
metrics: Percentage of backup sets passing clean-room integrity validation
Number of clean, verified recovery-point generations available
ITID-96112.notes: The scenario is planned against T1486/T1490 as the assumed attacker technique motivating the clean-room step, not as a technique the exercise validates detection of; the isolated environment must have no network path back to production.

playbook.name: Isolated/Clean-Room Restore Environment Recovery Exercise
playbook.description: Planned exercise validating that a dedicated clean-room environment can be stood up and used to safely restore systems following a simulated ransomware event.

steps.title: Define the clean-room stand-up scenario and objective
steps.desc: Document the scenario being simulated and what is being validated — specifically the ability to stand up an isolated clean-room environment from scratch under time pressure.
steps.outcome: Scenario and objective documented and approved.

steps.title: Define target stand-up time objective
steps.desc: Set a target time for how quickly the clean-room environment should be operational and ready for restore.
steps.outcome: Target documented.

steps.title: Obtain DR lead and infrastructure sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval for the exercise, including any infrastructure resources needed to stand up the clean room.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Confirm the clean-room network has no path to production
steps.desc: Verify the environment being stood up has no network connectivity to production systems or data.
steps.outcome: Isolation confirmed.
steps.abort: Abort if isolation cannot be guaranteed.

steps.title: Stand up the clean-room environment from scratch
steps.desc: Provision the isolated infrastructure per the DR runbook, timing the full stand-up process.
steps.outcome: Clean-room environment operational, with stand-up time captured.

steps.title: Perform a sample restore into the clean room to validate readiness
steps.desc: Restore a representative system/dataset into the new environment to confirm it functions as intended.
steps.outcome: Sample restore succeeds.

steps.title: Measure stand-up time against target
steps.desc: Compare actual time to stand up the clean room against the defined target.
steps.outcome: Result documented against target.

steps.title: Tear down the clean-room environment
steps.desc: Decommission the temporary environment and securely wipe any test data.
steps.outcome: Environment torn down.

steps.title: File remediation actions for any gaps found
steps.desc: Open tasks for infrastructure automation or documentation gaps that slowed stand-up.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update the clean-room stand-up runbook
steps.desc: Revise the runbook with lessons learned to speed up future stand-ups.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated.

ITID-96113.def: A ransomware recovery exercise whose restore methodology (direct full restore versus isolated clean-room validation) has not been determined or does not map cleanly to a defined sibling leaf.
ITID-96113.purpose: Intake bucket for ransomware recovery simulations that do not cleanly fit the full-restore or clean-room sub-categories, or that have not yet been reclassified.
scopeIncludes: Recovery exercises pending classification into a specific sub-type
scopeExcludes: Exercises clearly performing a direct full restore (use ITID-96111)
Exercises clearly performing isolated clean-room validation (use ITID-96112)
ITID-96113.severity: Apply the severity guidance of the most applicable sibling leaf once findings are categorized.
ITID-96113.priority: Triage for reclassification within one review cycle; do not leave findings permanently under this catch-all code.
ITID-96113.escalation: Business continuity owner reviews all records filed under this code at least quarterly to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf.
indicators: Record awaiting classification triage
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation
rootCauses: Exercise scoping did not designate a single restore methodology
New recovery-testing format not yet mapped to an existing taxonomy leaf
controls: Taxonomy governance / periodic ITID review process
ITID-96113.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96113.response: Reclassify into a specific sibling leaf as soon as the exercise's restore methodology is clear.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
sops: ITID Taxonomy Governance and Review SOP
ITID-96113.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; business continuity leadership should periodically reclassify entries into ITID-96111 or ITID-96112 rather than allowing this bucket to accumulate.

ITID-96121.def: A planned recovery drill in which a database is restored to a precise prior point in time (e.g., immediately before a simulated data-corruption or accidental-deletion event) using transaction-log replay against a base backup, validating both the mechanical restore process and the accuracy of the recovered data at the target timestamp.
ITID-96121.purpose: Captures a drill that validates the organization's ability to restore a database to a specific historical point in time using transaction logs and backups, distinct from full-instance failover.
scopeIncludes: Point-in-time restore using base backup plus transaction/write-ahead log replay
Validation of data accuracy and consistency at the recovered timestamp
scopeExcludes: Promotion of a live standby replica to primary with no log-replay restore involved (see Database Failover/Replica Promotion Drill)
Full application-stack ransomware recovery exercises (see Ransomware Recovery Simulation leaves)
ITID-96121.severity: Failure to restore to the exact target timestamp, or data inconsistency/corruption in the restored database, is a Critical finding.
ITID-96121.priority: P1 remediation for point-in-time restore failures on databases supporting critical business functions; P2 for non-critical databases.
ITID-96121.escalation: Database engineering leadership and the application owner are notified of the drill outcome; escalate to IT leadership on any Critical finding.
indicators: Database successfully restores to the exact target timestamp with full data consistency
A genuine finding: actual recovery time exceeded the target RTO, or the restored data reflects an incorrect timestamp or is internally inconsistent
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation
rootCauses: Transaction log retention window shorter than the required recovery window
Base backup and log chain broken due to a missed or corrupted backup job
Restore runbook lacks precise timestamp-targeting procedure, causing manual error
controls: Database backup and transaction-log retention policy
ITID-96121.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96121.response: File a remediation ticket for any restore failure or data-accuracy gap; retest after backup/log-retention or runbook fixes.
metrics: Actual RTO vs. target RTO for point-in-time restore
Data accuracy/consistency pass rate at target timestamp
ITID-96121.notes: Must be run against a non-production database instance or a clearly isolated copy to avoid impacting live application availability.

playbook.name: Point-in-Time Database Recovery Drill
playbook.description: Planned exercise restoring a database to a specific prior point in time in an isolated environment to validate the point-in-time recovery capability.

steps.title: Define the recovery point scenario and RTO/RPO targets
steps.desc: Document the simulated data-loss scenario (e.g. accidental mass delete) and the specific point-in-time recovery target, plus RTO/RPO objectives.
steps.outcome: Scenario and targets documented and approved.

steps.title: Select the database instance and backup/transaction-log set
steps.desc: Identify which database and which backup/log chain will be used for the point-in-time restore.
steps.outcome: Database and backup set documented.

steps.title: Obtain DBA and system owner sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval for the drill, confirming it will run in an isolated environment only.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Provision an isolated restore target
steps.desc: Stand up a separate database instance for the restore so production data cannot be overwritten.
steps.outcome: Isolated target confirmed ready.
steps.abort: Abort if the restore cannot be isolated from production.

steps.title: Notify application owners this is a drill
steps.desc: Advise dependent application teams the drill is planned so any related alerts aren't escalated as a real incident.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Execute the point-in-time restore
steps.desc: Restore the database to the target point in time on the isolated instance, timing the process.
steps.outcome: Restore completed with timing captured.

steps.title: Validate data state matches the intended recovery point
steps.desc: Confirm the restored data reflects exactly the intended point in time, with no data corruption or gaps.
steps.outcome: Data state validated.

steps.title: Measure RTO/RPO achievement
steps.desc: Compare actual restore time and data recency against defined targets.
steps.outcome: Results documented against targets.

steps.title: Tear down the isolated restore instance
steps.desc: Decommission the test database instance and securely remove restored test data.
steps.outcome: Test instance torn down.

steps.title: File remediation actions for any gaps found
steps.desc: Open tasks for backup process, tooling, or documentation gaps identified.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update the database recovery runbook
steps.desc: Revise the runbook with corrected steps or timings based on the drill.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated.

ITID-96122.def: A planned recovery drill in which a standby/replica database (already synchronized via ongoing replication) is promoted to the primary role following a simulated primary-database outage, validating failover automation or manual procedure, replication-lag data loss, and application reconnection behavior.
ITID-96122.purpose: Captures a drill that validates the organization's ability to promote a live standby database replica to primary role during an outage, distinct from a log-replay point-in-time restore.
scopeIncludes: Promotion of a synchronized standby replica to primary role
Validation of application/connection-string failover and replication-lag data loss at the moment of promotion
scopeExcludes: Restore of a database to a specific historical point in time via backup and log replay (see Point-in-Time Database Recovery Drill)
ITID-96122.severity: Failover taking longer than the documented target RTO, or replication lag at promotion exceeding the target RPO, is a Critical finding.
ITID-96122.priority: P1 remediation for failover failures on databases supporting critical business functions; P2 for non-critical databases.
ITID-96122.escalation: Database engineering leadership and the application owner are notified of the drill outcome; escalate to IT leadership on any Critical finding.
indicators: Standby replica promotes to primary and applications reconnect successfully within the target RTO
A genuine finding: applications fail to reconnect automatically, requiring manual intervention, or replication lag at promotion exceeded the target RPO
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation
rootCauses: Replication lag exceeded acceptable thresholds due to network or load conditions
Application connection strings/DNS not configured for automatic failover
Failover automation script untested or out of date
ITID-96122.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96122.response: File a remediation ticket for any failover gap; retest after replication, automation, or application connection-handling fixes.
metrics: Actual failover RTO vs. target
Replication lag/data loss at promotion vs. target RPO
Percentage of applications reconnecting automatically without manual intervention
ITID-96122.notes: Should be scheduled during a low-traffic maintenance window if run against any production-adjacent replica pair, with a documented rollback/fail-back plan.

playbook.name: Database Failover/Replica Promotion Drill
playbook.description: Planned exercise promoting a standby database replica to primary to validate the failover process and measure downtime.

steps.title: Define the failover scenario and downtime target
steps.desc: Document the simulated primary-failure scenario and the target failover time (RTO) being validated.
steps.outcome: Scenario and target documented and approved.

steps.title: Select the primary/replica pair and confirm replication health
steps.desc: Identify the database pair for the drill and confirm the replica is currently in sync before starting.
steps.outcome: Pair identified and replication confirmed healthy.
steps.abort: Abort if the replica is not currently in sync.

steps.title: Obtain DBA and application owner sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval for the drill and its scheduled maintenance window.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Schedule the drill in a low-traffic maintenance window
steps.desc: Confirm the promotion will occur during a window that minimizes real user impact if failover doesn't go smoothly.
steps.outcome: Maintenance window confirmed.

steps.title: Notify dependent application teams and on-call of the drill
steps.desc: Advise application owners and on-call staff so any connection-drop alerts during the drill aren't escalated as a real outage.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Promote the replica to primary
steps.desc: Execute the failover/promotion procedure, timing the full process including application reconnection.
steps.outcome: Replica promoted successfully with timing captured.
steps.abort: Abort and fail back if promotion produces data inconsistency.

steps.title: Validate application connectivity and data consistency post-failover
steps.desc: Confirm dependent applications reconnect successfully and data is consistent on the new primary.
steps.outcome: Connectivity and consistency confirmed.

steps.title: Measure actual downtime against the RTO target
steps.desc: Compare the measured failover/reconnection time against the target.
steps.outcome: Results documented against target.

steps.title: Re-establish replication and restore original topology if needed
steps.desc: Rebuild the standby replica relationship so the environment returns to its normal resilient state.
steps.outcome: Replication topology restored.

steps.title: File remediation actions for any gaps found
steps.desc: Open tasks for automation or documentation gaps that slowed the failover.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update the failover runbook
steps.desc: Revise the runbook based on lessons learned from the drill.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated.

ITID-96123.def: A database recovery drill whose recovery mechanism (point-in-time restore versus replica promotion/failover) has not been determined or does not map cleanly to a defined sibling leaf.
ITID-96123.purpose: Intake bucket for database recovery drills that do not cleanly fit the point-in-time or failover sub-categories, or that have not yet been reclassified.
scopeIncludes: Recovery drills pending classification into a specific sub-type
scopeExcludes: Drills clearly using point-in-time backup/log restore (use ITID-96121)
Drills clearly using replica promotion/failover (use ITID-96122)
ITID-96123.severity: Apply the severity guidance of the most applicable sibling leaf once findings are categorized.
ITID-96123.priority: Triage for reclassification within one review cycle; do not leave findings permanently under this catch-all code.
ITID-96123.escalation: Database engineering leadership reviews all records filed under this code at least quarterly to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf.
indicators: Record awaiting classification triage
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation
rootCauses: Drill scoping did not designate a single recovery mechanism
New database recovery format not yet mapped to an existing taxonomy leaf
controls: Taxonomy governance / periodic ITID review process
ITID-96123.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96123.response: Reclassify into a specific sibling leaf as soon as the drill's recovery mechanism is clear.
metrics: Count of records pending reclassification
Average time to reclassification
sops: ITID Taxonomy Governance and Review SOP
ITID-96123.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; database engineering leadership should periodically reclassify entries into ITID-96121 or ITID-96122 rather than allowing this bucket to accumulate.

steps.outcome: Scenario and targets documented and approved.

steps.title: Obtain DBA sign-off

steps.title: Confirm the drill runs in an isolated environment
steps.desc: Verify no risk to production data from the drill.

steps.title: Execute the recovery procedure

steps.title: Validate recovered data integrity

steps.outcome: Integrity confirmed.
