ITID-96131.def: A planned disaster-recovery exercise in which a cloud-hosted workload (compute, storage, networking, and dependent services) is failed over from its primary cloud region to a pre-provisioned secondary region, validating infrastructure-as-code re-provisioning or standby-region activation, data replication currency, and DNS/traffic-routing cutover.
ITID-96131.purpose: Captures a drill validating the organization's ability to fail over an entire cloud workload from a primary region to a secondary region during a regional outage.
scopeIncludes: Full regional failover of cloud infrastructure and dependent services
DNS/traffic-routing cutover validation
Cross-region data replication currency validation at the moment of failover
scopeExcludes: Restore-time measurement of a specific cloud-native backup artifact without a full regional failover (see Cloud Backup Restore Time Objective (RTO) Validation Test)
ITID-96131.severity: Failover taking longer than the documented target RTO, or cross-region data replication lag exceeding the target RPO, is a Critical finding.
ITID-96131.priority: P1 remediation for failover failures affecting critical business workloads; P2 for non-critical workloads.
ITID-96131.escalation: Cloud infrastructure leadership and the business continuity owner are notified of the drill outcome; escalate to CISO/executive sponsor on any Critical finding affecting a critical workload.
indicators: Workload successfully activates in the secondary region and serves traffic within the target RTO
A genuine finding: DNS/traffic cutover fails to redirect users automatically, or dependent services in the secondary region are not provisioned correctly
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation
rootCauses: Infrastructure-as-code templates for the secondary region are stale or untested
Cross-region data replication configured with excessive lag or not enabled for all required data stores
DNS/traffic-manager failover policy misconfigured or not automated
Undocumented dependency on a primary-region-only service
ITID-96131.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96131.response: File a remediation ticket for any regional failover gap; retest after infrastructure-as-code, replication, or DNS/traffic-routing fixes.
metrics: Actual regional failover RTO vs. target
Cross-region replication lag at failover vs. target RPO
Percentage of dependent services successfully activated in the secondary region
ITID-96131.notes: Should be scoped to a non-production environment or a clearly bounded production workload with executive sign-off, given the potential customer-facing impact of a live regional cutover.

playbook.name: Cross-Region Cloud Failover Test
playbook.description: Planned exercise failing over a cloud workload from its primary region to a secondary region to validate multi-region disaster recovery capability.

steps.title: Define the regional outage scenario and RTO target
steps.desc: Document the simulated primary-region outage scenario and the target time to fail over to the secondary region.
steps.outcome: Scenario and target documented and approved.

steps.title: Select the workload and confirm secondary region readiness
steps.desc: Identify the workload in scope and confirm the secondary region has current data replication and adequate capacity.
steps.outcome: Workload and secondary region readiness confirmed.

steps.title: Obtain cloud platform owner and leadership sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval for the failover test given its potential customer-facing impact.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Schedule the test in a low-traffic window
steps.desc: Confirm the failover will occur during a window that minimizes real customer impact.
steps.outcome: Window confirmed.

steps.title: Notify SOC, support, and status-page owners of the test window
steps.desc: Advise operational teams so any failover-related alerts or brief latency reports are correctly attributed to the drill.
steps.outcome: Teams acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Define a fail-back trigger condition
steps.desc: Set a clear threshold (e.g. sustained error rate) that triggers immediate fail-back to the primary region.
steps.outcome: Fail-back trigger documented.
steps.abort: Fail back immediately if the trigger threshold is breached.

steps.title: Execute the failover to the secondary region
steps.desc: Perform the planned failover procedure, timing the full process including DNS/traffic cutover.
steps.outcome: Failover completed with timing captured.
steps.abort: Abort and fail back per the defined trigger condition.

steps.title: Validate application functionality and data consistency in the secondary region
steps.desc: Confirm the workload functions correctly and data is consistent after failover.
steps.outcome: Functionality and consistency confirmed.

steps.title: Measure actual failover time against the RTO target
steps.desc: Compare the measured failover time against the target.
steps.outcome: Results documented against target.

steps.title: Fail back to the primary region and confirm normal operation
steps.desc: Return the workload to the primary region and confirm it is operating normally.
steps.outcome: Primary region confirmed restored to normal operation.

steps.title: File remediation actions for any gaps found
steps.desc: Open tasks for automation, capacity, or documentation gaps identified during the failover.
steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.title: Update the cloud DR runbook
steps.desc: Revise the multi-region failover runbook based on lessons learned.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated.

ITID-96132.def: A planned test in which a cloud-native backup (snapshot, managed-service backup, or object-storage backup copy) is restored into a fresh cloud resource, measuring elapsed restore time and data currency against documented RTO/RPO targets for that specific backup mechanism.
ITID-96132.purpose: Captures a focused test measuring the actual time required to restore a cloud-native backup artifact (e.g., a managed database snapshot or object-storage backup) against the organization's documented restore time objective, without a full regional failover.
scopeIncludes: Restore-time measurement for a specific cloud-native backup mechanism (e.g., managed database snapshot restore, object-storage versioned restore)
Data currency/RPO validation for the restored artifact
scopeExcludes: Full multi-service regional failover exercises (see Cross-Region Cloud Failover Test)
ITID-96132.severity: Actual restore time exceeding the documented target RTO for that backup mechanism is a Critical finding.
ITID-96132.priority: P1 remediation for RTO misses on backup mechanisms protecting critical business data; P2 for non-critical data stores.
ITID-96132.escalation: Cloud infrastructure leadership and the business continuity owner are notified of the test outcome; escalate to IT leadership on any Critical RTO miss for a critical data store.
indicators: Cloud-native backup restores successfully within the documented target RTO
A genuine finding: actual restore time exceeded the target RTO, or the restored artifact's data currency exceeded the target RPO
vectors: N/A — this is a recovery/continuity exercise, not an attack simulation
rootCauses: Backup snapshot frequency insufficient to meet the target RPO
Cloud provider restore throughput/service limits not accounted for in RTO planning
Backup retention policy misconfigured, resulting in the needed recovery point being unavailable
controls: Cloud-native backup service configuration and retention policy
ITID-96132.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability, not detection coverage.
ITID-96132.response: File a remediation ticket for any RTO/RPO miss, adjusting backup frequency, retention, or restore procedure as needed; retest after remediation.
metrics: Actual RTO vs. target RTO by backup mechanism
Actual RPO vs. target RPO by backup mechanism
ITID-96132.notes: Should be run against a dedicated test/sandbox cloud resource, not directly overwriting production, to keep the exercise non-disruptive.

steps.title: Define the restore scenario and RTO target
steps.desc: Document the simulated data-loss scenario and the target restore time objective being validated.
steps.outcome: Scenario and target documented and approved.

steps.title: Select the workload and backup snapshot to restore
steps.desc: Identify the specific cloud workload and backup/snapshot to use for the test restore.
steps.outcome: Workload and backup snapshot documented.

steps.title: Obtain cloud platform owner sign-off
steps.desc: Get written approval for the restore test.
steps.outcome: Signed authorization on file.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sign-off.

steps.title: Provision an isolated cloud environment for the restore
steps.desc: Stand up a separate account/subscription or VPC for the restore so production is unaffected.
steps.outcome: Isolated environment confirmed ready.
steps.abort: Abort if isolation cannot be guaranteed.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders this is a drill
steps.desc: Advise relevant teams the restore test is planned, not a real recovery event.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders acknowledge notification.

steps.title: Execute the restore from backup
steps.desc: Restore the workload into the isolated environment, timing the full process.
steps.outcome: Restore completed with timing captured.

steps.title: Validate restored workload functionality and data integrity
steps.desc: Confirm the restored workload functions correctly and data is intact.
steps.outcome: Functionality and integrity confirmed.

steps.title: Measure achieved RTO against the target
steps.desc: Compare the actual restore time against the defined RTO target.
steps.outcome: Results documented against target.

steps.outcome: Test environment torn down.

steps.outcome: Remediation actions tracked.

steps.outcome: Baseline updated.

ITID-96211.def: A facilitated, scenario-driven tabletop exercise in which C-suite executives (CEO, CFO, COO, CISO, General Counsel, etc.) work through the key operational decisions of a simulated major breach scenario — containment authorization, ransom pay/no-pay, resource allocation, customer/partner communication timing — without executing any actual technical response actions.
ITID-96211.purpose: Captures a tabletop exercise walking the C-suite through the operational decisions required during a major cyber breach, testing executive decision-making rather than technical response.
scopeIncludes: Executive-level decision-making walkthrough for a major breach scenario
Testing of decision authority, escalation thresholds, and resource-allocation processes at the executive level
scopeExcludes: Board-level and external/investor communication rehearsal specifically (see Board-Level Cyber Crisis Communication Simulation)
Legal, IT, and communications team operational coordination at the working level (see Cross-Departmental Incident Response Drill leaves)
ITID-96211.severity: A decision-making delay or ambiguity in decision authority during the exercise that would materially worsen a real incident's outcome (e.g., no clear owner for ransom pay/no-pay decision) is a Critical finding.
ITID-96211.priority: P1 remediation for undefined or contested decision authority on time-critical decisions; P2 for process clarity gaps that did not block a decision but caused confusion.
ITID-96211.escalation: CEO and board liaison are notified of the exercise after-action report; CISO and General Counsel are notified of any decision-authority gap requiring policy update.
indicators: Executives correctly identify decision owners and reach a documented decision within the scenario's simulated time pressure
A genuine finding: no clear consensus on decision ownership, or a required decision (e.g., ransom pay/no-pay) has no documented authority or criteria
vectors: N/A — this is a business-continuity/disaster-recovery exercise, not an adversary-technique-detection exercise; it validates operational resilience, not detection coverage
rootCauses: Crisis management plan does not clearly assign decision authority for key breach decisions
Executives have not previously participated in a breach-scenario exercise and lack familiarity with the process
Legal and business risk tolerance for key decisions (e.g., ransom payment) has never been formally documented
controls: Crisis management plan / executive decision-authority matrix
Business continuity and crisis communication policy
ITID-96211.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability and organizational resilience, not detection coverage.
ITID-96211.response: Update the crisis management plan and decision-authority matrix for any gap identified; schedule a follow-up tabletop to confirm the update resolves the gap.
metrics: Time to reach key decisions during the exercise
Percentage of decision points with clearly documented authority
Number of crisis-plan updates resulting from the exercise
sops: Executive Cyber Crisis Tabletop Facilitation SOP
ITID-96211.notes: Should be facilitated by an experienced tabletop facilitator (internal or external) with a realistic, sector-relevant scenario; findings are organizational/process gaps, not technical vulnerabilities.

playbook.name: C-Suite Decision-Making Tabletop for Major Breach Scenario
playbook.description: Planned, discussion-based tabletop exercise walking C-suite executives through a major breach scenario to validate crisis decision-making and IR plan alignment.

steps.title: Design the breach scenario and injects
steps.desc: Draft a realistic major-breach scenario with a sequence of injects (new facts introduced during the session) that test key decision points.
steps.outcome: Scenario and inject sequence documented.

steps.title: Identify and confirm executive participant list
steps.desc: Confirm which C-suite members and key advisors (Legal, Comms, CISO) will participate.
steps.outcome: Participant list confirmed.

steps.title: Obtain executive sponsor sign-off and schedule
steps.desc: Get approval and calendar commitment from an executive sponsor before finalizing the session.
steps.outcome: Session scheduled and approved.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sponsor sign-off.

steps.title: Set facilitator ground rules
steps.desc: Establish and communicate ground rules: no real notifications, no real regulator/media/customer contact, all actions are simulated for the session.
steps.outcome: Ground rules documented and communicated to all participants.

steps.title: Designate a facilitator to intercept any real-world action
steps.desc: Assign a facilitator responsible for immediately stopping any participant from taking a real external action (e.g. actually calling a regulator).
steps.outcome: Facilitator role confirmed and briefed.
steps.abort: Facilitator intervenes immediately if a participant attempts a real external action.

steps.title: Run the tabletop session
steps.desc: Walk participants through the scenario and injects, prompting decisions at each stage.
steps.outcome: Session completed through all planned injects.

steps.title: Capture decisions and discussion points in real time
steps.desc: Record key decisions made, disagreements, and any process gaps surfaced during the session.
steps.outcome: Session notes captured.

steps.title: Debrief participants immediately after the session
steps.desc: Facilitate a hot-wash discussion capturing immediate participant reactions and observations.
steps.outcome: Debrief completed.

steps.title: Identify decision-making or communication gaps
steps.desc: Analyze session notes to identify where the IR plan or crisis communication plan was unclear or insufficient.
steps.outcome: Gap list produced.

steps.title: Publish an after-action report to executive sponsors
steps.desc: Summarize findings, decisions, and recommended plan updates for executive stakeholders.
steps.outcome: Report published.

steps.title: Update the incident response and crisis communication plans
steps.desc: Revise the relevant plans to close gaps identified during the tabletop.
steps.outcome: Plans updated.

ITID-96212.def: A facilitated simulation in which participants rehearse board notification, investor/analyst communication, media statements, and regulator/customer messaging for a simulated major breach, testing the accuracy, consistency, timing, and approval workflow of external-facing crisis communications.
ITID-96212.purpose: Captures a simulation focused specifically on board-level and external crisis communication during a major cyber breach, testing messaging, timing, and stakeholder coordination rather than internal operational decisions.
scopeIncludes: Board notification content and timing rehearsal
Investor relations, media, and public statement drafting and approval-workflow rehearsal
Cross-stakeholder message consistency validation
scopeExcludes: C-suite operational decision-making walkthrough not focused on external communications (see C-Suite Decision-Making Tabletop for Major Breach Scenario)
Working-level legal/IT/communications coordination drills (see Cross-Departmental Incident Response Drill leaves)
ITID-96212.severity: Inconsistent or inaccurate messaging across stakeholder channels (e.g., board briefing conflicts with the draft public statement) during the exercise is a Critical finding.
ITID-96212.priority: P1 remediation for message-consistency or approval-workflow gaps that would delay legally required disclosures; P2 for stylistic or clarity issues.
ITID-96212.escalation: CEO, board chair, and General Counsel are notified of the exercise after-action report and any communication-process gap.
indicators: Draft communications for board, media, and regulators remain consistent and are approved within the simulated timeline
A genuine finding: draft messages conflict across channels, or the approval workflow cannot produce an approved statement within the required disclosure window
vectors: N/A — this is a business-continuity/disaster-recovery exercise, not an adversary-technique-detection exercise; it validates operational resilience, not detection coverage
rootCauses: No pre-drafted communication templates exist for common breach scenarios
Approval workflow for external statements involves too many sequential sign-offs to meet disclosure deadlines
Board communication channel/process not pre-established for out-of-cycle crisis briefings
controls: Crisis communication plan and pre-drafted message templates
ITID-96212.detection: N/A — this validates recovery capability and organizational resilience, not detection coverage.
ITID-96212.response: Update crisis communication templates and approval workflows for any gap identified; retest with a follow-up simulation to confirm the fix.
metrics: Time to produce an approved external statement during the exercise

ITID-96221.def: A facilitated tabletop exercise in which participants walk through the specific steps, decision points, and internal handoffs required to determine breach-notification obligations and deliver a compliant notification within a single jurisdiction's mandated timeline (e.g., a 72-hour regulatory window), timing each step against the deadline.

vectors: N/A — this is a business-continuity/disaster-recovery exercise, not an adversary-technique-detection exercise; it validates operational resilience, not detection coverage

No pre-established criteria for determining whether an incident triggers a notification obligation

playbook.name: General Cross-Departmental Incident Response Drill
playbook.description: General-purpose planned, discussion-based tabletop exercising cross-departmental coordination when no more specific joint drill scenario applies.

steps.title: Design the scenario requiring cross-departmental coordination
steps.desc: Draft a scenario and identify which departments must jointly respond.
steps.outcome: Scenario documented with departments identified.

steps.title: Confirm participant list across departments
steps.desc: Identify representatives from each involved department who will participate.
steps.outcome: Participant list confirmed.

steps.title: Obtain sponsor sign-off and schedule
steps.desc: Get approval and scheduling commitment from sponsors across the involved departments.
steps.outcome: Session scheduled and approved.
steps.abort: Do not proceed without sponsor sign-off.

steps.title: Set facilitator ground rules
steps.desc: Establish that no real system changes or external communications will occur during the session.
steps.outcome: Ground rules documented and communicated.

steps.title: Designate a facilitator to intercept any real-world action
steps.desc: Assign a facilitator to stop any participant from taking a real action during the session.
steps.outcome: Facilitator role confirmed.
steps.abort: Facilitator intervenes immediately if a real action is attempted.

steps.title: Run the tabletop session
steps.desc: Walk participants through the scenario, prompting joint decisions across departments at each stage.
steps.outcome: Session completed through all planned injects.

steps.title: Capture handoff points and coordination friction
steps.desc: Record where cross-departmental handoffs were smooth or where friction/delay occurred.
steps.outcome: Session notes captured.

steps.title: Debrief participants immediately after the session
steps.desc: Facilitate a hot-wash discussion capturing immediate observations.
steps.outcome: Debrief completed.

steps.title: Identify cross-departmental coordination gaps
steps.desc: Analyze session notes to identify where the joint response plan was unclear.
steps.outcome: Gap list produced.

steps.title: Publish an after-action report and update the joint response plan
steps.desc: Summarize findings for stakeholders and update the relevant cross-departmental response plan.
steps.outcome: Report published and plan updated.
